knowledge_statements.title: Dualized Clique-Tree Conversions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lagrangian dualization of separator equalities in a clique-tree SDP conversion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For clique variables \(X_k\succeq0\), suppose the converted objective contains \(\sum_k\langle Q_k,X_k\rangle\) and separator equations \(R_{ke}X_kR_{ke}^{\mathsf T}=R_{\ell e}X_\ell R_{\ell e}^{\mathsf T}\). Assign a symmetric multiplier \(Y_e\) to each oriented tree edge. Dualization replaces the coupled objective by \[\sum_k\left\langle Q_k+\sum_{e\ni k}\sigma_{ke}R_{ke}^{\mathsf T}Y_eR_{ke},X_k\right\rangle,\] where \(\sigma_{ke}=1\) at one endpoint and \(-1\) at the other. Under primal or dual Slater feasibility, optimizing this dualized formulation has the same value as the separator-consistent conversion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dualizing separator equalities replaces explicit clique coupling by separator multipliers that enter adjacent clique objectives with opposite signs; Slater feasibility gives equal optimal values.
assumptions_latex: Clique variables and separator maps form a finite-dimensional conic program.
A primal or dual Slater point exists.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p^\star=d^\star\), with each \(Y_e\) contributing oppositely to the two clique coefficients incident to \(e\).

notation.meaning: Symmetric multiplier for the separator equality on edge \(e\).

knowledge_statements.title: Nonsymmetric Sparse-SDP Formulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal and dual chordal cones represented with structurally different lifted variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a chordal pattern \(G\), let \(\mathcal K_G\) be the cone of PSD-completable partial matrices and let \(\mathcal K_G^*\) be the cone of PSD matrices supported on \(G\). They admit the paired representations \[\mathcal K_G=\{X:E_kXE_k^{\mathsf T}\succeq0\ \forall k\},\qquad \mathcal K_G^*=\left\{\sum_kE_k^{\mathsf T}Z_kE_k:Z_k\succeq0\right\}.\] A lifted sparse-SDP formulation using clique restrictions for the first cone and clique sums for the second is nonsymmetric in its lifted coordinates: primal copies are coupled by overlap agreement, whereas dual clique matrices are coupled through their embedded sum, despite the two cones being dual under the trace pairing.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Chordal primal and dual cones have different lifted forms: consistent clique restrictions describe PSD completions, while embedded sums of clique PSD matrices describe sparse PSD matrices.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is chordal.
The partial-matrix and sparse-matrix spaces use the trace pairing on specified entries.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal K_G^*=\{\sum_kE_k^{\mathsf T}Z_kE_k:Z_k\succeq0\}\), while \(\mathcal K_G\) is described by clique restrictions and consistency.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The paired completion-cone and sparse-cone representations are plausible, but the specialized meaning of “nonsymmetric” and the lifted-coordinate interpretation lack a cited source. knowledge_statements.title: Reformulation Size
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar dimension of a clique-based semidefinite lifting.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a chordal conversion use clique PSD variables \(X_k\in\mathbb S_+^{r_k}\), where \(r_k=|C_k|\). Before counting auxiliary linear variables, the lifted semidefinite variables contain \[N_{\mathrm{psd}}=\sum_{k=1}^{q}\frac{r_k(r_k+1)}{2}\] independent scalar coordinates. If dense cone blocks are stored explicitly, their storage is \(\Theta(\sum_kr_k^2)\), and generic dense factorizations internal to those blocks require at most \(O(\sum_kr_k^3)\) arithmetic per blockwise factorization. These quantities measure the reformulation rather than the dimension of the original sparse partial matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Clique conversion uses the sum of clique symmetric dimensions; explicit block storage is quadratic and dense block factorization cubic in clique sizes.
assumptions_latex: Each maximal clique produces one dense symmetric PSD block.
Scalar coordinates use the upper-triangular representation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N_{\mathrm{psd}}=\sum_k r_k(r_k+1)/2\), with storage \(\Theta(\sum_kr_k^2)\) and block-factorization work \(O(\sum_kr_k^3)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Coupling-Constraint Burden
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Number of separator equalities in a clique-tree conversion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T\) be a clique tree and let \(s_e=|C_k\cap C_\ell|\) for each edge \(e=(k,\ell)\). Enforcing equality of symmetric separator submatrices introduces exactly \[N_{\mathrm{sep}}=\sum_{e\in E(T)}\frac{s_e(s_e+1)}{2}\] scalar linear equalities when one independent equation is used for each upper-triangular separator entry. Explicit storage of their dense coefficient blocks is \(O(\sum_es_e^2)\), although actual KKT-system work also depends on incidence, numerical ordering, and additional SDP constraints. The count applies to a tree conversion without redundant nonedge overlap equations.

children.title: Size–Coupling Tradeoff
children.top_down_role: Conversion choices balancing local block size against global consistency overhead.

knowledge_statements.title: Size–Coupling Tradeoff
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural cost proxy for choosing a chordal extension and clique tree.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a chordal extension with clique sizes \(r_k\) and clique-tree separator sizes \(s_e\), a basic conversion-cost proxy is \[\Phi_{\alpha,\beta}=\alpha\sum_k\frac{r_k(r_k+1)}{2}+\beta\sum_e\frac{s_e(s_e+1)}{2},\qquad \alpha,\beta>0.\] The first term measures lifted cone size and the second measures linear coupling. Adding fill can merge or enlarge cliques and can simultaneously change the number and sizes of separators; hence neither term alone orders all chordal extensions. A size-optimal conversion therefore need not be coupling-optimal, and the preferred extension depends on the solver-dependent weights and resulting KKT sparsity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Chordal extensions trade lifted PSD-block size against separator coupling; minimizing either count alone need not minimize total solver cost.
assumptions_latex: Candidate extensions are chordal and admit clique trees.
Positive weights represent solver-dependent costs of cone coordinates and coupling equations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\arg\min\sum_kr_k(r_k+1)/2\) need not equal \(\arg\min\sum_es_e(s_e+1)/2\) or \(\arg\min\Phi_{\alpha,\beta}\).

notation.meaning: Weighted structural proxy for conversion cost.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The principle correctly identifies competing clique-size and separator-coupling measures, but the proposed weighted proxy and the claimed noncoincidence of optima require comparative or methodological support. No source is supplied.

children.title: Multifrontal Factorization

knowledge_statements.title: Multifrontal Factorization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Elimination-tree factorization by assembled dense frontal matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a symmetric positive-definite sparse matrix \(A\) and an elimination ordering. Construct its elimination tree. At each node \(j\), assemble a frontal matrix \(F_j\) from entries of \(A\) associated with the node's pivot variables and update variables, plus Schur-complement contributions received from its children. Factor the pivot block \(F_{PP}=L_{PP}D_PL_{PP}^{\mathsf T}\), compute \(L_{UP}=F_{UP}L_{PP}^{-\mathsf T}D_P^{-1}\), and pass \[U_j=F_{UU}-L_{UP}D_PL_{UP}^{\mathsf T}\] to the parent. Processing nodes bottom-up yields factors \(A=LDL^{\mathsf T}\); failure of a positive pivot detects violation of positive definiteness in exact arithmetic.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multifrontal factorization assembles dense fronts along an elimination tree, factors each pivot block, and passes its Schur-complement update to the parent.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) is symmetric positive definite.
The elimination ordering and symbolic fill pattern are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A=LDL^{\mathsf T}\), assembled from the frontal pivot factors and update blocks.

notation.meaning: Pivot and update index sets of a front.

knowledge_statements.title: Supernodal Factorization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Blocked sparse factorization using columns with common filled structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Input a symmetric positive-definite sparse matrix \(A\), an elimination ordering, and a partition of consecutive columns into supernodes whose filled subdiagonal structures agree. For each supernode \(J
earrow\), assemble its dense diagonal block and rectangular update block from prior contributions; compute a dense factorization \(A_{JJ}^{(J)}=L_{JJ}D_JL_{JJ}^{\mathsf T}\); solve for the block column \(L_{IJ}=A_{IJ}^{(J)}L_{JJ}^{-\mathsf T}D_J^{-1}\); and apply the update \[A_{II}^{\mathrm{new}}=A_{II}^{(J)}-L_{IJ}D_JL_{IJ}^{\mathsf T}.\] After all supernodes are processed, the stored block columns form \(A=LDL^{\mathsf T}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Supernodal factorization groups columns with common filled structure and applies dense block factorizations, triangular solves, and Schur-complement updates.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) is symmetric positive definite.
Columns in each supernode have compatible filled subdiagonal patterns.

children.title: Frontal–Supernodal Regimes

knowledge_statements.title: Frontal–Supernodal Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operation counts and structural regimes for two blocked sparse-factorization organizations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a pivot block of size \(p\) with \(u\) update indices, either frontal or supernodal dense processing has arithmetic scale \[\Theta(p^3+p^2u+pu^2)\] and factor-storage scale \(\Theta(p^2+pu)\), excluding transient assembled updates. Multifrontal organization is naturally effective when the elimination tree has many separately assembled child contributions and supports tree parallelism. Supernodal organization is naturally effective when long groups of columns share filled structure, permitting large contiguous block operations. These structural conditions do not imply universal dominance: amalgamation changes \(p\), transient storage, parallelism, and the amount of work performed on structural zeros.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Both organizations have comparable local dense costs; multifrontal methods favor tree-structured assembly, while supernodal methods favor long compatible column blocks. Neither universally dominates.
assumptions_latex: The factorization uses fixed symbolic fill and dense kernels within each block.
\(p\) and \(u\) denote local pivot and update sizes.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(W=\Theta(p^3+p^2u+pu^2)\) and \(M=\Theta(p^2+pu)\) locally, while the preferable organization depends on elimination-tree and supernode structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Projected Inverse Computation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Selected inversion on the filled Cholesky pattern without forming a dense inverse.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input \(A=LDL^{\mathsf T}\succ0\), where \(L\) is unit lower triangular, and let \(\mathcal F\) be the symmetric filled pattern of \(L+L^{\mathsf T}\). Initialize no dense inverse. For \(i=n,n-1,\ldots,1\), compute the requested entries \(Z_{ij}\) with \((i,j)\in\mathcal F\) and \(j\ge i\) by \[Z_{ij}=\frac{\delta_{ij}}{D_{ii}}-\sum_{k>i}L_{ki}Z_{kj},\] where only nonzero \(L_{ki}\) and closure-required selected entries are used; then set \(Z_{ji}=Z_{ij}\). The output satisfies \(Z=\mathcal P_{\mathcal F}(A^{-1})\), while entries outside \(\mathcal F\) need not be computed or stored.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A reverse selected-inversion recurrence computes exactly the inverse entries on the filled factor pattern, avoiding formation and storage of the dense inverse.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) is symmetric positive definite and \(A=LDL^{\mathsf T}\) uses unit lower-triangular \(L\).
The selected pattern is the symmetric chordal fill pattern of the factor.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Z_{ij}=(A^{-1})_{ij}\) for every \((i,j)\in\mathcal F\), without computing entries outside \(\mathcal F\).

notation.meaning: Symmetric filled pattern induced by the sparse factor.

knowledge_statements.title: Selected-Entry Coverage
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coverage of projected inverse entries needed by sparse barrier derivatives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P_E:\mathbb S^n\to\mathcal V_E\) be the orthogonal coordinate projection onto matrices supported on \(E\). Because \(E\subseteq E^+\), knowledge of \((X^{-1})_{ij}\) for every \((i,j)\in E^+\) determines \(P_E(X^{-1})\). Consequently, for \(F(X)=-\log\det X\) restricted to \(\mathcal V_E\cap\mathbb S_{++}^n\), the gradient with respect to the Frobenius inner product is \(\nabla F(X)=-P_E(X^{-1})\). Thus no inverse entry outside \(E^+\) is required to evaluate this gradient.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Because the chordal filled pattern contains the original sparsity pattern, its selected inverse entries determine every coordinate of the projected inverse used by the sparse log-determinant gradient.
assumptions_latex: \(E\subseteq E^+\) are symmetric index patterns containing every diagonal, and \(G^+=(V,E^+)\) is chordal.
\(X\in\mathcal V_E\cap\mathbb S_{++}^n\), where \(\mathcal V_E\) is the subspace of symmetric matrices supported on \(E\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Selected inversion on \(E^+\) covers every entry of \(P_E(X^{-1})\), hence every coordinate of the sparse log-determinant gradient.

knowledge_statements.title: Sparse Log-Barrier Calculus
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Differential calculus for the log-determinant barrier on a fixed sparse matrix subspace.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(F:\mathcal V_E\cap\mathbb S_{++}^n\to\mathbb R\) by \(F(X)=-\log\det X\). With the Frobenius inner product, its gradient is \(\nabla F(X)=-P_E(X^{-1})\). For every \(H\in\mathcal V_E\), the Hessian action is \(\nabla^2F(X)[H]=P_E(X^{-1}HX^{-1})\). Equivalently, for all \(H,K\in\mathcal V_E\), \(D^2F(X)[H,K]=\operatorname{tr}(X^{-1}HX^{-1}K)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On the sparse positive-definite domain, the log-determinant barrier has projected negative-inverse gradient, and its Hessian maps a sparse direction through two inverse factors followed by projection.

\(X\in\mathcal V_E\cap\mathbb S_{++}^n\), where \(\mathcal V_E\) is the subspace of symmetric matrices supported on \(E\).

Each clique has a local variable and potential, and adjacent clique variables agree on their separator.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Two directed passes on \(T\) compute the exact optimum and a globally consistent collection of clique minimizers whenever all message infima are attained.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose a root of \(T\). For every oriented edge \(i\to j\), compute \[m_{i\to j}(s)=\inf_{x_i:\,x_i|_{S_{ij}}=s}\left(\phi_i(x_i)+\sum_{k\in N(i)\setminus\{j\}}m_{k\to i}(x_i|_{S_{ki}})\right).\] First evaluate messages from leaves to the root. Minimize the root potential plus all incoming messages, then traverse outward, selecting at each clique an attaining minimizer consistent with its parent's separator value. The running-intersection property makes these pairwise separator agreements globally consistent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Clique potentials are eliminated toward a root through separator-valued messages, then an outward pass reconstructs globally consistent clique solutions.

knowledge_statements.title: Parallel Clique-PSD Kernels
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Embarrassingly parallel spectral projections for clique-local PSD blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each \(k\in\{1,\ldots,q\}\), independently compute \(W_k=Q_k\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_{k,1},\ldots,\lambda_{k,p_k})Q_k^{\mathsf T}\), where \(p_k=|C_k|\), and set \[Y_k=Q_k\operatorname{diag}(\max\{\lambda_{k,1},0\},\ldots,\max\{\lambda_{k,p_k},0\})Q_k^{\mathsf T}.\] Return \((Y_1,ldots,Y_q)\) after all local eigendecompositions finish. Any separator averaging or agreement update is a separate synchronization stage. Each \(Y_k\) is the Frobenius-norm projection of \(W_k\) onto \(\mathbb S_+^{p_k}\), and no clique projection depends on another clique's eigendecomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each clique PSD projection independently thresholds the eigenvalues of its local symmetric matrix, permitting concurrent execution before a separate separator-consistency stage.
assumptions_latex: For \(k=1,\ldots,q\), the clique \(C_k\) has order \(p_k=|C_k|\), and \(W_k\in\mathbb S^{p_k}\).
Each local kernel uses a symmetric eigendecomposition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The outputs satisfy \(Y_k=\Pi_{\mathbb S_+^{p_k}}(W_k)\) independently for every \(k\), so all clique kernels may execute concurrently before separator synchronization.

notation.meaning: Symmetric matrix associated with clique k
Frobenius-norm projection onto the positive-semidefinite cone of order p_k

children.title: Excessive Fill
children.top_down_role: Chordal extensions whose added structure defeats sparse storage or factorization.

assumptions_latex: \(G_n=(V_n,E_n)\) is a sparse graph family and \(G_n^+=(V_n,E_n^+)\) is the chordal fill produced by the chosen ordering.
Sparse factorization stores at least one numerical entry per filled edge.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(|E_n^+|/|E_n|\to\infty\), fill storage and arithmetic cannot remain proportional to the original sparse input size.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Asymptotic loss of sparsity caused by an unfavorable chordal completion.

source_refs.locator: 3.3 Special Cases and Structure Exploitation p. 86

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f_n=|E_n^+\setminus E_n|\) denote the number of fill edges. A chordal method enters the excessive-fill regime when \[\frac{|E_n^+|}{|E_n|}=1+\frac{f_n}{|E_n|}\longrightarrow\infty.\] Since a numerical factorization must represent contributions on the filled pattern, its storage is at least \(\Omega(|E_n^+|)\). Thus no implementation based on this completion can have storage proportional to \(|E_n|\); arithmetic involving the filled factors likewise scales with the completion rather than the original graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Chordal sparsity ceases to scale when the filled graph grows asymptotically larger than the original graph, forcing storage and work to follow the fill.
knowledge_statements.title: Excessive Fill

knowledge_statements.title: Oversized Cliques
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dense local PSD kernels become dominant when the chordal completion contains a large clique.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a clique \(C_k\) of order \(p_k=|C_k|\), its local symmetric matrix has \(p_k(p_k+1)/2\) independent scalar entries. A dense representation uses \(\Theta(p_k^2)\) storage, and a standard full eigendecomposition or dense Cholesky-type factorization uses \(\Theta(p_k^3)\) arithmetic. Therefore, if \(\omega=\max_k p_k\), the clique collection requires at least \[\Omega(\omega^2)\text{ storage and }\Omega(\omega^3)\text{ arithmetic}\] for such a largest-clique kernel. If \(\omega\) grows comparably with the ambient matrix order, clique decomposition does not remove the dense-kernel bottleneck.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A largest clique of order omega forces quadratic dense storage and cubic work for a standard full spectral or factorization kernel, even if the remaining cliques are small.
assumptions_latex: A chordal conversion has maximal cliques \(C_1,\ldots,C_q\).
Each clique is processed by a dense full spectral or Cholesky-type kernel.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A clique of order \(\omega\) forces \(\Omega(\omega^2)\) storage and \(\Omega(\omega^3)\) arithmetic for a standard dense full spectral or factorization kernel.

assumptions_latex: An elimination step removes a vertex \(v\) having \(d\) later neighbors.
Those later neighbors are not already a clique.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Eliminating \(v\) completes its later-neighbor set into a clique, potentially creating \(\binom d2\) edges and a clique of order at least \(d\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At elimination of \(v\), chordal completion adds every missing edge among vertices in \(N_+(v)\). The number added at this step is \[\binom d2-|E(N_+(v))|,\] and \(N_+(v)\cup\{v\}\) becomes a clique in the filled graph. In particular, eliminating the center first in a star with \(d\) leaves adds \(\binom d2\) edges and creates a clique on all leaves. Thus an unfavorable ordering can convert bounded original clique size into clique size growing with \(d\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Eliminating a vertex connects all of its remaining neighbors; a high-degree early elimination can turn a sparse neighborhood into a large filled clique.
knowledge_statements.title: Fill-Induced Clique Growth

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an edge \((i,j)\in E(T)\), equality of the two symmetric principal submatrices on \(S_{ij}\) requires \(|S_{ij}|(|S_{ij}|+1)/2\) scalar equations. Therefore \[N_{\mathrm{sep}}=\sum_{(i,j)\in E(T)}\frac{|S_{ij}|(|S_{ij}|+1)}2.\] Separator constraints proliferate when this sum is not small relative to the original affine-constraint count or sparse-variable dimension. In that regime, the converted formulation may spend more storage and linear-system work enforcing consistency than processing the original constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A clique-tree conversion adds one equality per symmetric separator entry; many large separators can make consistency constraints dominate the converted model.

assumptions_latex: The converted Newton system has block-diagonal local scaling \(H=\operatorname{diag}(H_1,\ldots,H_q)\succ0\).
The affine-constraint matrix \(A\) has rows that simultaneously touch multiple clique blocks.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The reduced matrix \(S=AH^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}\) may be dense even though \(H\) is block diagonal.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Chordal block structure does not guarantee sparsity of the reduced affine-constraint system.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Write the row and block partitions as \(A=[A_1\ \cdots\ A_q]\) and \(H=\operatorname{diag}(H_1,\ldots,H_q)\). Then \[S=AH^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}=\sum_{k=1}^q A_kH_k^{-1}A_k^{\mathsf T}.\] For constraint rows \(a
e b\), the entry \(S_{ab}\) can be nonzero whenever both rows touch a common clique block. If every pair of constraint rows overlaps on some block, the structural pattern of \(S\) is complete. Thus clique-local PSD structure can coexist with a dense global reduced system after conversion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Local clique Hessians can remain block diagonal while globally coupled constraints produce a dense Schur complement, removing the expected sparse linear-algebra benefit.
knowledge_statements.title: Dense Coupling After Conversion

assumptions_latex: Consistency equations are represented by \(Bx=0\), and \(W\succ0\) is the local scaling on duplicated separator variables.
The independent-row consistency matrix is denoted \(\bar B\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The consistency Schur matrix \(K=\bar BW^{-1}\bar B^{\mathsf T}\) is positive definite but becomes ill-conditioned when the scaled rows of \(\bar B\) are nearly dependent; retained redundant rows make it singular.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral failure boundary for scaled separator-consistency equations.

source_refs.locator: 3.3 Special Cases and Structure Exploitation p. 86
source_refs.source_title: Semidefinite Optimization and Convex Algebraic Geometry

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: With redundant consistency rows removed, define \(K=\bar BW^{-1}\bar B^{\mathsf T}\). Its extreme eigenvalues satisfy \[\lambda_{\min}(K)=\sigma_{\min}(\bar BW^{-1/2})^2,\qquad \lambda_{\max}(K)=\sigma_{\max}(\bar BW^{-1/2})^2.\] Hence \(\kappa_2(K)=\kappa_2(\bar BW^{-1/2})^2\), so nearly dependent scaled consistency rows produce a severely ill-conditioned system. If dependent rows are retained, then \(B\) lacks full row rank and \(BW^{-1}B^{\mathsf T}\) is singular, requiring constraint removal, regularization, or a null-space treatment.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Consistency Schur systems square the condition number of the scaled incidence operator; near dependencies cause ill-conditioning, while exact redundant equations cause singularity.
knowledge_statements.title: Ill-Conditioned Consistency Systems

knowledge_statements.statement_title: SDP face-dimension, nondegeneracy, and complementarity rank bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rank restrictions for feasible primal and dual SDP faces; \(t(k)=k(k+1)/2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a primal–dual SDP pair defined by \(A\), with \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), \(c\in\mathcal S^n\), feasible \(\bar x\) and \((\bar y,\bar z)\), primal feasible-set face \(\mathcal F=\operatorname{face}(\bar x,\operatorname{Feas}(P))\), dual feasible-set face \(\mathcal G=\operatorname{face}((\bar y,\bar z),\operatorname{Feas}(D))\), and ranks \(r=\operatorname{rank}\bar x\), \(s=\operatorname{rank}\bar z\). With \(t(k)=k(k+1)/2\), one has \(t(r)\leq m+\dim\mathcal F\) and \(t(s)\leq t(n)-m+\dim\mathcal G\). If \(\bar x\) is nondegenerate, then \(t(n-r)\leq t(n)-m\); if \((\bar y,\bar z)\) is nondegenerate, then \(t(n-s)\leq m\). Moreover, the pair is strictly complementary if and only if \(r+s=n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The ranks of feasible primal and dual SDP points are bounded by the number of affine constraints plus the dimensions of their feasible-set faces. Nondegeneracy strengthens the complementary-rank bounds. Strict complementarity is exactly the condition that the primal and dual slack ranks sum to the matrix size.
assumptions_latex: \bar x\in\operatorname{Feas}(P),\quad (\bar y,\bar z)\in\operatorname{Feas}(D)
\mathcal F=\operatorname{face}(\bar x,\operatorname{Feas}(P)),\quad r=\operatorname{rank}\bar x
\mathcal G=\operatorname{face}((\bar y,\bar z),\operatorname{Feas}(D)),\quad s=\operatorname{rank}\bar z
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: t(r)\leq m+\dim\mathcal F,\quad t(s)\leq t(n)-m+\dim\mathcal G;\quad \bar x\text{ nondegenerate}\Rightarrow t(n-r)\leq t(n)-m;\quad (\bar y,\bar z)\text{ nondegenerate}\Rightarrow t(n-s)\leq m;\quad \text{strict complementarity}\Longleftrightarrow r+s=n.

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Complementary primal and dual PSD optima of the same order have orthogonal ranges, so their ranks sum to at most that order; equality characterizes strict complementarity.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L_*\) be the aggregate range of the primal optimal set, and let \(S_*\succeq0\) be a dual optimal slack complementary to every primal optimum. Then \(S_*X=0\) for all primal optima \(X\), so \(L_*\subseteq\ker(S_*)\). Thus the exposed face \[\{X\succeq0:\langle S_*,X\rangle=0\}=\{X\succeq0:\operatorname{range}(X)\subseteq\ker(S_*)\}\] contains the primal optimal face. knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dimension Relations for Complementary SDP Faces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Facial, tangent-cone, normal-cone, and rank relations at complementary primal-dual SDP solutions; the displayed minus signs normalize apparent extraction corruption.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \((P)\) and \((D)\) be semidefinite programs with the source's primal-dual data and notation. Let \(\bar x\) and \((\bar y,\bar z)\) be complementary solutions, set \(r=\operatorname{rank}\bar x\), \(s=\operatorname{rank}\bar z\), \(\mathcal F=\operatorname{face}(\bar x,\operatorname{Feas}(P))\), \(\mathcal T=\tan(\bar x,\operatorname{Feas}(P))\), \(\mathcal G=\operatorname{face}((\bar y,\bar z),\operatorname{Feas}(D))\), and \(\mathcal U=\tan((\bar y,\bar z),\operatorname{Feas}(D))\), where \(t(k)=k(k+1)/2\). Then
\[
t(r)-m+\dim\mathcal U\leq \dim\mathcal F\leq t(n-s)-m+\dim\mathcal U,
\]
\[
\dim\mathcal F+\dim\operatorname{ncone}(\bar x,\operatorname{Feas}(P))\geq t(r)+t(s)+\dim\bigl(\operatorname{res}\mathcal F\cap\mathcal R(A^*)\bigr).
\]
If strict complementarity holds, then
\[
\dim\mathcal U+\dim\mathcal T=\dim\mathcal F+\dim\mathcal G+r(n-r)
\]
and
\[
t(n)-t(n-r)-\dim\mathcal T\leq m\leq t(r)+\dim\mathcal U.
\]
The left inequality is an equality if and only if the primal solution is unique, and the right inequality is an equality if and only if the dual solution is unique.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(n,r\in\mathbb N\) with \(r\le n\), and let \(Y\in\mathbb R_*^{n\times r}\). At \(Y\), infinitesimal motion along the right orthogonal gauge orbit has the form \(Y\Omega\), where \(\Omega\in\mathbb R^{r\times r}\) satisfies \(\Omega^{\mathsf T}=-\Omega\). Hence the vertical space is \(\mathcal V_Y=\{Y\Omega:\Omega^{\mathsf T}=-\Omega\}\). With the Frobenius metric on \(T_Y\mathbb R_*^{n\times r}=\mathbb R^{n\times r}\), its orthogonal complement is \[\mathcal H_Y=\{\xi\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}:Y^{\mathsf T}\xi=\xi^{\mathsf T}Y\}.\] Every tangent perturbation decomposes uniquely into vertical and horizontal components; only the horizontal component represents a first-order displacement in the quotient.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a full-column-rank factor, tangent directions split uniquely into orthogonal gauge directions and Frobenius-orthogonal horizontal directions that represent quotient displacements.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(n,r\in\mathbb N\), let \(Y\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}\), and define \(X=YY^{\mathsf T}\). The orthogonal gauge orbit through \(Y\) is \(\mathcal O_Y=\{YQ:Q\in\mathrm O(r)\}\), and every member satisfies \((YQ)(YQ)^{\mathsf T}=YY^{\mathsf T}\). Thus the factorization is nonunique whenever this orbit contains more than one point. Let \(\phi:\mathbb S_+^n\to\mathbb R\) be differentiable on a neighborhood of \(X\) relative to its domain, and define \(f:\mathbb R^{n\times r}\to\mathbb R\) by \(f(Y)=\phi(YY^{\mathsf T})\). Then \(f(YQ)=f(Y)\) for every \(Q\in\mathrm O(r)\). Consequently, for every \(\Omega\in\mathbb R^{r\times r}\) satisfying \(\Omega^{\mathsf T}=-\Omega\), \[\langle\nabla f(Y),Y\Omega\rangle_F=0,\] so orbit directions are redundant first-order directions in an unreduced factor parametrization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Right orthogonal rotations leave YY transpose unchanged, producing equivalent factors; for any differentiable objective depending only on YY transpose, the Frobenius directional derivative vanishes along every infinitesimal orbit direction.
knowledge_statements.title: Gauge-Orbit Redundancy

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Quadratic and Minimizer-Distance Bounds for a Low-Rank Schatten Surrogate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The theorem first gives a pointwise lower bound, then two consequences for minimizers over a nonempty set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume \(r\ge1\) and \(\frac1r\|X\|_{(2)}^2\le\|X\|_{(\infty)}^2\le\|X\|_{(2p)}^2\) for every \(X\in\mathbb S_n\) with \(\operatorname{rank}(X)\le r\) and every integer \(p\ge1\). Let \(f_p(y)=\tfrac12\|X(y)\|_{(2p)}^2\), where \(X(y)\in\mathbb S_n\), \(\operatorname{rank}(X(y))\le r\), and \(\|y\|_G=\|X(y)\|_{(\infty)}\) for every \(y\in\mathbb R^m\). Then \(\frac1{2r}\|y\|_G^2\le f_p(y)\) for every \(y\). Consequently, if \(\varnothing\ne Q\subseteq\mathbb R^m\), \(y_p^*\in\arg\min_{y\in Q}f_p(y)\), and \(f_p^*=\min_{y\in Q}f_p(y)\), then \(\frac1{2r}\|y_p^*\|_G^2\le f_p^*\); moreover, if \(x_0\in\arg\min_{y\in Q}\|y\|_G\), then \(\frac12\|y_p^*-x_0\|_G^2\le r f_p^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The low-rank Schatten-norm comparison makes the surrogate dominate one over 2r times the squared G-seminorm. This bounds the norm of a surrogate minimizer and, relative to a minimum-G-norm point of the feasible set, bounds its squared distance by 2r times the optimal surrogate value.

\operatorname{rank}(X(y))\le r,\quad \|y\|_G=\|X(y)\|_{(\infty)}\quad\forall y\in\mathbb R^m
\varnothing\ne Q\subseteq\mathbb R^m,\quad y_p^*\in\arg\min_{y\in Q}f_p(y)
x_0\in\arg\min_{y\in Q}\|y\|_G\quad\text{for the distance conclusion}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \frac1{2r}\|y\|_G^2\le f_p(y)\ \forall y;\qquad \frac1{2r}\|y_p^*\|_G^2\le f_p^*;\qquad \frac12\|y_p^*-x_0\|_G^2\le r f_p^*

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Y=QR\), where the columns of \(Q\in\mathbb R^{n\times s}\) are orthonormal and span \(\operatorname{range}(Y)\). Define \(B=RR^{\mathsf T}\succeq0\) and choose its positive-semidefinite square root \(B^{1/2}\). The compressed factor \[Z=QB^{1/2}\in\mathbb R^{n\times s}\] satisfies \[ZZ^{\mathsf T}=QRR^{\mathsf T}Q^{\mathsf T}=YY^{\mathsf T}.\] Hence redundant columns are removed exactly, and the factor width becomes \(s=\operatorname{rank}(Y)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rank-revealing factorization removes redundant factor columns while preserving the represented positive-semidefinite matrix exactly.
knowledge_statements.title: Factor Compression

children.title: Rank Truncation
children.top_down_role: Removal of weak factor directions to control effective rank.

knowledge_statements.title: Rank Truncation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive-semidefinite specialization of best rank-\(k\) approximation in Frobenius norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\sum_{j=1}^n\lambda_jq_jq_j^{\mathsf T}\in\mathbb S_+^n\), with \(\lambda_1\ge\cdots\ge\lambda_n\ge0\), and define \(X_k=\sum_{j=1}^k\lambda_jq_jq_j^{\mathsf T}\). Then \[X_k\in\underset{Z\in\mathbb S_+^n,\,\operatorname{rank}(Z)\le k}{\operatorname{argmin}}\|X-Z\|_F,\qquad \|X-X_k\|_F=\left(\sum_{j=k+1}^n\lambda_j^2\right)^{1/2}.\] A compatible truncated factor is \(Y_k=[\sqrt{\lambda_1}q_1,\ldots,\sqrt{\lambda_k}q_k]\), for which \(Y_kY_k^{\mathsf T}=X_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Keeping the largest k eigenpairs gives the closest rank-k positive-semidefinite approximation in Frobenius norm.
assumptions_latex: \(X\in\mathbb S_+^n\) has eigenvalues \(\lambda_1\ge\cdots\ge\lambda_n\ge0\).
\(0\le k<n\), and \(X_k=\sum_{j=1}^k\lambda_jq_jq_j^{\mathsf T}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X_k\) minimizes \(\|X-Z\|_F\) over \(Z\in\mathbb S_+^n\) with \(\operatorname{rank}(Z)\le k\), and the minimum is \((\sum_{j>k}\lambda_j^2)^{1/2}\).

notation.meaning: Ordered eigenvalues and orthonormal eigenvectors of X

children.title: Compression Error Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Accuracy and certificate limits introduced by approximate factor reduction.

assumptions_latex: \(X,X_k\in\mathbb S_+^n\) are the matrix and its rank-\(k\) spectral truncation.
\(\mathcal A:\mathbb S^n\to\mathbb R^m\) is linear with induced norm \(\|\mathcal A\|_{F\to2}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|\mathcal A(X)-\mathcal A(X_k)\|_2\le\|\mathcal A\|_{F\to2}(\sum_{j>k}\lambda_j^2)^{1/2}\), and the spectral tail cannot generally be omitted.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp norm boundary relating discarded eigenvalues to constraint and linear-objective perturbations.

source_refs.locator: 2.2 Norms and inner products p. 28

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(E_k=X-X_k=
\sum_{j>k}\lambda_jq_jq_j^{\mathsf T}\), \[\|E_k\|_2=\lambda_{k+1},\qquad \|E_k\|_F=\left(\sum_{j>k}\lambda_j^2\right)^{1/2},\qquad \operatorname{tr}(E_k)=\sum_{j>k}\lambda_j.\] Consequently, \[\|\mathcal A(X)-\mathcal A(X_k)\|_2\le\|\mathcal A\|_{F\to2}\|E_k\|_F.\] For any \(C\in\mathbb S^n\), \(|\langle C,E_k\rangle|\le\|C\|_F\|E_k\|_F\). These bounds are attained for aligned operators or objectives, so truncation offers no uniform smaller guarantee without additional structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Discarded eigenvalues exactly determine matrix error and bound constraint and objective perturbations; aligned data can attain these bounds.

children.title: Fixed-Rank Regimes
children.top_down_role: Problem phases where a prescribed factor rank remains adequate.

assumptions_latex: A factorized SDP uses \(X=YY^{\mathsf T}\) with \(Y\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}\).
The prescribed rank \(r\) is unchanged throughout the run.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The regime is certified only when feasibility, stationarity, and cone-dual residuals meet their tolerances without increasing \(r\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational fixed-width regime defined relative to residual certificates supplied by the enclosing solver.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A run is in a fixed-rank regime of width \(r\) when every iterate is represented as \(X_t=Y_tY_t^{\mathsf T}\) with \(Y_t\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}\), and no rank-expansion or restart event occurs. It terminates successfully in that regime only if its declared certificates satisfy \[\|R_p(Y_t)\|\le\varepsilon_p,
\qquad \|R_s(Y_t)\|\le\varepsilon_s,
\qquad \|R_d(Y_t)\|\le\varepsilon_d.\] Failure to meet these inequalities is not by itself evidence that the underlying SDP is infeasible; the chosen factor width may be insufficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed-rank run keeps one factor width and succeeds only when all declared residual certificates pass at that width.
knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Rank Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The fixed-width description is plausible, but the residual maps and their relationship to feasibility, stationarity, and cone duality are solver-dependent and undefined. An authoritative source specifying the enclosing certificate system is required.

children.title: Rank-Continuation Regimes
children.top_down_role: Problem phases using a sequence of increasing or adapted ranks.

assumptions_latex: Factor widths satisfy \(1\le r_0<r_1<\cdots\le n\).
At each stage, the current factor is embedded into the next factor space without changing its represented matrix.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The continuation either terminates at the first certified stage or increases rank while preserving the previous matrix as the next stage's initial point.

notation.meaning: Factor width at continuation stage ell

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Warm-started continuation over increasing factor widths, with solver-specific certificates left abstract.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose widths \(r_0<r_1<\cdots"). At stage \(\ell\), optimize over \(Y^{(\ell)}\in\mathbb R^{n\times r_\ell}\) from the available warm start and test the declared termination certificate. If it passes, output \(X^{(\ell)}=Y^{(\ell)}Y^{(\ell)\mathsf T}\). Otherwise choose \(r_{\ell+1}>r_\ell\), initialize \[Y_0^{(\ell+1)}=[Y^{(\ell)}\ \ 0],\] so that \(Y_0^{(\ell+1)}Y_0^{(\ell+1)\mathsf T}=X^{(\ell)}\), and continue. Stop with failure if no larger permitted width remains.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rank continuation warm-starts a sequence of increasing factor widths and stops at the first stage whose certificate passes.
knowledge_statements.title: Rank-Continuation Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The zero-column embedding identity is correct, but the continuation schedule, stopping certificate, and exhaustion rule define a framework-dependent algorithm with no cited source.

children.title: Rank-Regime Transitions
children.top_down_role: Diagnostics and events motivating movement between fixed-rank and continuation modes.

assumptions_latex: The current stage has width \(r\), residual state \(R\), and rank-control tolerances.
A transition policy specifies mutually exclusive predicates for acceptance, expansion, restart, and failure.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exactly one transition is selected from \(\{\mathrm{accept},\mathrm{expand},\mathrm{restart},\mathrm{fail}\}\) according to the ordered predicates.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic transition interface; numerical thresholds must be supplied by the enclosing rank-control system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(P_{\mathrm{acc}}(R)\), \(P_{\mathrm{exp}}(R,r)\), and \(P_{\mathrm{rst}}(R,r)\) be declared predicates. Require \(P_{\mathrm{acc}}\) to encode the complete stopping certificate and evaluate decisions in the order \[\tau=
\begin{cases}
\mathrm{accept},&P_{\mathrm{acc}}(R),\\
\mathrm{expand},&\neg P_{\mathrm{acc}}(R)\wedge P_{\mathrm{exp}}(R,r),\\
\mathrm{restart},&\neg P_{\mathrm{acc}}(R)\wedge\neg P_{\mathrm{exp}}(R,r)\wedge P_{\mathrm{rst}}(R,r),\\
\mathrm{fail},&\text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}\] A rank-regime transition is well-defined only if each predicate uses diagnostics available at the current stage and every permitted state receives one decision.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rank-regime transition applies ordered certificate, expansion, and restart predicates so every stage has one deterministic outcome.
knowledge_statements.title: Rank-Regime Transitions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The ordered case distinction is deterministic once predicates are supplied, but the predicates contain all substantive rank-control semantics and are neither defined nor sourced.

children.title: Rank Expansion
children.top_down_role: Increasing factor capacity while retaining useful current-state information.

assumptions_latex: \(Y\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}\) is the current factor and \(v_1,\ldots,v_p\in\mathbb R^n\) are selected orthonormal expansion directions.
\(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_p>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The expanded factor \(Y_+=[Y,\sqrt{\alpha_1}v_1,\ldots,\sqrt{\alpha_p}v_p]\) represents \(Y_+Y_+^{\mathsf T}=YY^{\mathsf T}+\sum_j\alpha_jv_jv_j^{\mathsf T}\succeq YY^{\mathsf T}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic rank expansion after an external certificate selects new directions and positive weights.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a certificate-selected block \(V=[v_1,\ldots,v_p]\) and positive weights \(\alpha_j\), form \[Y_+=[Y,\sqrt{\alpha_1}v_1,\ldots,\sqrt{\alpha_p}v_p].\] Then \[Y_+Y_+^{\mathsf T}=YY^{\mathsf T}+\sum_{j=1}^p\alpha_jv_jv_j^{\mathsf T}\succeq YY^{\mathsf T}.\] Continue optimization at width \(r+p\), and stop according to the enclosing solver's certificate. The expansion is effective only when the selected directions are not contained in \(\operatorname{range}(Y)\); otherwise the represented matrix changes but its attainable column space does not expand.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rank expansion appends positively weighted certified directions to the factor and then resumes optimization at the larger width.
knowledge_statements.title: Rank Expansion

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The appended-column identity is correct, but the candidate presents an algorithm whose direction and weight selection are delegated to an unspecified certificate. A source for the actual rank-expansion rule is required.

children.title: Rank Restart
children.top_down_role: Reinitializing low-rank state after inadequate or unstable rank choices.

assumptions_latex: \(X_c\in\mathbb S_+^n\) is a restart matrix obtained from the current solver state.
A restart width \(r_+\) and spectral retention rule are specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The restarted factor \(Y_+\) satisfies \(Y_+Y_+^{\mathsf T}=(X_c)_{r_+}\), the retained positive spectral part of \(X_c\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral reconstruction of a factor after the enclosing policy declares the current factor state unsuitable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Compute an eigendecomposition \(X_c=Q\operatorname{diag}(\lambda)Q^{\mathsf T}\), with \(\lambda_1\ge\cdots\ge\lambda_n\ge0\). Retain \(s\le r_+\) eigenvalues prescribed by the restart rule and set \[Y_+=[\sqrt{\lambda_1}q_1,\ldots,\sqrt{\lambda_s}q_s,0,
\ldots,0]\in\mathbb R^{n\times r_+}.\] Reinitialize factor-dependent solver state and resume from \(Y_+\). The represented restart matrix is \(Y_+Y_+^{\mathsf T}=\sum_{j=1}^s\lambda_jq_jq_j^{\mathsf T}\); any discarded spectral mass is governed by the truncation error bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rank restart rebuilds the factor from a chosen positive-semidefinite matrix's retained eigenpairs and resets factor-dependent solver state.
knowledge_statements.title: Rank Restart

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Spectral factor reconstruction is algebraically valid, but selection of the restart matrix, retained spectrum, restart width, and reset state is method-dependent and unsupported.

children.title: Expansion–Restart Selection
children.top_down_role: Structural and numerical signals distinguishing expansion from restart.

assumptions_latex: The stopping certificate fails at the current factor \(Y\).
An expansion direction test and a restart-validity test are available from current diagnostics.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Choose expansion when a certified improving direction lies outside \(\operatorname{range}(Y)\); choose restart when expansion lacks such a direction but the restart-validity test passes.

notation.meaning: Orthogonal projector onto the complement of the factor range

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract selection principle separating representational rank deficiency from a defective current factor state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: After the stopping certificate fails, let \(v\) be a direction satisfying the enclosing method's improvement certificate. Select rank expansion when \[\|P_Y^\perp v\|_2>\eta_{\mathrm{span}}\] and the predicted improvement exceeds its acceptance threshold. Select rank restart when no accepted out-of-span direction exists, but the diagnostics declare the current factorization or solver state defective and provide a valid restart matrix \(X_c\succeq0\). If neither test passes, return an unresolved rank-control failure rather than asserting convergence. Thus expansion addresses insufficient attainable column space, whereas restart replaces an unsuitable state.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Expand for a certified direction outside the current factor range; restart for a defective state with a valid replacement matrix; otherwise report failure.
knowledge_statements.title: Expansion–Restart Selection

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed distinction between expansion and restart is plausible but solver-dependent. The improvement certificate, span threshold, predicted-improvement test, defect diagnostic, and restart-validity test require a precise sourced method.

knowledge_statements.title: Rank-Adequacy Diagnostics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact primal-dual diagnostic for adequacy of a chosen factor rank.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the primal SDP \(\min\{\langle C,X\rangle:\mathcal A(X)=b,\ X\succeq0\}\) and its dual \(\max\{b^{\mathsf T}y:C-\mathcal A^*(y)\succeq0\}\). A factor rank \(r\) is adequate whenever there exist \(Y\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}\) and \(y\in\mathbb R^m\) such that \[\mathcal A(YY^{\mathsf T})=b,\qquad S:=C-\mathcal A^*(y)\succeq0,\qquad SY=0.\] Then \(X=YY^{\mathsf T}\) is primal optimal, \(y\) is dual optimal, and the primal-dual gap is zero. Failure to find such objects is not, by itself, evidence that rank \(r\) is inadequate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rank is certified adequate when a feasible factor and feasible dual slack satisfy complementary slackness; failure to obtain this certificate is inconclusive.
assumptions_latex: \(C\in\mathbb S^n\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(\mathcal A:\mathbb S^n\to\mathbb R^m\) is linear.
The displayed primal and dual problems have finite objective values.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X=YY^{\mathsf T}\) and \(y\) are optimal with \(\langle C,X\rangle=b^{\mathsf T}y\).

children.title: Dual-Slack Validation
children.top_down_role: Feasibility, spectral, and storage checks for reconstructed dual slack.

assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal A:\mathbb S^n\to\mathbb R^m\) is linear, \(C\in\mathbb S^n\), and \(b\in\mathbb R^m\).
The primal problem is \(\min\{\langle C,X\rangle:\mathcal A(X)=b,\ X\succeq0\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((y,S)\) is dual feasible and \(b^{\mathsf T}y\le \langle C,X\rangle\) for every primal-feasible \(X\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal A:\mathbb S^n\to\mathbb R^m\), \(C\in\mathbb S^n\), and \(b\in\mathbb R^m\). For the dual problem \(\max\{b^{\mathsf T}y:C-\mathcal A^*(y)\succeq0\}\), a proposed multiplier \(y\in\mathbb R^m\) is validated by reconstructing \(S\in\mathbb S^n\), checking \(C-\mathcal A^*(y)-S=0\), and verifying \(\lambda_{\min}(S)\ge0\). These checks imply \(S=C-\mathcal A^*(y)\succeq0\), so \((y,S)\) is dual feasible. Consequently, \(b^{\mathsf T}y\) is a lower bound on \(\langle C,X\rangle\) for every \(X\in\mathbb S^n\) satisfying \(\mathcal A(X)=b\) and \(X\succeq0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A reconstructed slack is valid when its defining equality holds and its smallest eigenvalue is nonnegative, yielding a dual lower bound.

children.title: Primal-Reconstruction Validation
children.top_down_role: Feasibility and consistency checks for a primal matrix recovered from compact state.

assumptions_latex: \(Y\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}\), \(\mathcal A:\mathbb S^n\to\mathbb R^m\) is linear, \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(C\in\mathbb S^n\).
The primal constraints are \(\mathcal A(X)=b\) and \(X\succeq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X=YY^{\mathsf T}\) is primal feasible whenever \(\mathcal A(YY^{\mathsf T})=b\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Y\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}\), and define \(X=YY^{\mathsf T}\in\mathbb S^n\). The factorization certifies \(X\succeq0\). For a linear map \(\mathcal A:\mathbb S^n\to\mathbb R^m\) and \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), if direct evaluation additionally gives \(\mathcal A(X)=b\), then \(X\) is feasible for \(\min\{\langle C,X\rangle:\mathcal A(X)=b,\ X\succeq0\}\), where \(C\in\mathbb S^n\). Thus primal validation requires checking only the affine residual after reconstruction; it does not certify optimality unless accompanied by a compatible dual certificate and zero gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A factor reconstruction is primal feasible when its affine residual vanishes; positive semidefiniteness follows automatically from the Gram form.

children.title: Cross-Certificate Consistency
children.top_down_role: Agreement among primal reconstruction, dual slack, objectives, and residual evidence.

assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal A:\mathbb S^n\to\mathbb R^m\) is linear, \(C\in\mathbb S^n\), and \(b,y\in\mathbb R^m\).
\(X\in\mathbb S^n\) satisfies \(\mathcal A(X)=b\) and \(X\succeq0\).
\(S=C-\mathcal A^*(y)\in\mathbb S^n\) satisfies \(S\succeq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\langle S,X\rangle=0\) implies \(\langle C,X\rangle=b^{\mathsf T}y\) and joint optimality.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal A:\mathbb S^n\to\mathbb R^m\), \(C\in\mathbb S^n\), and \(b\in\mathbb R^m\). Let \(X\in\mathbb S^n\) satisfy \(\mathcal A(X)=b\) and \(X\succeq0\), and let \(y\in\mathbb R^m\) and \(S=C-\mathcal A^*(y)\in\mathbb S^n\) satisfy \(S\succeq0\). Their objective gap obeys \[\langle C,X\rangle-b^{\mathsf T}y=\langle S,X\rangle\ge0.\] The certificates are cross-consistent at optimality exactly when \(\langle S,X\rangle=0\). For \(S\succeq0\) and \(X\succeq0\), this equality is equivalent to \(SX=0\). If \(X=YY^{\mathsf T}\) for some \(Y\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}\), it is also equivalent to \(SY=0\). Any of these zero-complementarity tests, together with the stated feasibility conditions, certifies primal-dual optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Feasible primal and dual reconstructions are jointly optimal precisely when their slack pairing, equivalently their objective gap, vanishes.
knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Certificate Consistency

knowledge_statements.title: Intrinsically High-Rank Optima
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of rank-restricted parametrization when every optimum has larger rank.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A rank-\(r\) factorization cannot represent an SDP optimum when the minimum rank among optimal matrices exceeds \(r\). Concretely, for \(n>r\), consider \[\min\ 0\quad\text{subject to}\quad X=I_n,\qquad X\succeq0.\] Its unique feasible and optimal matrix is \(I_n\), which has rank \(n\). Since every matrix \(YY^{\mathsf T}\) with \(Y\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}\) has rank at most \(r\), the corresponding rank-restricted factor problem is infeasible even though the original SDP is feasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If all SDP optima have rank above the factor width, the factorized model excludes every optimum and may become infeasible.
assumptions_latex: Factors are restricted to \(Y\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No \(Y\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}\) satisfies \(YY^{\mathsf T}=I_n\).

knowledge_statements.title: Rank-Deficient Factor Constraint Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Jacobian degeneracy induced by unused columns of a rank-deficient factor.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the factorized constraint map \(F(Y)=\mathcal A(YY^{\mathsf T})-b\) for \(Y\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}\). Its derivative is \[DF(Y)[H]=\mathcal A(YH^{\mathsf T}+HY^{\mathsf T}).\] If \(\operatorname{rank}(Y)<r\), choose nonzero \(v\in\ker Y\). For every \(z\in\mathbb R^n\), the perturbation \(H=zv^{\mathsf T}\) satisfies \(DF(Y)[H]=0\). Hence the factor constraint Jacobian has an at least \(n\)-dimensional null subspace, and standard regularity or local-identifiability conditions can fail at rank-deficient factors.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Unused factor directions create a large kernel in the factorized constraint Jacobian, potentially violating regularity and identifiability.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal A:\mathbb S^n\to\mathbb R^m\) is linear.
\(Y\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}\) satisfies \(\operatorname{rank}(Y)<r\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{zv^{\mathsf T}:z\in\mathbb R^n\}\subseteq\ker DF(Y)\) for every nonzero \(v\in\ker Y\).

knowledge_statements.title: Ill-Conditioned Factor Scaling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Numerical instability as the smallest retained factor singular value vanishes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(0<\varepsilon\le1\), let \(Y_\varepsilon=\operatorname{diag}(1,\sqrt\varepsilon)\) and \(X_\varepsilon=Y_\varepsilon Y_\varepsilon^{\mathsf T}=\operatorname{diag}(1,\varepsilon)\). Then \[\kappa_2(Y_\varepsilon)=\varepsilon^{-1/2},\qquad \kappa_2(X_\varepsilon)=\varepsilon^{-1}.\] Thus factors representing matrices near a rank drop become unboundedly ill-conditioned. Perturbations on the scale of \(\varepsilon\) can eliminate or change the relative accuracy of the smallest eigenvalue of \(X_\varepsilon\), so no uniform relative-accuracy guarantee for all factor directions persists as \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Near a rank drop, the factor and Gram matrix condition numbers diverge, making small spectral directions numerically unreliable.
assumptions_latex: \(0<\varepsilon\le1\).
Condition numbers use the spectral norm and are restricted to nonsingular matrices.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\kappa_2(Y_\varepsilon)\to\infty\) and \(\kappa_2(X_\varepsilon)\to\infty\) as \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\).

knowledge_statements.title: Loss of Convex Global Certification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order stationarity after factorization does not imply global SDP optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the convex SDP \[\min\ X_{22}\quad\text{subject to}\quad \operatorname{tr}(X)=1,\qquad X\succeq0.\] Its optimum is \(0\), attained at \(X=e_1e_1^{\mathsf T}\). Under the rank-one parametrization \(X=yy^{\mathsf T}\), the problem becomes \(\min\ y_2^2\) subject to \(\lVert y\rVert_2=1\). The point \(y=e_2\) satisfies the first-order Lagrange stationarity equations but has objective value \(1\), hence is not globally optimal. Factorized stationarity alone therefore cannot replace a convex primal-dual certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After low-rank factorization, even a first-order stationary point can be globally suboptimal, so an independent primal-dual certificate remains necessary.
assumptions_latex: \(e_1,e_2\) are the coordinate vectors in \(\mathbb R^2\).
The factorization is restricted to rank one.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: First-order stationarity of the factor problem does not certify global optimality of the SDP.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Operator Access
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Matrix-free action of adjoint combinations and dual slack matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\mathcal A:\mathbb S^n\to\mathbb R^m\), dual operator access is an oracle that accepts \(y\in\mathbb R^m\) and \(v\in\mathbb R^n\) and returns \(\mathcal A^*(y)v\), or equivalently \(S(y)v=(C-\mathcal A^*(y))v\), without forming the dense matrices \(\mathcal A^*(y)\) or \(S(y)\). With \(\mathcal A(X)_i=\langle A_i,X\rangle\), exact access satisfies \[\mathcal A^*(y)v=\sum_{i=1}^m y_iA_iv.\] This interface supplies the matrix-vector products required by iterative spectral routines.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dual matrix-free oracle applies an adjoint matrix combination or slack matrix to vectors without explicitly assembling that matrix.
assumptions_latex: \(A_i,C\in\mathbb S^n\).
\(\mathcal A(X)_i=\langle A_i,X\rangle\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The oracle returns \(\mathcal A^*(y)v\) or \((C-\mathcal A^*(y))v\) exactly.

knowledge_statements.title: Bidirectional Access Coverage
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Completeness condition for primal-dual matrix-free operator access.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A matrix-free SDP implementation has bidirectional access coverage when it provides both: \(X\mapsto\mathcal A(X)\) for every admissible implicit primal matrix \(X\), and \((y,v)\mapsto\mathcal A^*(y)v\) for every \(y\in\mathbb R^m\) and \(v\in\mathbb R^n\). The two interfaces must represent adjoint maps, meaning that for every admissible \(X\) and every \(y\), \[y^{\mathsf T}\mathcal A(X)=\langle\mathcal A^*(y),X\rangle.\] Coverage is incomplete if either direction is unavailable or if this adjoint-consistency identity fails.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bidirectional coverage requires matrix-free primal evaluation, dual-adjoint action, and consistency of both interfaces under the adjoint identity.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal A:\mathbb S^n\to\mathbb R^m\) is linear.
The implicit input class is sufficient to evaluate the displayed inner product.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Both operator directions are available and satisfy \(y^{\mathsf T}\mathcal A(X)=\langle\mathcal A^*(y),X\rangle\).

If \(\theta<0\), it is a directly checkable witness that \(S(y)\not\succeq0\).
