children.title: Matrix-Free Residual Interface
children.top_down_role: Operator-based evaluation and reporting of optimization residuals.

knowledge_statements.title: Matrix-Free Residual Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual reporting for a primal-dual SDP iterate using operator products rather than assembled matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the primal-dual pair 
\[\min_{X\succeq0}\ \langle C,X\rangle\quad\text{subject to }\mathcal A(X)=b,\qquad \max_y\ b^\top y\quad\text{subject to }S=C-\mathcal A^*(y)\succeq0,\]
a matrix-free residual interface maps an iterate \((X,y,S)\) to \(r_p=\mathcal A(X)-b\), \(r_d=\mathcal A^*(y)+S-C\), and \(r_g=\langle C,X\rangle-b^\top y\), using callable evaluations of \(\mathcal A\), \(\mathcal A^*\), and required inner products. It reports normalized residuals \(\eta_p=\|r_p\|_2/(1+\|b\|_2)\), \(\eta_d=\|r_d\|_F/(1+\|C\|_F)\), and \(\eta_g=|r_g|/(1+|\langle C,X\rangle|+|b^\top y|)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The interface evaluates normalized primal, dual, and objective-gap residuals through linear-operator calls and inner products, without assembling the SDP constraint operator.
assumptions_latex: \(C,X,S\in\mathbb S^n\), \(b,y\in\mathbb R^m\).
\(\mathcal A:\mathbb S^n\to\mathbb R^m\) and its adjoint \(\mathcal A^*\) are callable.
The displayed norms and inner products can be evaluated to the claimed numerical accuracy.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((\eta_p,\eta_d,\eta_g)\) is a matrix-free residual summary for \((X,y,S)\).

notation.meaning: real symmetric matrices of order n
normalized primal, dual, and gap residuals

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the residual-interface leaf and is internally coherent, but no citation supports the particular normalization convention or its designation as a matrix-free interface.

children.title: Matrix-Free Certificate Interface
children.top_down_role: Operator-based production and checking of solution evidence.

knowledge_statements.title: Matrix-Free Certificate Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Verifiable approximate optimality certificate for a matrix-free primal-dual SDP implementation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given tolerances \((\varepsilon_p,\varepsilon_d,\varepsilon_g,\varepsilon_c)\), the interface accepts \((X,y,S)\) as an approximate primal-dual certificate when the residual interface returns \(\eta_p\leq\varepsilon_p\), \(\eta_d\leq\varepsilon_d\), and \(\eta_g\leq\varepsilon_g\), while spectral oracles certify \(\lambda_{\min}(X)\geq-\varepsilon_c\) and \(\lambda_{\min}(S)\geq-\varepsilon_c\). The certificate payload contains the iterate, residual values, eigenvalue lower bounds, tolerances, and oracle error guarantees. If all reported inequalities are rigorous, the payload certifies approximate equality feasibility and approximate membership of both matrix variables in the positive-semidefinite cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A certificate combines residual tests with certified lower bounds on the smallest eigenvalues of the primal and dual slack matrices.
assumptions_latex: The primal-dual SDP and normalized residuals use the residual-interface convention.
Each spectral oracle returns a valid lower bound on the relevant smallest eigenvalue.
All tolerances are nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The accepted payload certifies \(\eta_p\leq\varepsilon_p\), \(\eta_d\leq\varepsilon_d\), \(\eta_g\leq\varepsilon_g\), \(X\succeq-\varepsilon_c I\), and \(S\succeq-\varepsilon_c I\).

notation.meaning: smallest eigenvalue of a symmetric matrix M
identity matrix of the required order

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate content kind and local placement are appropriate. A source is required for the proposed payload contract, tolerance convention, and rigorous eigenvalue-lower-bound requirement.

children.title: Certificate Reliability Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Limits imposed by approximate oracles, sketches, and incomplete matrix access.

knowledge_statements.title: Certificate Reliability Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limits of certificates based on inexact operator evaluations, sketches, and approximate eigensolvers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A matrix-free certificate is reliable only relative to quantified errors in every oracle used to construct it. If the computed residual obeys \(\|\widehat r-r\|\leq\delta_r\), then \(\|\widehat r\|\leq\varepsilon\) implies only \(\|r\|\leq\varepsilon+\delta_r\). If an eigensolver supplies merely a Ritz value \(\widehat\lambda=q^\top Mq\), then \(\widehat\lambda\geq0\) does not imply \(M\succeq0\), because unsearched directions may have negative curvature. Likewise, residuals measured only after a non-injective sketch do not control the full residual without an embedding guarantee on the admissible residual set. Thus unbounded oracle error, uncertified Ritz values, or unvalidated sketches invalidate deterministic feasibility claims.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Small computed residuals and nonnegative Ritz values are not certificates unless operator errors, omitted spectral directions, and sketch distortion are controlled.
assumptions_latex: \(M\in\mathbb S^n\) and \(q\in\mathbb R^n\) satisfies \(\|q\|_2=1\).
\(r\) and \(\widehat r\) denote exact and computed residuals in the same normed space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Deterministic certification requires explicit oracle-error bounds, certified spectral bounds, and any necessary sketch-embedding guarantee.

notation.meaning: computed Rayleigh quotient or Ritz value

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role is correct, and the individual cautions are mathematically plausible. Direct sources are still required for the combined deterministic-certification boundary.

knowledge_statements.title: Matrix-Free Preconditioning Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operator contract for preconditioning iterative SDP linear-system solves without forming the system matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H:\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R^m\) be the linear operator in an SDP Newton, Schur-complement, or normal-equation system. A matrix-free preconditioning interface provides a callable linear map \(z\mapsto P^{-1}z\) for a symmetric positive-definite operator \(P\), together with dimension, symmetry, definiteness, and application-accuracy metadata. The interface must apply \(P^{-1}\) without assembling \(H\); it may use structured solves, inner iterations, or low-rank formulas. For a requested tolerance \(\tau\), an inexact application returns \(w\) satisfying \(\|Pw-z\|_{P^{-1}}\leq\tau\|z\|_{P^{-1}}\). Krylov iteration then acts on the preconditioned operator \(P^{-1/2}HP^{-1/2}\), explicitly or through equivalent split applications.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The interface applies an SPD preconditioner and reports its accuracy while leaving the SDP system operator unassembled.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a callable symmetric linear operator on \(\mathbb R^m\).
\(P\) is symmetric positive definite.
The preconditioner application is exact or satisfies the declared inexactness condition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The interface defines a valid matrix-free application of \(P^{-1}\) for preconditioned Krylov execution.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the interface leaf, but the specific inexactness norm, metadata contract, and compatibility with Krylov execution require a source. Variable or nonlinear inexact applications may require flexible Krylov variants.

knowledge_statements.title: Lanczos Oracle Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Matrix-vector-product oracle for an extremal eigenpair of a symmetric SDP matrix operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a symmetric matrix operator \(v\mapsto Mv\), a unit vector \(q_1\), iteration limit \(k\), and tolerance \(\varepsilon\), set \(q_0=0\) and \(\beta_0=0\). For \(j=1,\ldots,k\), compute \(w=Mq_j-\beta_{j-1}q_{j-1}\), \(\alpha_j=q_j^\top w\), replace \(w\leftarrow w-\alpha_jq_j\), optionally reorthogonalize against prior basis vectors, set \(\beta_j=\|w\|_2\), and, if \(\beta_j>0\), set \(q_{j+1}=w/\beta_j\). Form the tridiagonal \(T_j\), extract an extremal Ritz pair \((\theta,z)\), and return \((\theta,Q_jz)\) when its Ritz residual is at most \(\varepsilon\), or after \(k\) iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lanczos builds a tridiagonal projection using only symmetric matrix-vector products and returns an extremal Ritz pair when its residual is small enough.
assumptions_latex: \(M\in\mathbb S^n\) is accessed through matrix-vector products.
\(q_1\in\mathbb R^n\) has unit norm.
Arithmetic is exact, or orthogonality loss is controlled by reorthogonalization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output \((\theta,u)\) satisfies \(\|u\|_2=1\) and has computable Ritz residual \(\|Mu-\theta u\|_2\).

notation.meaning: returned Ritz value and Ritz vector

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm is a recognizable Lanczos recurrence and fits the terminal container, but no inspectable source locator is supplied.

knowledge_statements.title: Block-Krylov Oracle Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Block matrix-product oracle for approximating an extremal invariant subspace of a symmetric operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(M\in\mathbb S^n\), a full-rank starting block \(\Omega\in\mathbb R^{n\times b}\), depth \(q\), and target rank \(r\leq b(q+1)\), construct the block Krylov space
\[\mathcal K_{q+1}(M,\Omega)=\operatorname{span}\{\Omega,M\Omega,\ldots,M^q\Omega\}.\]
Using stable block orthogonalization, form an orthonormal basis \(Q\) of this space. Compute the leading or trailing \(r\) eigenpairs \((\theta_i,z_i)\) of \(B=Q^\top MQ\), according to the requested spectral end, and return \((\theta_i,Qz_i)\). Stop early if every requested Ritz residual \(\|M(Qz_i)-\theta_iQz_i\|_2\) is at most the prescribed tolerance; otherwise return after depth \(q\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A block-Krylov oracle expands several starting directions together, projects the symmetric operator, and returns extremal Ritz vectors with explicit residuals.
assumptions_latex: \(M\) is symmetric and callable on vector blocks.
\(\Omega\) has at least one component in each desired invariant direction.
Block orthogonalization removes numerical rank deficiencies.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned vectors lie in \(\mathcal K_{q+1}(M,\Omega)\) and their eigenpair residuals are directly computable.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The block-Krylov construction and algorithm content kind fit the leaf. Its assumptions, rank handling, and stopping rule need an inspectable source.

knowledge_statements.title: Randomized Subspace Oracles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Random-start subspace iteration for approximate dominant eigenspaces using only block operator products.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(M\in\mathbb S^n\), target rank \(r\), oversampling \(p\geq0\), power count \(q\geq0\), and failure probability target \(\delta\), draw \(\Omega\in\mathbb R^{n\times(r+p)}\) from the declared random distribution. Compute \(Y=M^q\Omega\), orthonormalizing between products, and let \(Q=\operatorname{orth}(Y)\). Form \(B=Q^\top MQ\), compute the requested extremal Ritz pairs \((\theta_i,z_i)\), and return \((\theta_i,Qz_i)\), their residuals, the random seed, and a stated probabilistic error bound. The oracle accepts the result only when the residual test and the declared probability-bound assumptions both hold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The oracle uses random starting vectors and subspace iteration to obtain approximate extremal eigenvectors, returning residuals and a probabilistic error declaration.
assumptions_latex: \(M\) is symmetric and supports block products.
The distribution of \(\Omega\) and its random seed are recorded.
Any claimed failure probability follows from a stated spectral-error bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is a reproducible randomized Ritz approximation whose guarantee has declared failure probability at most \(\delta\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The claimed failure probability cannot be assessed without a specified sampling distribution and error theorem. Moreover, powers of a symmetric matrix naturally emphasize eigenvalues of largest magnitude, so the requested spectral end must be stated precisely.

knowledge_statements.title: Warm-Started Spectral Oracles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reuse of a previous approximate invariant subspace for a nearby sequence of symmetric SDP operators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For successive symmetric operators \(M_{t-1}\) and \(M_t\), the interface receives an orthonormal prior Ritz basis \(U_{t-1}\), optional fresh directions \(G_t\), a tolerance \(\varepsilon_t\), and an iteration budget \(k_t\). Initialize \(Q_0=\operatorname{orth}([U_{t-1},G_t])\), then apply a declared Lanczos, block-Krylov, or subspace-iteration update using products with \(M_t\). At each iteration, diagonalize \(Q_j^\top M_tQ_j\), compute the requested extremal Ritz residuals, and stop when they are all at most \(\varepsilon_t\). Return the Ritz pairs, residuals, and a flag recording whether fresh directions were used; otherwise return the best pairs at budget exhaustion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A warm-started oracle seeds the current spectral iteration with the preceding Ritz subspace, optionally augmented by fresh directions to detect eigenspace changes.
assumptions_latex: Each \(M_t\in\mathbb S^n\) is available through matrix-vector or block products.
\(U_{t-1}\) has orthonormal columns.
Fresh directions are supplied when retaining only the old subspace could conceal new extremal directions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The oracle returns current Ritz pairs with explicit residuals, but warm starting alone supplies no convergence guarantee without spectral-change assumptions.

knowledge_statements.title: Schur-Complement Krylov Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Matrix-free Krylov solution of the reduced multiplier system arising from an SDP Newton equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider the symmetric block system
\[\begin{pmatrix}H&A^*\\A&0\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}\Delta x\\\Delta y\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}r_x\\r_y\end{pmatrix},\]
where \(H\) is invertible. Define the Schur operator \(S=AH^{-1}A^*\) and right-hand side \(g=AH^{-1}r_x-r_y\). Apply conjugate gradients to \(S\Delta y=g\) when \(S\) is positive definite, or a symmetric-indefinite Krylov method when required, evaluating \(v\mapsto Sv\) as \(v\mapsto A(H^{-1}(A^*v))\). Stop when the preconditioned residual meets the prescribed tolerance, then recover \(\Delta x=H^{-1}(r_x-A^*\Delta y)\). No explicit Schur matrix is formed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Eliminate the primal Newton variable, solve the multiplier Schur system through nested operator applications, and recover the eliminated step afterward.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is invertible and its inverse action is available exactly or with controlled error.
\(A\) and \(A^*\) are callable.
The selected Krylov solver matches the symmetry and definiteness of \(S\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned \((\Delta x,\Delta y)\) approximately solves the block system with accuracy controlled by the Krylov and inner-solve residuals.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The block elimination signs are consistent and the algorithm fits the leaf. A source must state the SDP setting and conditions under which inexact inverse actions preserve the claimed outer-solve accuracy.

knowledge_statements.title: Normal-Equation Krylov Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Krylov execution on matrix-free least-squares normal equations with explicit conditioning caveat.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a callable linear operator \(J:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\), its adjoint \(J^*\), data \(d\in\mathbb R^m\), and regularization \(R\succeq0\), define \(N=J^*J+R\) and \(h=J^*d\). Apply preconditioned conjugate gradients to \(Nx=h\) when \(N\) is positive definite, evaluating \(v\mapsto Nv\) as \(J^*(Jv)+Rv\), and stop when the declared preconditioned-residual tolerance is met. If forming normal equations would cause unacceptable conditioning, apply LSQR or LSMR directly to the equivalent augmented least-squares operator instead. Return the iterate, the original residual \(Jx-d\), and the normal residual \(J^*(Jx-d)+Rx\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Normal-equation Krylov methods use forward and adjoint products, but should switch to an augmented least-squares iteration when squared conditioning is unsafe.
assumptions_latex: \(J\), \(J^*\), and \(R\) are callable linear operators.
\(N=J^*J+R\) is positive definite when conjugate gradients is used.
Stopping tests are evaluated in declared norms.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The method approximately solves \((J^*J+R)x=J^*d\) without assembling \(J\) or \(N\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The normal-equation operator is coherent, but an equivalent augmented least-squares formulation requires an available factorization or square root of the regularizer. The SDP-specific interpretation and conditioning guidance also need sources.

knowledge_statements.title: Low-Rank-Corrected Preconditioners
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Woodbury application of a structured base preconditioner plus a low-rank spectral correction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(P_0\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\), \(U\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}\), and \(D\in\mathbb S_{++}^r\), and define \(P=P_0+UDU^\top\). Then
\[P^{-1}=P_0^{-1}-P_0^{-1}U\bigl(D^{-1}+U^\top P_0^{-1}U\bigr)^{-1}U^\top P_0^{-1}.\]
Thus applying \(P^{-1}\) requires applications of \(P_0^{-1}\), products with \(U\) and \(U^\top\), and a solve with the \(r\times r\) matrix \(D^{-1}+U^\top P_0^{-1}U\). The correction is matrix-free with respect to the full system and is positive definite under the stated assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A low-rank update to an SPD base preconditioner can be inverted through base solves and one small dense Woodbury system.
assumptions_latex: \(P_0\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\).
\(D\in\mathbb S_{++}^r\).
Applications of \(P_0^{-1}\), \(U\), and \(U^\top\) are available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed Woodbury formula gives an SPD matrix-free preconditioner application for \(P=P_0+UDU^\top\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Woodbury representation is mathematically correct under the stated SPD assumptions and fits the low-rank-preconditioner leaf, but it has no cited source or locator.

knowledge_statements.title: Structure-Aware Preconditioners
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral-equivalence criterion for preconditioners that preserve exploitable decomposition in an SDP linear operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\) be a matrix-free SDP linear-system operator assembled conceptually from exploitable components, and let \(P\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\) be applicable using the same block, sparsity, chordal, Kronecker, or low-rank structure. If constants \(0<\alpha\leq\beta<\infty\) satisfy
\[\alpha P\preceq H\preceq\beta P,\]
then every eigenvalue of \(P^{-1/2}HP^{-1/2}\) lies in \([\alpha,\beta]\), and its spectral condition number is at most \(\beta/\alpha\). Consequently, preconditioned conjugate gradients attains the standard convergence bound governed by \(\sqrt{\beta/\alpha}\), while each iteration can retain the structured operator implementation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A structure-aware SPD preconditioner is effective when it is cheaply applicable through problem structure and spectrally equivalent to the system operator.
assumptions_latex: \(H,P\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\).
\(\alpha P\preceq H\preceq\beta P\) for finite positive constants \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\).
Applications of \(H\) and \(P^{-1}\) preserve the declared structure.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\kappa(P^{-1/2}HP^{-1/2})\leq\beta/\alpha\), so preconditioned Krylov convergence is controlled independently of representation details.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The spectral-equivalence implication is correct and the principle role fits the leaf. The referenced standard PCG convergence bound should be stated or cited precisely, and the listed SDP structure classes need direct support.

children.title: Range Sketches
children.top_down_role: Randomized state summaries targeting dominant column-space information.

knowledge_statements.title: Range Sketches
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Right-sided range sketch for a matrix-free square matrix state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) and let \(\Omega\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times k}\) be fixed independently of \(X\). The range sketch of \(X\) associated with \(\Omega\) is \[Y=X\Omega\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times k}.\] It stores the action of \(X\) on the test subspace \(\operatorname{range}(\Omega)\). If \(\operatorname{range}(X)\subseteq\operatorname{range}(Y)\), then an orthonormal basis obtained from \(Y\) spans the column space of \(X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A range sketch stores matrix products with a small test matrix and can reveal the matrix column space when sufficiently informative.
assumptions_latex: \(X\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\)
\(\Omega\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times k}\) is fixed independently of \(X\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Y=X\Omega\) is the range sketch of \(X\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition and conditional column-space statement are mathematically consistent and fit the Range Sketches leaf, but no citation or inspectable locator supports the terminology or claim.

children.title: Co-Range Sketches
children.top_down_role: Randomized state summaries targeting complementary row-side information.

knowledge_statements.title: Co-Range Sketches
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Left-sided sketch complementing a range sketch.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) and let \(\Psi\in\mathbb{R}^{\ell\times n}\) be fixed independently of \(X\). The co-range sketch of \(X\) associated with \(\Psi\) is \[W=\Psi X\in\mathbb{R}^{\ell\times n}.\] It records measurements of the rows of \(X\). For any matrix \(Q\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times r}\) whose columns span \(\operatorname{range}(X)\), the sketch determines the coefficient matrix in \(X=QB\) whenever \(\Psi Q\) has full column rank, because \(B=(\Psi Q)^{\dagger}W\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A co-range sketch stores left measurements and recovers coordinates relative to a known column-space basis when the sampled basis is injective.
assumptions_latex: \(X\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\)
\(\Psi\in\mathbb{R}^{\ell\times n}\) is fixed independently of \(X\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(W=\Psi X\) is the co-range sketch of \(X\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The co-range definition and coefficient-recovery condition are algebraically sound and appropriately classified, but the record has no supporting citation with a specific locator.

children.title: Two-Sided Sketch Coverage
children.top_down_role: Coverage, redundancy, and reconstruction value obtained from paired sketch orientations.

knowledge_statements.title: Two-Sided Sketch Coverage
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact coverage criterion for a two-sided sketch pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Y=X\Omega\) and \(W=\Psi X\), where \(X\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\). Let \(Q\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times r}\) have orthonormal columns and satisfy \(\operatorname{range}(Q)=\operatorname{range}(Y)=\operatorname{range}(X)\). If \(\Psi Q\) has full column rank, then the pair \((Y,W)\) covers both the column space and its coefficient representation, and \[X=Q(\Psi Q)^{\dagger}W.\] Thus exact reconstruction follows whenever the range sketch spans \(\operatorname{range}(X)\) and the co-range map is injective on that subspace.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The two sketches determine the matrix exactly when one captures its column space and the other is injective on that space.
assumptions_latex: \(\operatorname{range}(Y)=\operatorname{range}(X)=\operatorname{range}(Q)\)
\(Q^{\mathsf T}Q=I_r\)
\(\operatorname{rank}(\Psi Q)=r\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X=Q(\Psi Q)^{\dagger}W\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The reconstruction identity is valid under the stated range and full-rank conditions, but the domains and dimensions of Omega and Psi are not explicitly introduced and no two-sided-sketch source is cited.

knowledge_statements.title: PSD-Aware Sketches
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nyström representation preserving positive semidefiniteness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\in\mathbb{S}_+^n\) and \(\Omega\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times k}\). Form \(Y=X\Omega\) and the symmetric core \(G=\Omega^{\mathsf T}Y=\Omega^{\mathsf T}X\Omega\). The PSD-aware Nyström reconstruction is \[\widehat X=YG^{\dagger}Y^{\mathsf T}.\] Since \(G\succeq0\), its pseudoinverse satisfies \(G^{\dagger}\succeq0\); hence \(\widehat X\succeq0\) and \(\operatorname{rank}(\widehat X)\leq k\). This sketch couples the range sample with a small PSD Gram matrix rather than treating the two matrix sides independently.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A range sample plus its small Gram matrix yields a Nyström approximation that remains positive semidefinite and has rank at most the sketch size.
assumptions_latex: \(X\in\mathbb{S}_+^n\)
\(\Omega\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times k}\)
\(Y=X\Omega\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat X=Y(\Omega^{\mathsf T}Y)^{\dagger}Y^{\mathsf T}\succeq0\) and \(\operatorname{rank}(\widehat X)\leq k\).

notation.meaning: cone of real symmetric positive semidefinite matrices

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Nyström representation is PSD and has rank at most k as claimed, and representation is an appropriate knowledge kind, but no authoritative randomized or PSD-sketching source is supplied.

knowledge_statements.title: Measurement-Space State Storage
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compressed storage of SDP iterates through linear measurements and sketches.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal A:\mathbb S^n\to\mathbb R^m\) be linear, and fix test matrices \(\Omega\in\mathbb R^{n\times k}\) and \(\Psi\in\mathbb R^{\ell\times n}\). A measurement-space representation of \(X\in\mathbb S^n\) is \[s(X)=\bigl(\mathcal A(X),X\Omega,\Psi X\bigr).\] For every update \(\Delta X\in\mathbb S^n\), linearity gives \[s(X+\Delta X)=s(X)+\bigl(\mathcal A(\Delta X),\Delta X\Omega,\Psi\Delta X\bigr).\] Hence feasibility measurements and reconstruction sketches can be maintained without storing the dense matrix \(X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Store constraint measurements and two sketches instead of the dense SDP iterate; every component updates linearly under matrix increments.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal A:\mathbb S^n\to\mathbb R^m\) is linear
\(X,\Delta X\in\mathbb S^n\)
\(\Omega\) and \(\Psi\) are fixed
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(s(X+\Delta X)=s(X)+s(\Delta X)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stored state and its linear update identity are precise and fit the representation container, but the matrix-free SDP storage interpretation lacks a direct cited source and locator.

knowledge_statements.title: Streaming Sketch Maintenance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Online maintenance of fixed linear sketches under streamed updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given fixed \(\Omega\), \(\Psi\), and a linear map \(\mathcal A\), initialize \(b_0=\mathcal A(X_0)\), \(Y_0=X_0\Omega\), and \(W_0=\Psi X_0\). When update \(\Delta X_t\) arrives, compute it once and set \[b_{t+1}=b_t+\mathcal A(\Delta X_t),\qquad Y_{t+1}=Y_t+\Delta X_t\Omega,\qquad W_{t+1}=W_t+\Psi\Delta X_t.\] After the stream, output \((b_T,Y_T,W_T)\). In exact arithmetic these values equal \((\mathcal A(X_T),X_T\Omega,\Psi X_T)\), where \(X_T=X_0+\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}\Delta X_t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Process each update once, adding its measurements and left and right sketch contributions to the maintained compressed state.
assumptions_latex: \(X_T=X_0+\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}\Delta X_t\)
\(\mathcal A\) is linear
\(\Omega\) and \(\Psi\) remain fixed
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((b_T,Y_T,W_T)=(\mathcal A(X_T),X_T\Omega,\Psi X_T)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The streaming recurrence is algebraically correct and algorithm is the proper content kind, but the dimensions of the fixed sketch matrices and update states are not fully specified and no streaming-sketch source is cited.

knowledge_statements.title: Rank-One Atomic Updates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact sketch updates for a single rank-one matrix atom.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the current matrix receive the rank-one update \(X^+=X+\alpha uv^{\mathsf T}\), with \(u,v\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(\alpha\in\mathbb R\). For sketches \(Y=X\Omega\) and \(W=\Psi X\), the updated sketches are \[Y^+=Y+\alpha u(v^{\mathsf T}\Omega),\qquad W^+=W+\alpha(\Psi u)v^{\mathsf T}.\] Both increments are rank at most one and require only multiplication of the atom factors by the fixed test matrices. If symmetry is required, choosing \(v=u\) preserves symmetry; choosing \(\alpha\geq0\) also preserves positive semidefiniteness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rank-one matrix update induces rank-one updates of both sketches using only the atom factors and fixed test matrices.
assumptions_latex: \(X^+=X+\alpha uv^{\mathsf T}\)
\(Y=X\Omega\)
\(W=\Psi X\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Y^+=Y+\alpha u(v^{\mathsf T}\Omega)\) and \(W^+=W+\alpha(\Psi u)v^{\mathsf T}\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The rank-one sketch-update formulas are correct. However, the assertion that alpha at least zero preserves positive semidefiniteness additionally requires the current X to be PSD (and v=u); no direct source is supplied to resolve and support the complete formulation.

knowledge_statements.title: Low-Rank Block Updates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact sketch propagation for factored low-rank matrix updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X^+=X+UCV^{\mathsf T}\), where \(U,V\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}\) and \(C\in\mathbb R^{r\times r}\). If \(Y=X\Omega\) and \(W=\Psi X\), then \[Y^+=Y+UC(V^{\mathsf T}\Omega),\qquad W^+=W+(\Psi U)CV^{\mathsf T}.\] These formulas update the sketches from the factors without forming the dense increment \(UCV^{\mathsf T}\). For a symmetric update take \(V=U\) and \(C=C^{\mathsf T}\); if additionally \(C\succeq0\), the update is positive semidefinite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A factored rank-block update propagates directly to both sketches without forming the corresponding dense matrix.
assumptions_latex: \(X^+=X+UCV^{\mathsf T}\)
\(U,V\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}\)
\(Y=X\Omega\) and \(W=\Psi X\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Y^+=Y+UC(V^{\mathsf T}\Omega)\) and \(W^+=W+(\Psi U)CV^{\mathsf T}\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The low-rank propagation formulas are correct and fit a property leaf. The last sentence should distinguish that UCU^T is a PSD increment when C is PSD from preservation of PSD by X plus that increment, which also assumes X is PSD; no direct source is cited.

knowledge_statements.title: Single-Pass Sketch Updates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-pass processing of factored low-rank updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(\Omega\) and \(\Psi\), and initialize \(Y=X_0\Omega\) and \(W=\Psi X_0\). For each streamed factorization \(\Delta X_t=U_tC_tV_t^{\mathsf T}\), form \(R_t=V_t^{\mathsf T}\Omega\) and \(L_t=\Psi U_t\) during its sole access, then update \[Y\leftarrow Y+U_tC_tR_t,\qquad W\leftarrow W+L_tC_tV_t^{\mathsf T}.\] Discard the factors afterward. After all updates, output \((Y,W)\); in exact arithmetic it equals \((X_T\Omega,\Psi X_T)\) for \(X_T=X_0+\sum_t\Delta X_t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each low-rank update is read once, compressed immediately against both test matrices, and then discarded while preserving the final sketches.
assumptions_latex: \(\Delta X_t=U_tC_tV_t^{\mathsf T}\)
\(X_T=X_0+\sum_t\Delta X_t\)
\(\Omega\) and \(\Psi\) remain fixed
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((Y,W)=(X_T\Omega,\Psi X_T)\) after one pass over the updates.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The one-pass update algorithm and exact-arithmetic invariant are consistent, but factor and sketch dimensions are not explicitly introduced and the record provides no cited single-pass sketching source.

knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Rank Reconstruction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-sided reconstruction at a prescribed output rank.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(Y=X\Omega\), \(W=\Psi X\), and a target rank \(r\), compute an orthonormal basis \(Q=\operatorname{orth}(Y)\). Form \(B=(\Psi Q)^{\dagger}W\), compute a best rank-\(r\) approximation \([B]_r\) in Frobenius norm, and output \[\widehat X_r=Q[B]_r.\] If \(Q\) has orthonormal columns, then \(\operatorname{rank}(\widehat X_r)\leq r\). When \(\operatorname{range}(X)\subseteq\operatorname{range}(Q)\), \(\Psi Q\) has full column rank, and \(\operatorname{rank}(X)\leq r\), the output equals \(X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Build a basis from the range sketch, recover its coefficients from the co-range sketch, truncate to the prescribed rank, and multiply.
assumptions_latex: \(Y=X\Omega\) and \(W=\Psi X\)
\(Q=\operatorname{orth}(Y)\)
\(1\leq r\leq\operatorname{rank}(Q)\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat X_r=Q[(\Psi Q)^{\dagger}W]_r\) and \(\operatorname{rank}(\widehat X_r)\leq r\).

notation.meaning: best rank-r approximation from a truncated singular-value decomposition
orthonormal basis extracted from the range sketch

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The fixed-rank reconstruction algorithm and exact-recovery conditions are mathematically consistent and appropriately classified, but no authoritative two-sided reconstruction source with a locator is supplied.

knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive-Rank Reconstruction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tolerance-driven rank selection within a sketched reconstruction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given sketches \(Y=X\Omega\), \(W=\Psi X\), and tolerance \(\varepsilon\geq0\), set \(Q=\operatorname{orth}(Y)\) and \(B=(\Psi Q)^{\dagger}W\). Let \(B=U\operatorname{diag}(\sigma_1,\ldots,\sigma_p)V^{\mathsf T}\), with \(\sigma_1\geq\cdots\geq\sigma_p\geq0\). Choose the smallest \(r\in\{0,\ldots,p\}\) satisfying \[\left(\sum_{j=r+1}^{p}\sigma_j^2\right)^{1/2}\leq\varepsilon,\] and output \(\widehat X=QU_r\operatorname{diag}(\sigma_1,\ldots,\sigma_r)V_r^{\mathsf T}\). Then \(\operatorname{rank}(\widehat X)\leq r\) and \(\|QB-\widehat X\|_F\leq\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Recover the small coefficient matrix, select the smallest singular-value truncation meeting a tolerance, and lift that adaptive-rank approximation.
assumptions_latex: \(Y=X\Omega\) and \(W=\Psi X\)
\(Q=\operatorname{orth}(Y)\)
\(\varepsilon\geq0\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{rank}(\widehat X)\leq r\) and \(\|QB-\widehat X\|_F\leq\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: ordered singular values of the recovered coefficient matrix
smallest selected rank meeting the tolerance

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The tolerance-driven truncated-SVD construction is sound, but p and the precise SVD convention are not defined, and no adaptive-rank reconstruction source is cited.

knowledge_statements.title: PSD Reconstruction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive-semidefinite reconstruction from a PSD-aware range sketch.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(Y=X\Omega\) for an implicit \(X\in\mathbb S_+^n\), form \(G=\Omega^{\mathsf T}Y\), symmetrize it as \(G_s=(G+G^{\mathsf T})/2\), and compute its positive spectral part \(G_+\). Output \[\widehat X=YG_+^{\dagger}Y^{\mathsf T}.\] Optionally truncate the eigendecomposition of \(\widehat X\) to a prescribed rank by retaining only its largest nonnegative eigenvalues. Because \(G_+^{\dagger}\succeq0\), the reconstructed matrix satisfies \(\widehat X\succeq0\), even when numerical asymmetry or small negative eigenvalues occur in the computed core.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Symmetrize and project the small core onto the PSD cone, then apply a Nyström reconstruction to guarantee a PSD output.
assumptions_latex: \(Y=X\Omega\) with \(X\in\mathbb S_+^n\)
\(G_s=(\Omega^{\mathsf T}Y+Y^{\mathsf T}\Omega)/2\)
\(G_+\) is the positive spectral part of \(G_s\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat X=YG_+^{\dagger}Y^{\mathsf T}\succeq0\).

notation.meaning: projection of the core onto the PSD cone

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stated construction always produces a PSD matrix because the pseudoinverse of G_+ is PSD, and algorithm is the correct kind. However, the discussion of numerical asymmetry and negative eigenvalues introduces a finite-precision regime without specifying its model, and no direct PSD-reconstruction source is cited.

children.title: Streaming Reconstruction Regimes
children.top_down_role: Reconstruction settings with continuously arriving or incrementally retained sketch information.

knowledge_statements.title: Streaming Reconstruction Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines matrix reconstruction when updates arrive sequentially and retained state is memory-limited.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A=\sum_{t=1}^{T}\Delta_t\in\mathbb S^n\), where the updates \(\Delta_t\) arrive in order. A streaming reconstruction regime with memory budget \(M\) consists of states \(s_t\in\mathbb R^M\), update maps \(s_t=U_t(s_{t-1},\Delta_t)\), and an output map \(\widehat A=R(s_T)\). After processing \(\Delta_t\), the algorithm may retain only \(s_t\), fixed randomness, and metadata counted within \(M\); access to earlier updates is unavailable unless explicitly included in the pass model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A streaming regime updates a bounded-memory state from sequential matrix increments and reconstructs a matrix from the final retained state.
assumptions_latex: \(A,\Delta_t\in\mathbb S^n\) for \(t=1,\ldots,T\).
The stream order and memory budget \(M\) are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat A=R(s_T)\) is determined solely by the terminal state and retained randomness.
review_flags: Exact sketch-based SDP streaming convention lacks a directly relevant supplied source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is mathematically coherent and fits the streaming-regime leaf, but no cited source supports the precise memory, randomness, metadata, and pass-model conventions.

children.title: Single-Pass Reconstruction Regimes
children.top_down_role: Reconstruction settings limited to one traversal of the source data.

knowledge_statements.title: Single-Pass Reconstruction Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Specifies the one-pass restriction for a streaming matrix reconstruction procedure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A streaming reconstruction procedure is single-pass if every update \(\Delta_t\) is presented exactly once, the state transition \(s_t=U_t(s_{t-1},\Delta_t)\) is completed before \(\Delta_{t+1}\) arrives, and neither reconstruction nor later transitions query any discarded update. Thus the output has the form \(\widehat A=R(s_T)\). Randomized procedures may retain a seed chosen before the stream, but may not use that seed to obtain a second evaluation of any \(\Delta_t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A regime is single-pass when each update is read once and all later computation uses only the retained state and fixed randomness.
assumptions_latex: The updates \((\Delta_t)_{t=1}^{T}\) form a nonrevisitable ordered stream.
All retained information is represented by \(s_t\) and fixed randomness.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each \(\Delta_t\) is accessed once and \(\widehat A=R(s_T)\).

notation.meaning: state transition at stream position t

review_flags: No supplied locator addresses single-pass randomized matrix reconstruction.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition correctly distinguishes a single-pass regime, but the exact nonrevisitation and randomized-seed conventions lack a supporting citation.

children.title: Incremental Sketch Retention
children.top_down_role: Retention choices for sketch state during nonrevisitable data streams.

knowledge_statements.title: Incremental Sketch Retention
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Maintains linear left and right sketches under additive symmetric-matrix updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input additive updates \(\Delta_t\in\mathbb S^n\), fixed test matrices \(\Omega\in\mathbb R^{n\times k}\) and \(\Psi\in\mathbb R^{\ell\times n}\), and initialize \(Y_0=0\), \(W_0=0\). For \(t=1,\ldots,T\), update \(Y_t=Y_{t-1}+\Delta_t\Omega\) and \(W_t=W_{t-1}+\Psi\Delta_t\), then discard \(\Delta_t\). After the stream, output the retained pair \((Y_T,W_T)=(A\Omega,\Psi A)\), or apply a specified reconstruction map \(R\) to obtain \(\widehat A=R(Y_T,W_T)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Linear sketches are retained incrementally by adding each update’s left and right sketch contributions, without storing the matrix updates.
assumptions_latex: \(A=\sum_{t=1}^{T}\Delta_t\).
The test matrices \(\Omega\) and \(\Psi\) remain fixed throughout the stream.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Y_T=A\Omega\) and \(W_T=\Psi A\).
review_flags: The algebraic update rule is unambiguous, but no supplied source supports this sketch family.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The incremental sketch algorithm and its dimensional identities are correct, but no source supports this particular two-sided sketch-retention construction in the stated SDP context.

children.title: Pass-Budget Accuracy Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Accuracy consequences associated with restricted traversal budgets.

knowledge_statements.title: Pass-Budget Accuracy Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relates additional data passes to adaptive sketch refinement and reconstruction error.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a fixed reconstruction class and memory budget, define \(E_p(A)=\inf_{\mathcal M_p}\mathbb E\lVert A-\widehat A_{\mathcal M_p}\rVert\), where \(\mathcal M_p\) ranges over admissible algorithms using at most \(p\) complete passes over the same data and the expectation covers internal randomness. Because a \(p\)-pass algorithm is admissible in the \((p+1)\)-pass class by ignoring the extra pass, \(E_{p+1}(A)\le E_p(A)\). Strict improvement is problem-dependent and requires the later pass to exploit information unavailable when the earlier sketch was fixed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optimal reconstruction error cannot worsen when another pass is permitted, although strict improvement depends on whether later passes enable useful adaptation.
assumptions_latex: The admissible algorithm classes are nested as the pass budget increases.
The norm, memory budget, input class, and randomness convention are held fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(E_{p+1}(A)\le E_p(A)\) for every admissible \(A\).

notation.meaning: best expected error attainable with at most p passes

review_flags: This monotonicity principle is definitional; quantitative tradeoffs require a specified reconstruction theorem and source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The monotonicity statement follows from the declared nesting of admissible pass classes and fits the tradeoff leaf, but the reconstruction model and claimed interpretation of strict improvement are uncited.

children.title: Nonrevisitable-Data Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Failure regimes caused by unavailable replay, insufficient retained state, or irreversible information loss.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonrevisitable-Data Failure Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identifies indistinguishability as the fundamental obstruction under nonrevisitable data.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a deterministic one-pass algorithm retain the state \(s(A)\) and output \(R(s(A))\). If two admissible inputs \(A_0,A_1\in\mathbb S^n\) produce the same terminal state, then their reconstructions coincide. Consequently, for any norm, \[\max_{i\in\{0,1\}}\lVert A_i-R(s(A_i))\rVert\ge \tfrac12\lVert A_0-A_1\rVert.\] Thus uniform error below half their separation is impossible without retaining information that distinguishes the inputs or revisiting the discarded data. The same conclusion holds conditionally for randomized algorithms whenever a fixed random seed yields the collision.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If two nonrevisitable inputs leave the same retained state, one common output must incur at least half their mutual distance on one input.
assumptions_latex: The output depends only on the terminal retained state.
Two admissible inputs satisfy \(s(A_0)=s(A_1)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\max_i\lVert A_i-R(s(A_i))\rVert\ge \frac12\lVert A_0-A_1\rVert\).

notation.meaning: terminal state produced from input A

review_flags: A directly relevant streaming lower-bound source is absent from the supplied inventory.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The deterministic collision lower bound is mathematically correct, and the randomized qualification is appropriately conditional, but a relevant streaming lower-bound source is required.

knowledge_statements.title: Storage-Optimality Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines storage optimality relative to a reconstruction task and accuracy criterion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix an input class \(\mathcal A\), error tolerance \(\varepsilon\), success probability \(1-\delta\), and computational model. Let \(M^*(\mathcal A,\varepsilon,\delta)\) be the infimum, over all admissible reconstruction algorithms, of the worst-case number of stored machine words needed to output \(\widehat A\) satisfying \(\Pr\{d(A,\widehat A)\le\varepsilon\}\ge 1-\delta\) for every \(A\in\mathcal A\). An algorithm family is storage-optimal up to factor \(c\) if its storage \(M\) obeys \(M\le cM^*(\mathcal A,\varepsilon,\delta)\) uniformly over the declared parameter range.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A reconstruction family is storage-optimal up to factor c when its memory is at most c times the least worst-case memory possible under the same input class, error criterion, success probability, and computational model.
assumptions_latex: The storage unit and computational model are fixed.
The distance \(d\), input class \(\mathcal A\), and guarantee are specified.
The approximation factor satisfies \(c\ge 1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M\le cM^*(\mathcal A,\varepsilon,\delta)\) defines factor-\(c\) storage optimality.
review_flags: The applicable machine-word and computational model needs a dedicated source.

knowledge_statements.title: Reconstruction-Accuracy Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Organizes reconstruction guarantees by error metric, comparator, and probability level.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a matrix class \(\mathcal A\), an approximation class \(\mathcal C_r\), a norm \(\lVert\cdot\rVert\), and failure probability \(\delta\in[0,1]\). A reconstruction algorithm belongs to the \((\alpha,\beta,\delta)\)-accuracy family if, for every \(A\in\mathcal A\), its output \(\widehat A\) satisfies \[\Pr\!\left\{\lVert A-\widehat A\rVert\le \alpha\inf_{B\in\mathcal C_r}\lVert A-B\rVert+\beta\right\}\ge 1-\delta.\] Here \(\alpha\ge 1\) is the relative-error factor and \(\beta\ge 0\) is the additive error allowance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An accuracy family groups reconstruction algorithms by a relative and additive error guarantee against the best matrix in a declared comparison class, together with a declared failure probability.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal A\) and \(\mathcal C_r\) are fixed matrix classes in the domain of the norm.
The norm and probability convention are fixed.
\(\alpha\ge 1\), \(\beta\ge 0\), and \(\delta\in[0,1]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed probability inequality defines membership in the \((\alpha,\beta,\delta)\)-accuracy family.
review_flags: No supplied source specifies the intended sketch-reconstruction norm or comparator family.

children.title: Operator-Application Cost Accounting
children.top_down_role: Computational cost attributable to implicit linear-operator evaluations.

knowledge_statements.title: Operator-Application Cost Accounting
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Represents the cost of applications of linear SDP operators and their adjoints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal A:\mathbb S^n\to\mathbb R^m\) be the SDP constraint operator and \(\mathcal A^*:\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb S^n\) its adjoint. If iteration \(t\) makes \(q_t\) calls to \(\mathcal A\) and \(q_t^*\) calls to \(\mathcal A^*\), then after \(T\) iterations the operator-call count is \(N_{\mathrm{op}}=\sum_{t=1}^{T}(q_t+q_t^*)\). Under fixed per-call costs \(c_{\mathcal A}\) and \(c_{\mathcal A^*}\), the corresponding arithmetic or communication cost is \(C_{\mathrm{op}}=\sum_{t=1}^{T}(q_tc_{\mathcal A}+q_t^*c_{\mathcal A^*})\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Total operator cost is represented by the sum of all forward-operator and adjoint-operator calls, weighted by their respective per-call costs.
assumptions_latex: Each call is charged according to a fixed declared cost model.
Calls made inside subordinate routines are included.
\(q_t,q_t^*\in\mathbb Z_{\ge 0}\) for \(t=1,\ldots,T\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N_{\mathrm{op}}=\sum_{t=1}^{T}(q_t+q_t^*)\) and \(C_{\mathrm{op}}=\sum_{t=1}^{T}(q_tc_{\mathcal A}+q_t^*c_{\mathcal A^*})\).

notation.meaning: adjoint of the SDP constraint operator
forward and adjoint call counts at iteration t

review_flags: A source for the intended matrix-free SDP oracle model is required.

children.title: Eigen-Oracle Cost Accounting
children.top_down_role: Computational cost attributable to extreme-eigenvalue or eigenspace queries.

knowledge_statements.title: Eigen-Oracle Cost Accounting
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Represents approximate extremal-eigenpair cost through the eigensolver's internal matrix-vector products.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose iteration \(t\) requests an extremal eigenpair of a symmetric matrix operator \(H_t\) to residual tolerance \(\eta_t\). Let \(k_t(\eta_t)\) be the number of products \(v\mapsto H_tv\) used by the eigensolver and let \(c_{H_t}\) be the cost per product. For \(T\) outer iterations, the eigen-oracle work is \(N_{\mathrm{eig}}=\sum_{t=1}^{T}k_t(\eta_t)\) matrix-vector products and \(C_{\mathrm{eig}}=\sum_{t=1}^{T}k_t(\eta_t)c_{H_t}\). Orthogonalization and vector-storage costs must be reported separately when non-negligible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Eigen-oracle work is represented by the matrix-vector products used at each requested residual tolerance, with non-negligible orthogonalization and storage costs reported separately.
assumptions_latex: Each \(H_t\) is symmetric and accessed through matrix-vector products.
The stopping rule certifies the declared residual tolerance \(\eta_t\).
\(k_t(\eta_t)\in\mathbb Z_{\ge 0}\) for \(t=1,\ldots,T\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N_{\mathrm{eig}}=\sum_{t=1}^{T}k_t(\eta_t)\) and \(C_{\mathrm{eig}}=\sum_{t=1}^{T}k_t(\eta_t)c_{H_t}\), excluding separately itemized overhead.

children.title: Cross-Oracle Cost Coupling
children.top_down_role: Interactions between operator evaluation expense and spectral-query expense.

knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Oracle Cost Coupling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Prevents double counting when eigen-operator products invoke SDP operators internally.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose an eigen-oracle product has the composite form \(H_tv=C_tv+\mathcal A^*(D_t\mathcal A(V_t(v)))\), where \(C_t,D_t,V_t\) are locally available maps. If one product with \(H_t\) invokes \(a_t\) calls to \(\mathcal A\) and \(b_t\) calls to \(\mathcal A^*\), then \(k_t\) eigen iterations induce \(a_tk_t\) forward and \(b_tk_t\) adjoint calls. Hence operator and eigen costs are coupled; a disjoint accounting must charge either the composite products or their expanded operator calls, but not both.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When each eigen iteration calls the SDP operator and adjoint, eigen and operator costs must be expanded consistently to avoid double counting.
assumptions_latex: The implementation of \(v\mapsto H_tv\) is fixed and exposes its nested oracle calls.
The same nested calls are not independently charged twice.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The induced counts are \(a_tk_t\) calls to \(\mathcal A\) and \(b_tk_t\) calls to \(\mathcal A^*\).

notation.meaning: composite operator used by the eigen oracle
nested forward and adjoint calls per composite product
composite products used at iteration t

children.title: Accuracy-Driven Oracle Cost
children.top_down_role: Resource growth associated with increasingly accurate oracle outputs.

knowledge_statements.title: Accuracy-Driven Oracle Cost
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Composes outer iteration complexity with the tolerance-dependent cost of inexact eigen calls.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let an SDP method require \(T(\varepsilon)\) outer iterations to return an \(\varepsilon\)-accurate solution when iteration \(t\) uses an eigen-oracle tolerance \(\eta_t(\varepsilon)\). If that call requires at most \(K_t(\eta_t)\) matrix-vector products, then the total eigen-oracle count satisfies \[N_{\mathrm{eig}}(\varepsilon)\le\sum_{t=1}^{T(\varepsilon)}K_t(\eta_t(\varepsilon)).\] Any valid end-to-end bound must choose the tolerances so that accumulated inexactness remains within the outer method's error budget; replacing \(K_t\) by an exact-oracle unit cost is valid only when exact calls are the declared model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: End-to-end oracle cost composes the outer iteration bound with the cost of meeting each accuracy-dependent inner eigen tolerance.
assumptions_latex: The outer convergence guarantee specifies admissible inner tolerances.
\(K_t(\eta)\) upper-bounds the work needed to attain tolerance \(\eta\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N_{\mathrm{eig}}(\varepsilon)\le\sum_{t=1}^{T(\varepsilon)}K_t(\eta_t(\varepsilon))\).

notation.meaning: outer iterations required for target accuracy
inner tolerance scheduled at iteration t

review_flags: Quantitative specialization requires an outer convergence theorem and an eigensolver bound.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The conditional composition bound is correctly stated and fits the complexity-bound leaf, but its applicability depends on an outer convergence theorem, admissible inner-tolerance schedule, and eigensolver work bound that are not cited.

children.title: Dominant Oracle-Cost Regimes
children.top_down_role: Problem regimes in which one oracle resource controls overall execution cost.

knowledge_statements.title: Dominant Oracle-Cost Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classifies which oracle contribution controls total matrix-free SDP work.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C_{\mathrm{op}},C_{\mathrm{eig}},C_{\mathrm{sk}}\ge0\) denote disjointly accounted operator, eigen-oracle, and sketch-maintenance costs, and set \(C_{\mathrm{tot}}=C_{\mathrm{op}}+C_{\mathrm{eig}}+C_{\mathrm{sk}}\). For a constant \(\gamma>1\), the operator-dominant regime is defined by \(C_{\mathrm{op}}\ge\gamma(C_{\mathrm{eig}}+C_{\mathrm{sk}})\); eigen dominance and sketch dominance are defined by cyclic permutation. If none holds, the computation is a mixed-cost regime. In an operator-dominant regime, \(C_{\mathrm{op}}\le C_{\mathrm{tot}}\le(1+\gamma^{-1})C_{\mathrm{op}}\), with analogous bounds for the other regimes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cost component is dominant when it exceeds the sum of the others by a declared factor; otherwise the computation has mixed costs.
assumptions_latex: All cost terms use a common unit and form a disjoint accounting.
The dominance factor satisfies \(\gamma>1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Operator dominance implies \(C_{\mathrm{op}}\le C_{\mathrm{tot}}\le(1+\gamma^{-1})C_{\mathrm{op}}\), with cyclic analogues.
review_flags: The dominance threshold is a local formal convention rather than a sourced standard.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The dominance definition and resulting inequality are correct under disjoint common-unit accounting, but the threshold convention is local and has no cited source.

children.title: Working-Memory Footprint
children.top_down_role: Transient storage required during sketching, oracle evaluation, or reconstruction.

knowledge_statements.title: Working-Memory Footprint
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Peak storage for a matrix-free SDP method maintaining a rank-sketch and distributed oracle state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\in\mathbb S_+^n\) be represented only through \(Y=X\Omega\in\mathbb R^{n\times k}\), where \(\Omega\in\mathbb R^{n\times k}\), and let the optimization state contain \(m\) scalar dual variables. If matrix-oracle products are streamed and no dense \(n\times n\) matrix is materialized, storing \(Y\), \(\Omega\), the dual state, and \(O(n+k)\) work vectors requires \(O(nk+m)\) words. With row-wise distribution across \(p\) workers and replicated dual variables, the corresponding peak local storage is \(O(nk/p+m+n/p+k)\) words, excluding storage intrinsic to the supplied linear operators.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A streamed rank-k sketch uses O(nk+m) total words, or O(nk/p+m+n/p+k) per worker under row distribution, apart from operator storage.
assumptions_latex: \(1\le k\le n\) and \(p\ge1\).
Matrix-oracle products are streamed without materializing dense \(n\times n\) matrices.
Sketch rows are balanced across workers; dual variables are replicated.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M_{\mathrm{total}}=O(nk+m)\) and \(M_{\mathrm{local}}=O(nk/p+m+n/p+k)\).
review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports this sketch-specific storage model.
Complexity depends on whether the test matrix and dual state are stored or regenerated.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound role and conditional storage accounting fit the leaf, but no inspectable source supports the sketch-storage model or its distribution assumptions.

children.title: Communication Volume
children.top_down_role: Data movement required across workers, devices, or storage boundaries.

knowledge_statements.title: Communication Volume
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Word communication for distributed matrix-free sketch updates under row partitioning.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(p\) workers hold balanced row partitions of \(Y\in\mathbb R^{n\times k}\). In each of \(T\) iterations, assume the only collective operations reduce one \(k\times k\) Gram matrix and one vector in \(\mathbb R^m\); all operator products otherwise use local data. Counting aggregate words injected into a tree reduction, the communicated volume is \(O(T(p-1)(k^2+m))\). Counting words on the critical path instead gives \(O(T(k^2+m)\log p)\). A final gathering of the distributed sketch adds \(O(nk)\) aggregate words when reconstruction occurs on one worker.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: T iterations communicate reductions of k²+m scalars; centralized final reconstruction additionally gathers nk sketch entries.
assumptions_latex: The sketch is row-partitioned over \(p\) workers.
Each iteration performs exactly the stated two collective reductions.
Communication is measured in scalar words.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(V_{\mathrm{aggregate}}=O(T(p-1)(k^2+m)+nk)\), with the \(nk\) term omitted for distributed reconstruction.
review_flags: No supplied source specifies this distributed communication model.
The bound is conditional on the stated collective schedule.

children.title: Synchronization Frequency
children.top_down_role: Coordination burden arising from collective or repeated execution barriers.

knowledge_statements.title: Synchronization Frequency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global synchronization count induced by collective sketch-oracle reductions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(T\) distributed iterations, each requiring \(q\) logically sequential collective reductions, followed optionally by one collective reconstruction. If reductions within an iteration cannot be fused because the input to reduction \(j+1\) depends on the result of reduction \(j\), then the execution requires exactly \(qT\) optimization synchronization rounds and at most one additional reconstruction round. If all \(q\) reduction payloads are available simultaneously, packing them into one collective reduces the optimization count to \(T\) rounds without changing their total payload size asymptotically.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sequential collectives require qT synchronization rounds; simultaneously available payloads can be fused to one round per iteration.
assumptions_latex: There are \(T\) iterations and \(q\) prescribed collectives per iteration.
A synchronization round is one blocking global collective.
Optional reconstruction uses at most one further collective.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S=qT+O(1)\), or \(S=T+O(1)\) when all per-iteration collectives are fusible.
review_flags: This is a model-dependent synchronization accounting statement.
No supplied source directly documents collective fusion for sketch-based SDP.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The synchronization accounting is internally consistent and the complexity-bound role fits, but collective dependencies and fusion assumptions require a source.

children.title: Memory–Communication Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Regimes where additional local storage reduces transfers or reduced storage increases transfers.

knowledge_statements.title: Memory–Communication Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Replication tradeoff for a row-distributed rank sketch reconstructed on selected workers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a sketch \(Y\in\mathbb R^{n\times k}\) initially be evenly row-partitioned over \(p\) workers, and let reconstruction be performed on \(r\) workers, where \(1\le r\le p\). If each reconstruction worker must receive a complete copy and aggregate communication counts separately delivered scalar words without multicast savings, replication communicates \(rnk(1-1/p)\) words and produces \(r\) complete copies requiring \(rnk\) words, apart from any retained distributed partitions. For \(p\ge2\), both quantities are respectively \(\Theta(rnk)\) and \(\Theta(rnk)\). Retaining distributed reconstruction keeps aggregate sketch storage at \(\Theta(nk)\) and avoids this replication traffic.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under separately counted deliveries, giving each of r reconstruction workers a full n-by-k sketch communicates rnk(1−1/p) words and stores rnk replicated words; distributed reconstruction avoids this replication.
assumptions_latex: \(Y\) is initially evenly row-partitioned over \(p\) workers without replication.
Each of the \(r\) selected reconstruction workers requires every entry of \(Y\).
Aggregate communication counts scalar words delivered separately to recipients, without multicast savings.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M_{\mathrm{rep}}=rnk\) and \(V_{\mathrm{rep}}=rnk(1-1/p)\); when \(p\ge2\), both are \(\Theta(rnk)\).

notation.meaning: number of reconstruction workers receiving a full sketch

review_flags: No supplied source supports this replication model.

children.title: Communication-Dominated Reconstruction
children.top_down_role: Reconstruction settings whose scalability is limited primarily by data movement.

knowledge_statements.title: Communication-Dominated Reconstruction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Criterion under which gathering a distributed sketch dominates local factor reconstruction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Y\in\mathbb R^{n\times k}\) be distributed across \(p\) workers and gathered to one worker before reconstruction. If the gather transfers \(V=\Theta(nk)\) words over effective bandwidth \(B\), incurs latency \(L\), and local reconstruction requires \(F_{\mathrm{rec}}\) arithmetic operations at sustained rate \(R\), define communication-dominated reconstruction by \[L+V/B\;\ge\;F_{\mathrm{rec}}/R.\] For a dense local factorization with \(F_{\mathrm{rec}}=\Theta(nk^2+k^3)\), bandwidth dominance occurs whenever \(nk/B\) asymptotically exceeds \((nk^2+k^3)/R\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reconstruction is communication-dominated when sketch-gather latency and transfer time exceed the time for local factorization.
assumptions_latex: The sketch is gathered to one reconstruction worker.
Communication and computation do not overlap.
The bandwidth-latency performance model applies.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_{\mathrm{comm}}=L+\Theta(nk/B)\ge T_{\mathrm{rec}}=F_{\mathrm{rec}}/R\).

notation.meaning: effective communication bandwidth in words per unit time

review_flags: The supplied sources do not support this hardware performance criterion.
Reconstruction flop counts depend on the chosen factorization procedure.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition role fits and the bandwidth-latency criterion is coherent, but the reconstruction flop count and nonoverlap performance model lack supporting citations.

knowledge_statements.title: Unfavorable Spectral Gaps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of reliable eigenspace separation when the target spectral gap approaches the perturbation scale.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A,\widetilde A\in\mathbb S^n\), let \(E=\widetilde A-A\), and let \(U\) span an invariant subspace of \(A\) whose eigenvalue cluster is separated from the complementary spectrum by \(\delta>0\). Let \(\widetilde U\) be the corresponding subspace extracted from \(\widetilde A\). Standard symmetric eigenspace perturbation bounds have the form \(\|\sin\Theta(U,\widetilde U)\|_2\le \|E\|_2/\delta\) when the clusters remain identifiable. Consequently, if \(\delta\le\|E\|_2/\varepsilon\), such a bound cannot guarantee subspace error below \(\varepsilon\); at \(\delta=0\), the individual target subspace need not be identifiable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the spectral gap is comparable to perturbation error, eigenspace guarantees become vacuous; with zero gap, the selected subspace may be unidentifiable.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) and \(\widetilde A\) are real symmetric.
The compared eigenvalue clusters are consistently selected.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\delta\le\|E\|_2/\varepsilon\) prevents the perturbation bound from certifying \(\|\sin\Theta(U,\widetilde U)\|_2<\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: separation between target and complementary spectra

review_flags: Standard-field rationale: symmetric eigenspace perturbation theory.
An authoritative theorem locator for the stated sin-theta bound is not supplied.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role fits, but a Davis–Kahan-type bound requires a precise spectral-separation convention and cluster-identification hypotheses. No authoritative theorem locator is supplied.

knowledge_statements.title: Inaccurate Extreme Eigenspaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: How extreme-eigenspace error corrupts rank-one linear-minimization oracles over a trace-bounded PSD cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(G\in\mathbb S^n\), consider minimizing \(\langle G,X\rangle\) over \(X\succeq0\) with \(\operatorname{tr}X=\tau\). If \(u\) is a unit eigenvector for \(\lambda_{\min}(G)\), the exact oracle returns \(X_\star=\tau uu^\top\). For a computed unit vector \(\widetilde u\), the oracle error is \[\langle G,\tau\widetilde u\widetilde u^\top\rangle-\tau\lambda_{\min}(G)=\tau\bigl(\widetilde u^\top G\widetilde u-\lambda_{\min}(G)\bigr).\] If this quantity exceeds the outer method's permitted additive oracle tolerance, its stated convergence guarantee no longer applies.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inaccurate minimum eigenvector creates a precisely measurable additive oracle error; exceeding the outer method's tolerance invalidates its convergence guarantee.
assumptions_latex: \(G\in\mathbb S^n\) and \(\tau>0\).
The outer convergence result assumes a bounded additive linear-oracle error.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(e_{\mathrm{oracle}}=\tau(\widetilde u^\top G\widetilde u-\lambda_{\min}(G))\); failure occurs when \(e_{\mathrm{oracle}}\) exceeds the allowed tolerance.
review_flags: The oracle identity is elementary, but no supplied locator supports the outer-method failure threshold.
The exact tolerance depends on the matrix-free SDP algorithm.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The oracle-error identity is correct, but the claimed convergence-failure boundary depends on an unspecified outer method and its additive-oracle tolerance.

knowledge_statements.title: Sketch-Rank Underestimation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Irreducible approximation error when sketch rank is below the numerical rank required by the SDP iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\in\mathbb S_+^n\) have eigenvalues \(\lambda_1(X)\ge\cdots\ge\lambda_n(X)\ge0\), and suppose reconstruction from a sketch is constrained to output \(\widehat X\succeq0\) with \(\operatorname{rank}(\widehat X)\le k\). Then every such reconstruction satisfies \[\|X-\widehat X\|_F\ge\left(\sum_{j>k}\lambda_j(X)^2\right)^{1/2},\qquad \|X-\widehat X\|_2\ge\lambda_{k+1}(X).\] Hence choosing \(k\) below the numerical rank needed for tolerance \(\varepsilon\) makes \(\varepsilon\)-accurate reconstruction impossible, irrespective of the sketching or recovery algorithm.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rank-k reconstruction cannot remove spectral tail error; if that tail exceeds tolerance, no recovery algorithm can succeed.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is real symmetric positive semidefinite.
Every admissible reconstruction has rank at most \(k<n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_{\operatorname{rank}(\widehat X)\le k}\|X-\widehat X\|_F=(\sum_{j>k}\lambda_j(X)^2)^{1/2}\).
review_flags: Standard-field rationale: Eckart–Young–Mirsky low-rank approximation theorem.
No authoritative theorem locator was supplied for this exact formulation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The low-rank spectral-tail bounds correctly express the failure regime and the content kind fits, but no authoritative Eckart–Young–Mirsky theorem locator is provided.

knowledge_statements.title: Reconstruction–Feasibility Mismatch
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constraint residual caused by reconstructing an approximate PSD iterate from a sketch.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal A:\mathbb S^n\to\mathbb R^m\) be linear, let \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and suppose \(X\succeq0\) satisfies \(\mathcal A(X)=b\). For a reconstructed matrix \(\widehat X\succeq0\), \[\|\mathcal A(\widehat X)-b\|_2=\|\mathcal A(\widehat X-X)\|_2\le\|\mathcal A\|_{F\to2}\,\|\widehat X-X\|_F.\] If \(\|\mathcal A\|_{F\to2}>0\), the reconstruction bound \(\|\widehat X-X\|_F\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{feas}}/\|\mathcal A\|_{F\to2}\) is sufficient for feasibility residual at most \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{feas}}\). A reconstruction guarantee allowing a larger error does not by itself ensure that feasibility tolerance. If \(\mathcal A=0\), the residual is identically zero because feasibility implies \(b=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reconstruction error can be amplified by the constraint operator. For a nonzero operator, dividing the feasibility tolerance by its Frobenius-to-Euclidean norm gives a sufficient matrix-error threshold; the zero-operator case has zero residual.
assumptions_latex: \(X\succeq0\) satisfies \(\mathcal A(X)=b\).
\(\widehat X\succeq0\) is reconstructed from the sketch.
\(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{feas}}>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(\|\mathcal A\|_{F\to2}>0\), then \(\|\widehat X-X\|_F\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{feas}}/\|\mathcal A\|_{F\to2}\) implies \(\|\mathcal A(\widehat X)-b\|_2\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{feas}}\); if \(\mathcal A=0\), the residual is zero.

notation.meaning: operator norm from Frobenius norm to Euclidean norm

review_flags: The norm inequality is standard, but no supplied source treats sketch-reconstruction feasibility.
A larger permitted reconstruction error is not a necessity claim because residual depends on error alignment.

knowledge_statements.title: Operator-Cost Dominance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Runtime regime in which matrix-free operator applications outweigh sketch algebra and communication.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let one iteration perform \(q_A\) applications of \(\mathcal A\) or \(\mathcal A^*\), each costing \(C_A\), together with sketch algebra costing \(C_S\) and communication costing \(C_C\). Define operator-cost dominance by \[q_A C_A\ge C_S+C_C.\] Over \(T\) iterations the runtime model is \(T(q_A C_A+C_S+C_C)\); under the displayed condition, operator work accounts for at least one half of this modeled runtime. Consequently, reducing sketch rank or communication cannot improve total runtime by more than a factor of two unless it also reduces \(q_A\), \(C_A\), or the iteration count.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Operator cost dominates when oracle applications consume at least as much time as sketch algebra and communication combined.
assumptions_latex: Costs are measured in the same time units.
The additive, nonoverlapping runtime model applies.
Per-iteration costs are stationary.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q_A C_A\ge C_S+C_C\) implies \(q_A C_A/(q_A C_A+C_S+C_C)\ge1/2\).

notation.meaning: cost of one constraint-operator or adjoint application

review_flags: This performance boundary is conditional on an additive nonoverlap model.
The supplied operator-point-of-view locator does not establish the claimed cost decomposition.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition and factor-two consequence are correct under the additive nonoverlap model, but no cited source establishes that model for the target matrix-free SDP setting.

knowledge_statements.title: Minimal-Face Identification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal PSD face containing the feasible set of an affine semidefinite system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal F=\{X\in\mathbb S_+^n:\mathcal A(X)=b\}\) be nonempty, and choose \(X^\circ\in\operatorname{relint}(\mathcal F)\). If \(U\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}\) has orthonormal columns spanning \(\operatorname{range}(X^\circ)\), then the minimal face of \(\mathbb S_+^n\) containing \(\mathcal F\) is \[\operatorname{face}(\mathcal F,\mathbb S_+^n)=\{USU^\top:S\in\mathbb S_+^r\}.\] Equivalently, it consists of the positive semidefinite matrices whose ranges lie in \(\operatorname{range}(X^\circ)\). Replacing \(X\) by \(USU^\top\) gives an exact reduced feasibility system \(\mathcal A(USU^\top)=b\), \(S\succeq0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A relative-interior feasible matrix identifies the minimal PSD face through its range, yielding an exact lower-dimensional SDP representation.

\(X^\circ\in\operatorname{relint}(\mathcal F)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Exposing-Vector Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual certificate exposing a proper face that contains an affine SDP feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\mathcal F=\{X\in\mathbb S_+^n:\mathcal A(X)=b\}\), a vector \(y\in\mathbb R^m\) satisfying \[W:=\mathcal A^*y\succeq0,\qquad b^\top y=0,\qquad W\ne0\] certifies that every \(X\in\mathcal F\) lies in the proper exposed face \(\mathbb S_+^n\cap W^\perp\). If \(X\) is feasible, invariance and convexity imply that \(\mathcal R_G(X)\) is feasible; moreover \(X\succeq0\) implies \(\mathcal R_G(X)\succeq0\). knowledge_statements.title: Orbit-Algebra Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite permutation-group representation underlying exact symmetry reduction of real SDPs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G\) act on \(V=\{1,\ldots,n\}\), with permutation matrices \(P_g\). The orbitals \(O_1,\ldots,O_t\) of the induced action on \(V\times V\) have adjacency matrices \((A_k)_{ij}=1\) exactly when \((i,j)\in O_k\). Then
\[\{X\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}:P_gX P_g^{\mathsf T}=X\ \forall g\in G\}=\operatorname{span}\{A_1,\ldots,A_t\}.\]
Consequently, the invariant symmetric matrices are the self-adjoint part of this commutant and have a basis obtained by retaining each self-transpose \(A_k\) and replacing every transposed pair \(A_k,A_k^{\mathsf T}\) by \(A_k+A_k^{\mathsf T}\). Thus orbit coefficients give exact coordinates for the symmetry-fixed SDP variable space.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Matrices invariant under a finite permutation group are precisely those constant on pair orbits; orbital adjacency matrices therefore provide exact coordinates for symmetry-fixed SDP variables.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is a finite group acting on \(V=\{1,\ldots,n\}\).
\(P_g\) is the permutation matrix representing \(g\in G\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(G\)-invariant matrices equal the orbital algebra, and invariant symmetric matrices equal its self-adjoint part.

notation.meaning: An orbit of the induced action on ordered pairs.
The zero-one adjacency matrix of orbital O_k.

knowledge_statements.title: Partition-Granularity Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nested pair partitions quantify the strength and exactness requirements of orbit-style compression.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\Omega=\{\{i,j\}:1\le i\le j\le n\}\), and let \(\mathcal P\) refine a partition \(\mathcal Q\) of \(\Omega\). For a partition \(\mathcal R\), let \(L_{\mathcal R}\subseteq\mathbb S^n\) contain matrices whose entries are constant on every cell of \(\mathcal R\). Then
\[L_{\mathcal Q}\subseteq L_{\mathcal P},\qquad L_{\mathcal Q}\cap\mathbb S_+^n\subseteq L_{\mathcal P}\cap\mathbb S_+^n.\]
Thus coarsening gives stronger compression and fewer scalar variables, whereas refinement gives a weaker restriction. Restricting an SDP to \(L_{\mathcal Q}\) preserves its optimal value whenever it possesses an optimal solution in \(L_{\mathcal Q}\); invariance of all data under a finite group inducing \(\mathcal Q\) is a standard sufficient condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Coarser pair partitions impose stronger matrix equality restrictions. Compression is exact whenever an optimal solution lies in the coarser subspace; group invariance supplies a standard sufficient condition.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal P\) and \(\mathcal Q\) partition the unordered index pairs \(\Omega\).
Every cell of \(\mathcal P\) is contained in a cell of \(\mathcal Q\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_{\mathcal Q}\subseteq L_{\mathcal P}\), with exact restriction to \(L_{\mathcal Q}\) whenever an optimum belongs to \(L_{\mathcal Q}\).

notation.meaning: Symmetric matrices constant on cells of partition R.
