knowledge_statements.title: Orbit-Compression Failure Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A concrete loss of exactness when the objective is not invariant under the compressing group.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G=\{I,P\}\), where \(P\) swaps the two coordinates, and consider
\[\max\{\langle C,X\rangle:X\succeq0,\ \operatorname{tr}(X)=1\},\qquad C=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&0\end{pmatrix}.\]
The unrestricted optimum is \(1\), attained at \(X=\operatorname{diag}(1,0)\). Orbit compression to the fixed space \(PXP^{\mathsf T}=X\) forces \(X_{11}=X_{22}=1/2\), so every compressed feasible matrix has objective \(1/2\). Hence averaging or restricting variables to a group-fixed algebra need not preserve the optimum when the objective or constraints are not invariant under that group.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A two-coordinate SDP loses half its optimum when compressed by coordinate swapping because its objective is not swap-invariant. Data invariance is therefore essential for unconditional exactness.
assumptions_latex: \(X\in\mathbb S_+^2\) and \(\operatorname{tr}(X)=1\).
\(P\) exchanges the two coordinate axes.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The original optimum is \(1\), while the fixed-space optimum is \(1/2\).

knowledge_statements.title: Linear-Dependency Detection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Detection and certification of dependencies among affine equality constraints in an SDP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For constraints \(\langle A_i,X\rangle=b_i\), form \(M\in\mathbb R^{m\times d}\), where \(d=n(n+1)/2\), with row \(i\) equal to \(\operatorname{svec}(A_i)^{\mathsf T}\). Use exact row reduction to obtain an index set \(I\) whose rows form a basis of \(\operatorname{row}(M)\), and coefficients \(D\) satisfying \(M_{I^c}=DM_I\). Test the corresponding right-hand-side identity \(b_{I^c}=Db_I\). If it fails, the equality system is inconsistent; if it holds, the rows outside \(I\) are algebraically dependent and eligible for exact removal. A rank-revealing QR or SVD with a declared tolerance may instead generate candidate dependencies, but those candidates require exact or independently bounded certification before removal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Vectorize the equality matrices, compute and certify a row basis and dependency coefficients, and verify that the right-hand side satisfies the same dependencies. Numerical rank revelation alone supplies only candidate dependencies.
assumptions_latex: \(A_i\in\mathbb S^n\) and \(b_i\in\mathbb R\) for \(i=1,\ldots,m\).
\(\operatorname{svec}:\mathbb S^n\to\mathbb R^{n(n+1)/2}\) is a linear isomorphism.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Certified identities \(M_{I^c}=DM_I\) and \(b_{I^c}=Db_I\) identify removable dependent rows; failure of the right-hand-side identity certifies inconsistency.

notation.meaning: Indices of a certified row basis of M.

knowledge_statements.title: Redundant-Constraint Elimination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact removal of affine SDP equalities after coefficient and right-hand-side compatibility tests.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(\langle A_i,X\rangle=b_i\), retain a row-basis index set \(I\). For each \(j\notin I\), compute coefficients \(d_{ji}\) such that \(A_j=\sum_{i\in I}d_{ji}A_i\). If \(b_j=\sum_{i\in I}d_{ji}b_i\), delete constraint \(j\); it follows from the retained equalities for every \(X\in\mathbb S^n\). If the coefficient identity holds but the right-hand-side identity fails, terminate with infeasibility. After all compatible dependent rows are deleted, solve the SDP with only indices in \(I\), retaining the coefficients \(d_{ji}\) as a reconstruction certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Delete an equality only when both its matrix and right-hand side are the same linear combination of retained equalities; a right-hand-side mismatch certifies infeasibility.
assumptions_latex: \(I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}\) indexes a basis of \(\operatorname{span}\{A_1,\ldots,A_m\}\).
Dependency identities are evaluated exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Compatible dependent constraints may be removed without changing the feasible set; an incompatible dependency proves infeasibility.

notation.meaning: Coefficient expressing discarded constraint j through retained constraint i.

children.title: Numerical-Rank Ambiguity
children.top_down_role: Uncertain dependency classification caused by finite precision or poorly separated singular values.

knowledge_statements.title: Numerical-Rank Ambiguity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Threshold sensitivity of numerical dependency decisions near clustered or small singular values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(M\) be the vectorized constraint matrix and declare singular values exceeding \(\tau>0\) to be nonzero. Suppose \(\sigma_r(M)>\tau\ge\sigma_{r+1}(M)\). For a perturbation \(E\), Weyl's bound gives \(|\sigma_k(M+E)-\sigma_k(M)|\le\|E\|_2\). Hence the reported rank remains \(r\) whenever
\[\|E\|_2<\min\{\sigma_r(M)-\tau,\ \tau-\sigma_{r+1}(M)\}.\]
If either gap is zero or comparable to data uncertainty, admissible perturbations can move a singular value across \(\tau\), changing which constraints are eliminated. Rank-based elimination is then numerically ambiguous and requires scaling, higher precision, or an explicit uncertainty report.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A thresholded numerical rank is reliable only when singular values are separated from the threshold by more than the data perturbation; otherwise elimination decisions can change.
assumptions_latex: \(M,E\in\mathbb R^{m\times d}\).
Numerical rank counts singular values strictly greater than \(\tau>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Rank \(r\) is stable under the displayed perturbation bound and ambiguous when no separating gap exceeds the uncertainty.

notation.meaning: The kth largest singular value of M.
Perturbation in the assembled constraint matrix.

children.title: Post-Elimination Consistency Checks
children.top_down_role: Checks concerning feasibility preservation and retained constraint consistency after elimination.

knowledge_statements.title: Post-Elimination Consistency Checks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A verifiable certificate that discarded equalities are implied by retained equalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(I\) be retained indices and let \(A_j=\sum_{i\in I}d_{ji}A_i\) for every discarded \(j\). A post-elimination consistency certificate consists of these coefficient identities and the checks
\[b_j=\sum_{i\in I}d_{ji}b_i\qquad(j\notin I).\]
If all checks hold, any \(X\) satisfying \(\langle A_i,X\rangle=b_i\) for \(i\in I\) automatically satisfies every discarded equality. For an approximate candidate \(\widehat X\), also evaluate all original residuals \(r_j=\langle A_j,\widehat X\rangle-b_j\); acceptance requires the declared scaled residual tolerance for both retained and reconstructed discarded rows, together with the original cone-feasibility test.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Store dependency coefficients, verify matching right-hand sides, then evaluate every original residual and cone condition on the returned solution.
assumptions_latex: \(A_j=\sum_{i\in I}d_{ji}A_i\) for every \(j\notin I\).
The acceptance rule declares residual and cone-feasibility tolerances.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The coefficient and right-hand-side identities certify exact equivalence of the retained and full equality systems.

notation.meaning: Stored dependency coefficients for discarded row j.
Residual of original equality j at the candidate solution.

knowledge_statements.title: Block-Diagonal Cone Decomposition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact product-cone representation of positive semidefinite matrices constrained to a fixed block-diagonal subspace.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(n=n_1+\cdots+n_q\), and let \(L\subseteq\mathbb S^n\) be the subspace of matrices block diagonal with these block sizes. The linear map
\[\Phi:\mathbb S^{n_1}\times\cdots\times\mathbb S^{n_q}\to L,\qquad \Phi(X_1,\ldots,X_q)=\operatorname{diag}(X_1,\ldots,X_q)\]
is an isomorphism satisfying
\[\Phi^{-1}(L\cap\mathbb S_+^n)=\mathbb S_+^{n_1}\times\cdots\times\mathbb S_+^{n_q}.\]
Thus \(X=\operatorname{diag}(X_1,\ldots,X_q)\) is positive semidefinite exactly when every \(X_k\succeq0\). An SDP restricted to \(L\) may therefore replace one semidefinite cone by this product cone, although affine constraints may still couple variables from different blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A block-diagonal matrix is positive semidefinite exactly when each diagonal block is positive semidefinite, yielding an exact product of smaller semidefinite cones.
assumptions_latex: \(n_k\ge1\) and \(n=\sum_{k=1}^q n_k\).
\(L\) is the block-diagonal subspace for the fixed block partition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L\cap\mathbb S_+^n\cong\prod_{k=1}^q\mathbb S_+^{n_k}\).

notation.meaning: Positive semidefinite cone for block k.

children.title: Free-Variable Elimination
children.top_down_role: Exact removal or substitution of unrestricted decision variables.

knowledge_statements.title: Free-Variable Elimination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projection and recovery for unrestricted variables appearing linearly in conic equality constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider \(\mathcal A(X)+By=b\), with conic variable \(X\in K\), unrestricted \(y\in\mathbb R^p\), and full-column-rank \(B\in\mathbb R^{m\times p}\). Choose \(N\) whose columns form a basis of \(\ker(B^{\mathsf T})\). Eliminate \(y\) by replacing the equality with
\[N^{\mathsf T}(\mathcal A(X)-b)=0,\qquad X\in K.\]
For every reduced feasible \(X\), recover the unique free variable
\[y=B^{\dagger}(b-\mathcal A(X)),\qquad B^{\dagger}=(B^{\mathsf T}B)^{-1}B^{\mathsf T}.\]
The projected equality ensures that \(b-\mathcal A(X)\in\operatorname{range}(B)\), so substitution recovers a feasible pair. Stop when the projected residual and recovered original residual satisfy their declared tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Project equalities onto the orthogonal complement of the free-variable coefficient range, solve the reduced conic system, and recover the eliminated variable by a left inverse.
assumptions_latex: \(X\in K\) for a closed convex cone \(K\).
\(B\in\mathbb R^{m\times p}\) has full column rank.
\(N\) spans \(\ker(B^{\mathsf T})\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The projected system is feasible exactly when the original system is feasible, with \(y=B^{\dagger}(b-\mathcal A(X))\).

notation.meaning: Left pseudoinverse of the full-column-rank matrix B.
Basis matrix for the orthogonal complement of range(B).
Linear map from the conic variable to equality residual space.

children.title: Slack-Variable Elimination

knowledge_statements.title: Slack-Variable Elimination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact substitution of a slack variable constrained to a cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider a conic constraint represented by
\[\mathcal A(x)+s=b,\qquad s\in K,\]
where \(\mathcal A:\mathbb R^p\to\mathbb R^m\) is linear and \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) is a closed convex cone. Eliminate \(s\) by substituting \(s=b-\mathcal A(x)\), producing the reduced constraint
\[b-\mathcal A(x)\in K.\]
Every feasible \(x\) of the reduced problem has the unique recovered slack \(s=b-\mathcal A(x)\), and every feasible pair \((x,s)\) maps to such an \(x\). Objectives independent of \(s\) are unchanged. If the objective contains \(\langle c_s,s\rangle\), substitute it as \(\langle c_s,b-\mathcal A(x)\rangle\) before deletion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replace a conic slack by its defining residual. This gives an equivalent cone-membership constraint and a unique formula for reconstructing the slack.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) is a closed convex cone.
\(s\) occurs in the defining equality with identity coefficient.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists s\in K:\mathcal A(x)+s=b\) if and only if \(b-\mathcal A(x)\in K\).

notation.meaning: Linear residual map for the retained variables.

children.title: Elimination-Order Effects
children.top_down_role: Structural consequences of choosing different orders for auxiliary-variable removal.

knowledge_statements.title: Elimination-Order Effects
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact reduced systems agree across admissible orders, but intermediate cost and numerical behavior need not.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Partition a linear system matrix into retained indices \(R\) and eliminated indices \(E=E_1\mathbin{\dot\cup}E_2\). If every required pivot block is nonsingular, exact block Gaussian elimination satisfies
\[\operatorname{Schur}_{E_2}(\operatorname{Schur}_{E_1}(M))=\operatorname{Schur}_{E}(M),\]
up to a simultaneous permutation of retained rows and columns; the same conclusion holds with \(E_1\) and \(E_2\) reversed. Thus admissible exact orders produce the same final reduced operator. Nevertheless, they can produce different intermediate nonzero patterns, frontal sizes, pivot magnitudes, and rounding-error growth. Elimination order therefore affects computational cost and numerical stability even when it does not alter the exact projected feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Admissible exact elimination orders yield the same final Schur complement, but can have very different intermediate sparsity, memory cost, pivots, and rounding errors.
assumptions_latex: \(M\) is partitioned into retained indices \(R\) and disjoint eliminated sets \(E_1,E_2\).
All pivot blocks required by both orders are nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Both orders yield \(\operatorname{Schur}_{E_1\cup E_2}(M)\) exactly, while intermediate sparsity and conditioning may differ.

notation.meaning: Schur complement after eliminating index set E.
Indices retained in the final reduced system.

children.title: Elimination Stability Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Numerical regimes where exact symbolic elimination becomes poorly conditioned in computation.

knowledge_statements.title: Elimination Stability Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Schur-complement sensitivity to perturbations of a symmetric positive-definite pivot block, with the coupling block bounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(M=\begin{pmatrix}A&B\\B^{\mathsf T}&D\end{pmatrix}\), where \(D\succ0\), and define \(S=A-BD^{-1}B^{\mathsf T}\). If \(\|D^{-1}\|_2\|\Delta D\|_2<1\), then
\[
\|(D+\Delta D)^{-1}-D^{-1}\|_2\leq\frac{\|D^{-1}\|_2^2\|\Delta D\|_2}{1-\|D^{-1}\|_2\|\Delta D\|_2}.
\]
Consequently, for bounded \(B\), the Schur-complement change caused by perturbing \(D\) is controlled while \(\lambda_{\min}(D)\) is bounded away from zero. As \(\lambda_{\min}(D)\downarrow0\), inverse sensitivity, and hence Schur-complement sensitivity for nonvanishing coupling, can become unbounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With a bounded coupling block, Schur-complement sensitivity to pivot perturbations is controlled when the pivot remains uniformly positive definite and can become unbounded as its smallest eigenvalue approaches zero.
assumptions_latex: \(A=A^{\mathsf T}\), \(D=D^{\mathsf T}\succ0\).
\(\|B\|_2\) is bounded when uniform Schur-complement sensitivity is asserted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lambda_{\min}(D)\downarrow0\) permits unbounded inverse sensitivity and, for nonvanishing coupling, unbounded Schur-complement sensitivity.

notation.meaning: Schur complement after eliminating the pivot block

knowledge_statements.title: Facial-Then-Chordal Reduction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact composition of face compression and chordal positive-semidefinite completion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose an SDP feasible set lies in the exposed face \(F=\{UYU^{\mathsf T}:Y\in\mathbb S_+^r\}\), where \(U^{\mathsf T}U=I_r\). Substitute \(X=UYU^{\mathsf T}\). Assume every reduced objective and constraint depends only on entries indexed by a chordal graph \(G=(V,E)\), with maximal cliques \(C_1,\ldots,C_q\). A reduced partial matrix \(Y_E\) admits a positive-semidefinite completion exactly when
\[
Y_E[C_k,C_k]\succeq0\quad(k=1,\ldots,q),
\]
with duplicated clique entries identified consistently. Thus face compression followed by the clique-completion formulation preserves feasibility and the optimal value under these hypotheses.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compress to the minimal face, then replace the reduced PSD constraint by consistent clique PSD constraints when its aggregate sparsity graph is chordal.
assumptions_latex: \(F=U\mathbb S_+^rU^{\mathsf T}\) contains the feasible set.
\(G\) is chordal and all reduced data use only \(E\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Y_E\) has a PSD completion if and only if every consistent maximal-clique submatrix is PSD.

notation.meaning: maximal cliques of the chordal graph
partial reduced matrix on the specified sparsity pattern

knowledge_statements.title: Symmetry-Then-Chordal Reduction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact fixed-point restriction followed by chordal decomposition of the resulting blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider an SDP invariant under \(X\mapsto Q_gXQ_g^{\mathsf T}\) for every \(g\) in a finite orthogonal group. Averaging gives \(\mathcal R(X)=|G|^{-1}\sum_gQ_gXQ_g^{\mathsf T}\), which preserves feasibility, objective value, and positive semidefiniteness. Hence an optimum exists in the fixed-point space. If an orthogonal basis simultaneously block-diagonalizes that space and each block's specified-entry graph is chordal, then each block PSD-completion constraint is equivalently represented by consistent PSD constraints on its maximal cliques. The symmetry restriction followed by these chordal formulations therefore preserves the optimal value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Average over an exact symmetry group, block-diagonalize the fixed-point space, and apply chordal clique formulations within each block.
assumptions_latex: The objective and feasible set are invariant under every \(Q_g\).
Each block's specified-entry graph is chordal.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An optimal fixed-point solution is represented exactly by consistent clique-wise PSD constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Reduction-Then-Low-Rank Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Factorized representation after an exact reduction to a smaller PSD cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let an exact reduction replace \(X\in\mathbb S_+^n\) by \(X=UYU^{\mathsf T}\), where \(U\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}\) has full column rank and \(Y\in\mathbb S_+^r\). Every reduced matrix has a factorization \(Y=ZZ^{\mathsf T}\) with \(Z\in\mathbb R^{r\times p}\) whenever \(p\geq\operatorname{rank}(Y)\). Thus choosing \(p\geq r\) gives an exact representation of the entire reduced cone:
\[
X=UZZ^{\mathsf T}U^{\mathsf T}.
\]
For \(p<r\), the formulation represents exactly the reduced matrices of rank at most \(p\) and is generally a nonconvex restriction, not an exact cone reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After exact cone reduction, factorizing the reduced PSD matrix is exact with sufficient factor width; smaller width imposes a nonconvex rank restriction.
assumptions_latex: \(U\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}\) has full column rank.
The preceding reduction \(X=UYU^{\mathsf T}\) is exact.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p\geq r\) represents all reduced PSD matrices, whereas \(p<r\) enforces \(\operatorname{rank}(Y)\leq p\).

knowledge_statements.title: Noncommuting Reduction Orders
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A two-dimensional example where facial restriction and symmetry projection do not commute.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F=\{t e_1e_1^{\mathsf T}:t\geq0\}\subset\mathbb S_+^2\), let \(P=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}\), and define \(\mathcal R(X)=(X+PXP^{\mathsf T})/2\). Then
\[
\mathcal R(F)=\{(t/2)I_2:t\geq0\},
\qquad
F\cap\operatorname{Fix}(\mathcal R)=\{0\}.
\]
Therefore averaging after restriction to \(F\) and restricting \(F\) to symmetry-fixed matrices give different cones. The obstruction is that \(F\) is not invariant under \(P\); consequently, exact facial and symmetry reductions cannot be reordered without an invariance or compatibility condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Facial and symmetry reductions can produce different cones when the selected face is not invariant under the symmetry group.
assumptions_latex: \(F=\{t e_1e_1^{\mathsf T}:t\geq0\}\).
\(P\) swaps the two coordinates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal R(F)\neq F\cap\operatorname{Fix}(\mathcal R)\), so the two reduction orders do not commute.

notation.meaning: rank-one face of the PSD cone

knowledge_statements.title: Approximate Exposing Vectors
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral-gap criterion for stable recovery of a face from an inexact exposing matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(W\succeq0\) expose the face \(F(W)=\{X\succeq0:\langle W,X\rangle=0\}\), and suppose every positive eigenvalue of \(W\) is at least \(\gamma>0\). For \(\widehat W=W+E\) with \(\|E\|_2<\gamma/2\), let \(P\) project onto \(\ker W\) and let \(\widehat P\) project onto the eigenvectors of \(\widehat W\) having eigenvalues below \(\gamma/2\). Then
\[
\|\widehat P-P\|_2\leq \frac{2\|E\|_2}{\gamma}.
\]
Without a positive spectral gap, arbitrarily small perturbations can change the inferred kernel dimension and hence the detected face.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An approximate exposing matrix identifies the face stably only when zero and positive eigenvalues are separated by a certified spectral gap.
assumptions_latex: \(W\succeq0\) and \(\sigma(W)\subseteq\{0\}\cup[\gamma,\infty)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|\widehat P-P\|_2\leq2\|E\|_2/\gamma\); no analogous uniform guarantee exists when \(\gamma=0\).

notation.meaning: face exposed by the PSD matrix W

knowledge_statements.title: Numerically Ambiguous Face Detection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Threshold ambiguity in numerical face detection from an exposing matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given a computed symmetric exposing matrix \(\widehat W\), classify eigenvalues not exceeding \(\tau\) as belonging to its detected kernel. Suppose the unknown symmetric perturbation satisfies \(\|E\|_2\leq\varepsilon\). If
\[
\operatorname{dist}\bigl(\tau,\sigma(\widehat W)\bigr)>\varepsilon,
\]
then the detected kernel dimension is invariant under every admissible perturbation. Conversely, if some eigenvalue lies at distance strictly less than \(\varepsilon\) from \(\tau\), an admissible symmetric perturbation can move that eigenvalue across the threshold, making the numerical rank, kernel dimension, and inferred PSD face ambiguous. At distance exactly \(\varepsilon\), invariance depends on the side of the threshold and the convention used at equality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Face detection is stable when every exposing-matrix eigenvalue is farther from the numerical threshold than the perturbation radius; an eigenvalue strictly inside that radius makes the detected face ambiguous.
assumptions_latex: \(\widehat W=\widehat W^{\mathsf T}\).
Admissible symmetric perturbations satisfy \(\|E\|_2\leq\varepsilon\).
Eigenvalues not exceeding \(\tau\) are classified as numerical zeros.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Distance greater than \(\varepsilon\) guarantees invariant threshold classification, while distance strictly less than \(\varepsilon\) permits ambiguity.

children.title: Symmetry-Detection Reliability
children.top_down_role: Reliability of detected invariances under numerical data, tolerances, or incomplete structural information.

knowledge_statements.title: Symmetry-Detection Reliability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact algebraic test for an orthogonal symmetry of standard-form SDP data.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the SDP \(\min\{\langle C,X\rangle:\langle A_i,X\rangle=b_i,\ X\succeq0\}\), an orthogonal matrix \(Q\) is a data symmetry if there exists a matrix \(R\) such that
\[
Q^{\mathsf T}CQ=C,\qquad Q^{\mathsf T}A_iQ=\sum_jR_{ij}A_j\ \text{for every }i,\qquad Rb=b.
\]
These identities imply that \(X\mapsto QXQ^{\mathsf T}\) preserves feasibility and objective value. With noisy data, tolerance-based detection is reliable as an exact reduction only when the displayed identities are certified for the underlying exact data; small empirical residuals alone establish merely approximate symmetry.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A candidate orthogonal symmetry is exact only when it preserves the objective and maps the affine constraint system, including its right-hand side, to itself.
assumptions_latex: \(Q^{\mathsf T}Q=I\).
The SDP data are \(C,A_1,\ldots,A_m,b\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed identities certify invariance under \(X\mapsto QXQ^{\mathsf T}\).

children.title: Invariant-Basis Growth
children.top_down_role: Growth of the basis required to represent the detected invariant matrix algebra.

knowledge_statements.title: Invariant-Basis Growth
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dimension of the Hermitian invariant space for a finite-dimensional unitary representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let a complex unitary representation decompose as
\[
\mathbb C^n\cong\bigoplus_{\alpha=1}^s\bigl(\mathbb C^{m_\alpha}\otimes V_\alpha\bigr),
\]
where the \(V_\alpha\) are pairwise inequivalent irreducible representations and \(m_\alpha\) are their multiplicities. The real vector space of Hermitian matrices commuting with the representation has dimension
\[
d=\sum_{\alpha=1}^s m_\alpha^2.
\]
Thus invariant-basis size is governed by multiplicities, not merely by the number of irreducible types. Large multiplicities can make \(d\) approach the unreduced Hermitian dimension \(n^2\), eliminating the dimensional benefit of symmetry reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The invariant Hermitian basis has dimension equal to the sum of squared irreducible multiplicities, so repeated representations can erase symmetry savings.
assumptions_latex: The representation is finite-dimensional and unitary over \(\mathbb C\).
The \(V_\alpha\) are pairwise inequivalent irreducible representations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\dim_{\mathbb R}\operatorname{Herm}(\operatorname{Comm}(G))=\sum_\alpha m_\alpha^2\).

notation.meaning: real dimension of the invariant Hermitian space

children.title: Approximate-Symmetry Regimes
children.top_down_role: Settings where apparent invariances are perturbed, incomplete, or tolerance dependent.

knowledge_statements.title: Approximate-Symmetry Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantitative data discrepancy under restriction to an approximately invariant model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal R\) be an orthogonal group-averaging projection, and suppose
\[
\|C-\mathcal R(C)\|_2\leq\delta_C,
\qquad
\|A_i-\mathcal R(A_i)\|_2\leq\delta_i.
\]
For every \(X\succeq0\) with \(\|X\|_*\leq R\),
\[
|\langle C-\mathcal R(C),X\rangle|\leq\delta_CR,
\qquad
|\langle A_i-\mathcal R(A_i),X\rangle|\leq\delta_iR.
\]
Thus averaging controls objective and constraint discrepancies on a norm-bounded region, but it is not an exact reduction unless the residuals vanish or additional robust-feasibility arguments absorb them.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Approximate symmetry yields bounded data errors on norm-bounded PSD sets, but does not justify an exact fixed-point reduction by itself.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal R\) is an orthogonal group-averaging projection.
\(X\succeq0\) and \(\|X\|_*\leq R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Data discrepancies are at most \(\delta_CR\) and \(\delta_iR\), but exactness generally requires zero residuals.

children.title: Basis-Expansion Cost Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Cases where basis construction or storage offsets the benefit of symmetry reduction.

knowledge_statements.title: Basis-Expansion Cost Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dense arithmetic and storage costs for explicitly expanding an invariant matrix basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B_1,\ldots,B_d\in\mathbb S^n\) be an invariant basis and write \(X=\sum_{k=1}^d z_kB_k\). For \(m\) dense constraint matrices, explicitly forming all reduced coefficients \(\langle A_i,B_k\rangle\) requires \(md\) dense matrix inner products and therefore \(O(mdn^2)\) arithmetic operations. Storing the basis and the coefficient table requires \(O(dn^2+md)\) scalars. Hence, when \(d\) approaches the ambient matrix-space dimension and the basis has no exploitable sparsity or implicit structure, explicit expansion can eliminate the intended preprocessing advantage; blockwise or matrix-free representations may reduce this cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dense invariant basis requires order md matrix inner products and can lose its preprocessing advantage when its dimension is large and no sparse or implicit structure is available.
assumptions_latex: All \(A_i\) and \(B_k\) are stored as dense \(n\times n\) matrices.
A dense matrix inner product costs \(O(n^2)\) arithmetic operations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Explicit expansion costs \(O(mdn^2)\) arithmetic operations and \(O(dn^2+md)\) scalar storage.

children.title: False-Symmetry Failure Modes
children.top_down_role: Structural or numerical consequences of accepting unsupported invariances.

knowledge_statements.title: False-Symmetry Failure Modes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A false coordinate-swap symmetry that destroys feasibility after fixed-point restriction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider the feasible SDP system
\[
X\succeq0,
\qquad X_{11}=1,
\qquad X_{22}=2.
\]
Let \(P=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}\). If \(P\) is falsely accepted as a symmetry, fixed-point reduction imposes \(X=PXP^{\mathsf T}\), which forces \(X_{11}=X_{22}\). This contradicts the two affine constraints, so the reduced system is infeasible although \(X=\operatorname{diag}(1,2)\) is feasible for the original system. Thus a false symmetry can remove every feasible point; approximate agreement of selected data is insufficient for exact symmetry reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Misclassifying a coordinate swap as a symmetry can make a feasible SDP infeasible after fixed-point restriction.
assumptions_latex: The original constraints are \(X\succeq0\), \(X_{11}=1\), and \(X_{22}=2\).
The erroneous reduction enforces \(X=PXP^{\mathsf T}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The original system is feasible, while its false-symmetry fixed-point restriction is infeasible.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\sigma_{\max}^+(T)\) and \(\sigma_{\min}^+(T)\) denote the largest and smallest nonzero singular values of a linear map \(T\), and set \(\kappa_2(T)=\sigma_{\max}^+(T)/\sigma_{\min}^+(T)\). For an injective exact-reduction map \(U\), the reduced operator \(\widehat{\mathcal A}=\mathcal A U\) satisfies \[\kappa_2(\widehat{\mathcal A})\leq \kappa_2(\mathcal A|_{\operatorname{range}U})\,\kappa_2(U).\] Hence an algebraically exact reduction need not preserve numerical conditioning; an ill-conditioned basis \(U\) can amplify the condition number by a factor as large as \(\kappa_2(U)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact SDP reduction can still degrade numerical conditioning: the reduced constraint operator may inherit the conditioning of the restricted original operator multiplied by that of the reduction basis.
knowledge_statements.title: Reduction-Induced Conditioning Loss

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize clique matrices \(X_k^0\succeq0\) and separator variables \(Z_{k\ell}^0\) for every clique-tree edge \((k,\ell)\). At iteration \(t\), each clique independently updates \(X_k^{t+1}\) by solving its local conic subproblem augmented with penalties or multipliers for \(R_{S_{k\ell}}(X_k)=Z_{k\ell}\). Each edge then updates \(Z_{k\ell}^{t+1}\) from the two incident separator copies and updates the associated dual variables. Stop when all local optimality residuals and \(\|R_{S_{k\ell}}(X_k)-R_{S_{k\ell}}(X_\ell)\|_F\) are below prescribed tolerances; output the consistent clique family.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve clique PSD subproblems in parallel, reconcile their shared separator entries, update interface multipliers, and stop when local optimality and separator-disagreement residuals meet tolerance.
knowledge_statements.title: Clique-Consensus Execution

knowledge_statements.title: Block-Separable Cone Execution
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parallel execution of separable cone-local operations over finite Cartesian products of closed convex cones.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(q\geq1\), let \(K_k\subseteq\mathbb R^{n_k}\) be closed convex cones, and set \(K=K_1\times\cdots\times K_q\). At a cone-operation stage, assign block \(k\) to a worker. For \(v=(v_1,\ldots,v_q)\), compute the Euclidean projections independently and assemble \[\Pi_K(v)=\bigl(\Pi_{K_1}(v_1),\ldots,\Pi_{K_q}(v_q)\bigr).\] If a barrier is used, its derivatives may likewise be evaluated independently when the selected barrier has the separable form \(\Phi(x)=\sum_{k=1}^q\Phi_k(x_k)\). After the block computations, aggregate only the quantities required by the model's linear coupling equations. The enclosing optimization algorithm supplies its global update and stopping tests.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Execute projections independently on the factors of a product cone. Barrier derivatives may also be executed independently when the chosen barrier is a sum of block barriers; linear coupling and global stopping tests remain the responsibility of the enclosing solver.
assumptions_latex: \(q\geq1\) and each \(K_k\subseteq\mathbb R^{n_k}\) is a closed convex cone.
The cone is the Cartesian product \(K=K_1\times\cdots\times K_q\).
Any barrier claimed to separate has the form \(\Phi(x)=\sum_{k=1}^q\Phi_k(x_k)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Pi_K(v_1,\ldots,v_q)=(\Pi_{K_1}(v_1),\ldots,\Pi_{K_q}(v_q))\), and derivatives of a separable barrier are block separable.

notation.meaning: Euclidean projection onto the closed convex cone \(K\)

children.title: Domain-Decomposition Execution
children.top_down_role: Execution organized through partitions of primal variables, matrix domains, or cone blocks.

assumptions_latex: The variable space decomposes orthogonally as \(\mathcal X=\mathcal X_1\oplus\cdots\oplus\mathcal X_q\).
The conic model has the form \(\min_x f(x)+g(\mathcal A x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Domain blocks can be updated concurrently, with coupling communicated through the aggregate image \(\sum_k\mathcal A_kx_k\).

notation.meaning: Restriction of \(\mathcal A\) to domain block \(\mathcal X_k\)

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: block-coordinate execution of a linearly coupled convex conic model
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Synchronous variable-space partitioning for linearly coupled conic models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Write \(x=\sum_{k=1}^q x_k\) with \(x_k\in\mathcal X_k\), initialize feasible block states, and maintain \(s^t=\sum_k\mathcal A_kx_k^t\). At iteration \(t\), each worker computes a local update \(x_k^{t+1}\) using its block objective, cone constraints, the current shared range information, and the algorithm's current multipliers. Reduce the increments \(\mathcal A_k(x_k^{t+1}-x_k^t)\) to form \(s^{t+1}\), then update shared multipliers. Stop when the assembled primal feasibility, stationarity, and gap residuals meet tolerance; output \(x^{t+1}=\sum_kx_k^{t+1}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partition variables by domain blocks, solve block updates concurrently, and combine their operator images to update the shared constraints, multipliers, and global residuals.
knowledge_statements.title: Domain-Decomposition Execution

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The execution pattern is plausible, but the local update, multiplier scheme, feasibility assumptions, and convergence conditions depend on the chosen decomposition algorithm. Standard-field rationale alone cannot establish this algorithmic record.

children.title: Range-Decomposition Execution
children.top_down_role: Execution organized through partitions of constraints, operator outputs, or dual ranges.

assumptions_latex: The constraint space decomposes orthogonally as \(\mathcal Y=\mathcal Y_1\oplus\cdots\oplus\mathcal Y_p\).
Each range block has a restriction operator \(P_j:\mathcal Y\to\mathcal Y_j\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Constraint-block computations can run concurrently and assemble by the adjoint sum \(\sum_j\mathcal A_j^*y_j\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: constraint-row partitioning and adjoint reduction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Synchronous constraint-space partitioning with adjoint aggregation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize range-block variables \(y_j^0\in\mathcal Y_j\). At iteration \(t\), broadcast the current primal state \(x^t\); each worker forms its local residual \(r_j^t=\mathcal A_jx^t-b_j\) and independently updates \(y_j^{t+1}\) using the local cone or proximal rule. Reduce the adjoint contributions to obtain \(g^{t+1}=\sum_{j=1}^p\mathcal A_j^*y_j^{t+1}\), and use \(g^{t+1}\) in the primal update. Stop when the norm assembled from the block residuals, the stationarity residual, and the gap satisfy tolerance; output the assembled primal-dual pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partition constraints across workers, update each constraint block independently, and sum adjoint contributions to obtain the global stationarity direction and stopping residuals.
knowledge_statements.title: Range-Decomposition Execution

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The adjoint aggregation is standard, but the multiplier and primal updates are algorithm-dependent and no source establishes their validity or convergence for the stated conic setting.

children.title: Cross-Decomposition Interface Coupling
children.top_down_role: Data dependencies connecting domain-oriented partitions with range-oriented partitions.

assumptions_latex: The domain and range partitions define blocks \(\mathcal A_{jk}=P_j\mathcal A|_{\mathcal X_k}\).
Workers exchange only data along nonzero operator blocks.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The two decompositions are exactly coupled when each range aggregate and each domain adjoint aggregate equals its full-operator counterpart.

notation.meaning: Operator block from domain block \(k\) to range block \(j\)

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: block operator and adjoint identities
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact algebraic interface between simultaneous domain and range partitions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For domain variables \(x_k\in\mathcal X_k\) and range multipliers \(y_j\in\mathcal Y_j\), define \(\mathcal A_{jk}=P_j\mathcal A|_{\mathcal X_k}\). Cross-decomposition communication is algebraically consistent precisely when every range worker forms \[s_j=\sum_k\mathcal A_{jk}x_k=P_j\mathcal A\Bigl(\sum_kx_k\Bigr),\] and every domain worker forms \[g_k=\sum_j\mathcal A_{jk}^*y_j=P_{\mathcal X_k}\mathcal A^*\Bigl(\sum_jy_j\Bigr),\] where \(P_{\mathcal X_k}\) is the orthogonal domain projector. These identities are the interface invariant required for decomposed residuals and stationarity equations to equal the undecomposed ones.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Domain and range partitions couple correctly when range workers sum all incident forward images and domain workers sum all incident adjoint images, exactly reproducing the global operator equations.
knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Decomposition Interface Coupling

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The block forward and adjoint identities are mathematically plausible under the stated orthogonal decompositions, but this nontrivial interface condition has no cited source or inspectable locator.

children.title: Load-Partitioning Regimes
children.top_down_role: Work allocation across decomposition units with heterogeneous dimensions or operator costs.

assumptions_latex: Task \(i\) has predicted nonnegative cost \(w_i\).
The tasks are assigned to \(p\) workers by a partition \(I_1,\ldots,I_p\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Execution is computation-balanced when \(\max_k L_k\) is controlled, communication-balanced when boundary traffic is controlled, and memory-balanced when resident block data fit each worker.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: makespan, communication, and memory partition objectives
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Static partitioning under computation, communication, and device-memory constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L_k=\sum_{i\in I_k}w_i\) and \(\bar L=p^{-1}\sum_iw_i\). A compute-balanced regime minimizes or bounds the makespan surrogate \(\max_kL_k\). A communication-aware regime additionally penalizes operator or clique interfaces crossing distinct workers. A memory-feasible regime requires each worker's resident matrix, factor, and workspace footprint to remain below its capacity. A load partition is admissible for execution only if its selected regime satisfies all hard resource constraints; among admissible partitions, the regime's objective determines whether computation, communication, or memory is the controlling resource.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partitioning may be compute-balanced, communication-aware, or memory-constrained; the applicable regime minimizes its controlling resource while satisfying every hard worker-capacity constraint.
knowledge_statements.title: Load-Partitioning Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The compute, communication, and memory regimes fit the container, but their performance-model formulation and admissibility principle lack a cited source.

children.title: Partition-Imbalance Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Scalability limits caused by uneven work, communication, or memory across partitions.

assumptions_latex: Independent tasks have costs \(w_i\geq0\) and are assigned without splitting to \(p\) workers.
Synchronous execution waits for the slowest worker at each barrier.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The idealized parallel efficiency is at most \(\bar L/L_{\max}=1/\rho\), so unbounded imbalance precludes uniformly efficient synchronous scaling.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic synchronous makespan bound excluding communication and scheduling overhead.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For worker loads \(L_1,\ldots,L_p\), any synchronous schedule completing one iteration has compute time \(T_p\geq L_{\max}\). Since the total work is \(W=\sum_kL_k=p\bar L\), its ideal work-based efficiency satisfies \[E_p=\frac{W}{pT_p}\leq\frac{\bar L}{L_{\max}}=\frac{1}{\rho}.\] Thus \(\rho\leq1+\varepsilon\) guarantees at most an imbalance loss factor \(1+\varepsilon\), whereas a family with \(\rho\to\infty\) cannot maintain efficiency bounded away from zero under barrier-synchronous execution, even before communication costs are counted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For synchronous workers, iteration time is at least the largest assigned load and ideal parallel efficiency is at most the reciprocal of the load-imbalance ratio.
knowledge_statements.title: Partition-Imbalance Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The inequality E_p <= 1/rho follows from the stated makespan lower bound, but rho <= 1+epsilon does not by itself guarantee efficiency or a bounded total loss when other delays are allowed. A source and a correction distinguishing an upper bound from a performance guarantee are required.

assumptions_latex: The PSD variable is block diagonal, \(X=\operatorname{diag}(X_1,\ldots,X_q)\).
Each block \(X_k\) is symmetric of order \(n_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The PSD projection and feasibility test decompose exactly across blocks, with parallel critical path governed by the largest block.

notation.meaning: PSD projection of a symmetric matrix
Negative part of a symmetric matrix

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assign each block \(X_k\) to a worker and compute \(X_k=Q_k\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_k)Q_k^\top\). Replace the eigenvalues componentwise by \((\lambda_k)_+=\max\{\lambda_k,0\}\), and return \(\Pi_+(X_k)=Q_k\operatorname{diag}((\lambda_k)_+)Q_k^\top\). Assemble \[\Pi_+(X)=\operatorname{diag}\bigl(\Pi_+(X_1),\ldots,\Pi_+(X_q)\bigr).\] Stop the enclosing solver when its global residual criteria hold; blockwise PSD infeasibility may be measured by \(\max_k\|(X_k)_-\|_F\). With concurrent dense eigensolvers, the arithmetic work is \(O(\sum_kn_k^3)\) and the ideal critical path is \(O(\max_kn_k^3)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Project each diagonal block onto its PSD cone independently, assemble the projected blocks, and aggregate block infeasibility; ideal parallel latency is set by the largest block.
knowledge_statements.title: Block-Parallel PSD Computation

assumptions_latex: Agents communicate over a connected undirected graph.
Each local objective \(f_i\) is closed, proper, and convex, and a saddle point exists.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A converged iterate with vanishing primal and dual residuals satisfies consensus and the first-order optimality conditions for \(\min_z\sum_i f_i(z)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Synchronous consensus ADMM for distributed convex subproblems arising from SDP decomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(z^0\), scaled multipliers \(u_i^0\), and choose \(\rho>0\). At iteration \(t\), every agent computes \[x_i^{t+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x_i}\left\{f_i(x_i)+\frac{\rho}{2}\|x_i-z^t+u_i^t\|_2^2\right\}.\] Aggregate the local copies to update \(z^{t+1}=N^{-1}\sum_i(x_i^{t+1}+u_i^t)\), then set \(u_i^{t+1}=u_i^t+x_i^{t+1}-z^{t+1}\). Stop when the primal residuals \(x_i^{t+1}-z^{t+1}\) and the dual residual \(\rho(z^{t+1}-z^t)\) meet prescribed tolerances; output \(z^{t+1}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Agents solve local penalized subproblems, average their copies into a consensus variable, update multipliers, and stop when primal disagreement and dual motion are sufficiently small.
knowledge_statements.title: Distributed Consensus Execution

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed update is centralized consensus ADMM with a global average; a merely connected communication graph does not specify how that average is computed. A dedicated consensus-ADMM source and precise communication and convergence assumptions are required.

children.title: Accelerator Factor Kernels
children.top_down_role: Accelerated dense or structured factor operations used by large-scale SDP execution.

assumptions_latex: A PSD block is represented by a factor \(Y\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}\) with \(r\ll n\).
The objective and constraints are differentiable functions of \(X=YY^\top\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Matrix-free factor kernels evaluate products and gradients without forming the dense \(n\times n\) matrix \(YY^\top\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: low-rank Gram and chain-rule kernels
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dense accelerator kernels for low-rank factored PSD variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Store \(Y\) on the accelerator and represent \(X\) implicitly as \(YY^\top\). Evaluate Gram quantities by matrix multiplication, linear measurements by contractions such as \(\langle A_i,YY^\top\rangle=\operatorname{tr}(Y^\top A_iY)\), and matrix-vector products by \(Xv=Y(Y^\top v)\). If \(F\) is differentiable and \(G=\nabla_XF(YY^\top)\) is symmetric, compute \(\nabla_YF(YY^\top)=2GY\). Apply the chosen factor update to \(Y\), and stop according to the enclosing solver's feasibility and stationarity tests; output the factor or materialize \(YY^\top\) only when required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Keep a low-rank PSD factor on the accelerator and use matrix multiplications and contractions to evaluate measurements, products, and gradients without materializing the full matrix.
knowledge_statements.title: Accelerator Factor Kernels

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Gram, contraction, matrix-vector, and symmetric chain-rule formulas are standard, but no source supports their accelerator-specific execution framing or the complete kernel record.

children.title: Accelerator Spectral Kernels
children.top_down_role: Accelerated eigenvalue, eigenspace, or spectral-transformation workloads.

assumptions_latex: The input \(X\in\mathbb S^n\) is stored on the accelerator.
A symmetric eigensolver returns \(X=Q\operatorname{diag}(\lambda)Q^\top\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Eigenvalue clipping computes the exact Euclidean PSD projection in exact arithmetic.
review_flags: accelerator execution details require dedicated source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Accelerator-resident symmetric eigendecomposition and PSD projection kernel.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Transfer or retain \(X\in\mathbb S^n\) in device memory, compute a symmetric eigendecomposition \(X=Q\operatorname{diag}(\lambda)Q^\top\), and clip eigenvalues by \(\lambda_i^+=\max\{\lambda_i,0\}\). Reconstruct \[\Pi_+(X)=Q\operatorname{diag}(\lambda^+)Q^\top,\] which minimizes \(\|Z-X\|_F\) over \(Z\succeq0\). For a PSD feasibility test, return \(\min_i\lambda_i\) or \(\|\min(\lambda,0)\|_2\). The enclosing optimization method determines the stopping tolerance and whether eigenvectors, projected matrices, or only spectral diagnostics are returned to host memory.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compute a symmetric eigendecomposition on the accelerator, clip negative eigenvalues, and reconstruct the exact Frobenius-norm PSD projection or return spectral feasibility diagnostics.
knowledge_statements.title: Accelerator Spectral Kernels

children.title: Device Data-Movement Bottlenecks
children.top_down_role: Transfer costs between host memory, device memory, or multiple accelerators.

assumptions_latex: \(F>0\) floating-point operations and \(Q>0\) bytes must be executed and transferred, respectively.
\(P>0\) and \(B>0\) are sustained device throughput and limiting-interface bandwidth.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T\ge \max\{F/P,Q/B\}\), and \(F/Q<P/B\) implies a data-movement lower bound dominates.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard roofline lower bound for accelerator kernels
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Roofline boundary for an SDP factorization or spectral kernel on one limiting device interface.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider an accelerator kernel requiring \(F\) floating-point operations and unavoidable movement of \(Q\) bytes across a limiting memory or interconnect interface. If sustained arithmetic throughput is at most \(P\) operations per second and sustained bandwidth is at most \(B\) bytes per second, then every execution satisfies \[T\geq \max\!\left\{\frac{F}{P},\frac{Q}{B}\right\}.\] With arithmetic intensity \(I=F/Q\), the bandwidth term dominates whenever \(I<P/B\). Consequently, increasing arithmetic throughput alone cannot reduce this lower bound unless data reuse increases \(I\) or the transferred volume \(Q\) decreases.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A kernel is bandwidth-bound when its arithmetic intensity lies below the device throughput-to-bandwidth ratio; additional compute capacity then cannot overcome required data transfers.
knowledge_statements.title: Device Data-Movement Bottlenecks

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The roofline lower bound and the selected complexity-bound role fit the device data-movement container, but no inspectable source is supplied for the nontrivial performance claim.

children.title: Reduced-Precision Regimes
children.top_down_role: Execution settings using reduced precision for factor or spectral computation.

assumptions_latex: \(n,m\in\mathbb N\), \(C,X,S\in\mathbb S^n\), \(b,y\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(\mathcal A:\mathbb S^n\to\mathbb R^m\) is linear with adjoint \(\mathcal A^*:\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb S^n\).
The certification tolerances \(\tau_p,\tau_d,\tau_c,\tau_K\geq0\) and the norms used for the residual tests are fixed in advance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A reduced-precision candidate is admissible only if independently evaluated primal, dual, gap, and cone violations satisfy the prescribed tolerances.

notation.meaning: Linear constraint map and its adjoint

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: residual-based acceptance of mixed-precision conic iterates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Acceptance condition for mixed-precision SDP computation with higher-precision final checks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C,X,S\in\mathbb S^n\), \(b,y\in\mathbb R^m\), and let \(\mathcal A:\mathbb S^n\to\mathbb R^m\) be linear with adjoint \(\mathcal A^*:\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb S^n\). For the primal-dual SDP equations \(\mathcal A(X)=b\), \(\mathcal A^*(y)+S=C\), and \(X,S\succeq0\), a reduced-precision result \((\widehat X,\widehat y,\widehat S)\) is admissible at fixed tolerances \((\tau_p,\tau_d,\tau_c,\tau_K)\) only if an independent evaluation satisfies \[\|\mathcal A(\widehat X)-b\|\leq\tau_p,\qquad \|\mathcal A^*(\widehat y)+\widehat S-C\|\leq\tau_d,\] \[|\langle C,\widehat X\rangle-b^T\widehat y|\leq\tau_c,\qquad \lambda_{\min}(\widehat X)\geq-\tau_K,\qquad \lambda_{\min}(\widehat S)\geq-\tau_K.\] The independent evaluation must use precision for which the rounding-error bound in each reported quantity is smaller than its corresponding tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A reduced-precision SDP candidate is admissible only when an independent, sufficiently accurate evaluation confirms the prescribed primal, dual, gap, and positive-semidefiniteness tolerances.
knowledge_statements.title: Reduced-Precision Regimes

children.title: Accelerator-Utilization Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Problem sizes or structures that produce poor device occupancy or limited acceleration.

assumptions_latex: The kernel has work \(F>0\), traffic \(Q>0\), and nonoverlappable latency \(L\geq0\).
Device limits are throughput \(P>0\) and bandwidth \(B>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(U\leq\min\{1,IB/P,F/(PL)\}\) when \(L>0\); low intensity or insufficient work prevents full utilization.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: roofline bound augmented by an unavoidable latency term
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary throughput, bandwidth, and granularity conditions for accelerator saturation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose an accelerator kernel performs \(F>0\) operations, transfers \(Q>0\) bytes, and incurs nonoverlappable launch or synchronization latency \(L\geq0\). For throughput and bandwidth limits \(P>0\) and \(B>0\), its execution time obeys \[T\geq\max\!\left\{\frac{F}{P},\frac{Q}{B},L\right\}.\] Hence the compute utilization \(U=F/(PT)\) satisfies, when \(L>0\), \[U\leq\min\!\left\{1,\frac{IB}{P},\frac{F}{PL}\right\},\qquad I=\frac{F}{Q}.\] When \(L=0\), the last term is omitted. Full compute utilization therefore requires \(I\geq P/B\) and, when \(L>0\), \(F\geq PL\); violation of either applicable condition is an accelerator-utilization boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Full accelerator utilization requires sufficient arithmetic intensity and, when nonoverlappable latency is positive, enough work to amortize that latency; bandwidth or launch overhead otherwise imposes a utilization ceiling.
knowledge_statements.title: Accelerator-Utilization Boundaries

assumptions_latex: \(T=(T_1,\ldots,T_m)\) is a block contraction with modulus \(q<1\).
Every block is updated infinitely often and all read delays are bounded by \(D<\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The asynchronous block iterates converge to the unique fixed point \(x^*=T(x^*)\).
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bounded-delay asynchronous block iteration applicable to separable SDP computational blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(x^0=(x_1^0,\ldots,x_m^0)\). At update \(k\), a worker selects block \(i_k\), reads a delayed vector \(\widetilde x^k\) with components \(\widetilde x_j^k=x_j^{k-d_{k,j}}\), where \(0\leq d_{k,j}\leq D\), and performs \[x_{i_k}^{k+1}=T_{i_k}(\widetilde x^k),\qquad x_j^{k+1}=x_j^k\quad(j\neq i_k).\] Stop when a consistently evaluated fixed-point residual satisfies \(\|x^k-T(x^k)\|\leq\varepsilon\), and output \(x^k\). If \(T\) is a contraction, delays are bounded, and every block is updated infinitely often, then the iterates converge to the unique fixed point of \(T\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Workers update blocks using boundedly stale data. Under contraction, bounded delay, and fair block selection, the asynchronous iterates converge to the unique fixed point.
knowledge_statements.title: Asynchronous Execution Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The bounded-delay block-update algorithm and its contraction-based convergence claim fit asynchronous execution regimes, but the convergence theorem has no inspectable citation.

assumptions_latex: The equality constraints are \(\langle A_i,X\rangle=b_i\) for \(i=1,\ldots,m\).
A floor \(\delta>0\) prevents division by zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Scaling by \(d_i=(\max\{\|A_i\|_F,|b_i|,\delta\})^{-1}\) preserves the feasible set and bounds every scaled row datum by one.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-pass row equilibration for equality constraints in standard-form SDP.

source_refs.locator: 1.5 Algorithms and software for SDP p. 21

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given SDP equalities \(\langle A_i,X\rangle=b_i\) and a safeguard \(\delta>0\), compute \[d_i=\frac{1}{\max\{\|A_i\|_F,|b_i|,\delta\}},\qquad \widetilde A_i=d_iA_i,
\qquad \widetilde b_i=d_ib_i.\] Replace each equality by \(\langle\widetilde A_i,X\rangle=\widetilde b_i\), leaving the objective and cone constraint unchanged. Because every \(d_i>0\), the transformed and original equality systems have exactly the same feasible matrices. Moreover, \(\|\widetilde A_i\|_F\leq1\) and \(|\widetilde b_i|\leq1\). The algorithm outputs the scaled data and the diagonal row-scaling matrix \(D=\operatorname{diag}(d_1,\ldots,d_m)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each equality is divided by a safeguarded measure of its matrix and right-hand-side magnitude, preserving feasibility while limiting row-scale variation.
knowledge_statements.title: Constraint Equilibration

children.title: Cone Scaling
children.top_down_role: Scaling choices associated with the ambient semidefinite cone or cone components.

assumptions_latex: \(K=\mathbb S_+^n\) and \(W\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) is nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X\mapsto WXW^T\) is a cone automorphism, with dual slack transformation \(S\mapsto W^{-T}SW^{-1}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Congruence scaling of a single positive-semidefinite cone block.

source_refs.locator: 4.4 Symmetries, Dual Cones, and Facial Structure p. 167
source_refs.source_title: Semidefinite Optimization and Convex Algebraic Geometry

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a nonsingular matrix \(W\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), define the primal scaling \(T_W:\mathbb S^n\to\mathbb S^n\) by \[T_W(X)=WXW^T.\] Then \(T_W(\mathbb S_+^n)=\mathbb S_+^n\), and its inverse is \(T_{W^{-1}}\). To preserve the trace pairing, transform a dual slack by \(S\mapsto T_W^{-*}(S)=W^{-T}SW^{-1}\); consequently, \[\langle W^{-T}SW^{-1},WXW^T\rangle=\langle S,X\rangle.\] Thus congruence scaling preserves primal and dual cone membership, complementarity pairing, and feasibility after the linear operator and objective data are transformed consistently.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonsingular congruence maps the PSD cone onto itself. Applying the inverse-adjoint congruence to dual slacks preserves the primal-dual trace pairing.
knowledge_statements.title: Cone Scaling

children.title: Block Scaling
children.top_down_role: Scaling choices applied separately to PSD blocks or decomposed matrix components.

assumptions_latex: \(K=K_1\times\cdots\times K_p\) is a product cone.
Each \(T_j\) is an invertible automorphism of \(K_j\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The block-diagonal map \(T=\operatorname{diag}(T_1,\ldots,T_p)\) is an automorphism of \(K\) and preserves block separability.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: direct product of cone automorphisms
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Independent automorphic scaling of blocks in a product-cone formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K=K_1\times\cdots\times K_p\) and let each invertible linear map \(T_j\) satisfy \(T_j(K_j)=K_j\). Define \[T(x_1,\ldots,x_p)=(T_1x_1,\ldots,T_px_p).\] Then \(T(K)=K\), \(T^{-1}=\operatorname{diag}(T_1^{-1},\ldots,T_p^{-1})\), and the dual variable must transform as \(s\mapsto T^{-*}s\). The identity \[\langle T^{-*}s,Tx\rangle=\langle s,x\rangle\] preserves complementarity. For a constraint operator \(A\), the scaled formulation uses \(A T^{-1}\); hence block scaling changes numerical coordinates without changing the represented feasible set or destroying product-cone separability.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent automorphisms of product-cone blocks combine into a block-diagonal cone automorphism, with inverse-adjoint dual scaling preserving complementarity.
knowledge_statements.title: Block Scaling

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The direct product of block automorphisms is a valid block-scaling representation and preserves product-cone separability, but no inspectable source is supplied.

children.title: Cross-Block Scale Disparity
children.top_down_role: Numerical behavior when decomposed blocks have substantially different magnitudes.

assumptions_latex:
Positive characteristic block scales \(s_1,
\ldots,s_p\) are measured in a common norm convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho=\max_js_j/\min_js_j\ge1\), with \(\rho=1\) exactly when all block scales agree.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: max-to-min ratio as a scale disparity measure
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dimensionless disparity measure for product-cone block data under one fixed norm convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For product-cone blocks indexed by \(j=1,
\ldots,p\), assign each block a positive characteristic scale \(s_j\), computed using the same norm convention from its operator, objective, or iterate data. The cross-block scale disparity is \[\rho=\frac{\max_{1\leq j\leq p}s_j}{\min_{1\leq j\leq p}s_j}.\] It satisfies \(\rho\geq1\), is invariant under multiplying every \(s_j\) by the same positive scalar, and equals one exactly when all characteristic scales coincide. A family has bounded cross-block disparity when \(\rho\leq\bar\rho\) for a prescribed finite threshold \(\bar\rho\); otherwise it is scale-disparate at that threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cross-block scale disparity is the largest characteristic block scale divided by the smallest, using one common norm convention; it is unchanged by uniform rescaling.
knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Block Scale Disparity

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The max-to-min ratio is a coherent definition once positive characteristic scales and a common convention are fixed, and the definition fits the container. No source is supplied for the chosen terminology and threshold convention.

children.title: Multi-Cone Scaling Compatibility
children.top_down_role: Compatibility of scaling choices across heterogeneous cone components.

assumptions_latex: \(K=\prod_{j=1}^pK_j\) and \(T=\operatorname{diag}(T_1,\ldots,T_p)\) is invertible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The scaling is compatible precisely when \(T_j(K_j)=K_j\) for every block and dual data use \(T^{-*}\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: compatibility follows from product-cone automorphisms and inverse-adjoint dual transformation
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compatibility predicate for independently scaling heterogeneous cone blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A block-diagonal scaling \(T=
\operatorname{diag}(T_1,\ldots,T_p)\) is compatible with the product cone \(K=K_1\times\cdots\times K_p\) when \[T_j(K_j)=K_j\quad\text{for every }j,\qquad s'=T^{-*}s,\qquad A'=AT^{-1}.\] Under these conditions, \(x\in K\) if and only if \(Tx\in K\), \(s\in K^*\) if and only if \(T^{-*}s\in K^*\), and \(\langle s',Tx\rangle=\langle s,x\rangle\). Thus the scaled equality \(A'(Tx)=b\) represents the original equality \(Ax=b\), even when the blocks belong to different cone families.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multi-cone scaling is compatible when every block map preserves its cone and the operator and dual variables receive the corresponding inverse transformations.
knowledge_statements.title: Multi-Cone Scaling Compatibility

children.title: Scaling-Induced Conditioning Loss
children.top_down_role: Cases where chosen scales worsen conditioning or obscure residual interpretation.

assumptions_latex: \(H\in\mathbb S^n\) satisfies \(H\succ0\), and \(S\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) is nonsingular.
Condition numbers use the Euclidean operator norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\kappa_2(H)/\kappa_2(S)^2\leq\kappa_2(S^THS)\leq\kappa_2(H)\kappa_2(S)^2\), and the upper growth factor is attained by an explicitly parameterized family.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard condition-number bounds under congruence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp conditioning loss possible under a nonsingular congruence scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\in\mathbb S^n\) satisfy \(H\succ0\), and let \(S\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) be nonsingular. In the Euclidean operator norm, congruence scaling obeys \[\frac{\kappa_2(H)}{\kappa_2(S)^2}\leq\kappa_2(S^THS)\leq\kappa_2(H)\kappa_2(S)^2.\] Therefore a scaling with large \(\kappa_2(S)\) can worsen conditioning by a quadratic factor even though it preserves positive definiteness. The upper growth factor is attained for \(H=I_2\), \(S=\operatorname{diag}(1,\epsilon)\), and \(0<\epsilon\leq1\), because \(\kappa_2(H)=1\) and \(\kappa_2(S^THS)=\epsilon^{-2}=\kappa_2(S)^2\). Thus invertibility and cone preservation alone do not ensure numerical improvement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A badly conditioned coordinate scaling can worsen the transformed system's condition number by the square of the scaling condition number; a two-dimensional diagonal family attains this growth.
knowledge_statements.title: Scaling-Induced Conditioning Loss

assumptions_latex: The Schur-complement matrix \(H\in\mathbb S^m\) and preconditioner \(M\in\mathbb S^m\) satisfy \(H\succ0\) and \(M\succ0\).
Preconditioned conjugate gradients is applied in exact arithmetic to the symmetrically preconditioned system.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The symmetric transformation is equivalent to \(H\Delta y=r\), and the reconstructed iterates satisfy the standard energy-norm convergence bound governed by \(\kappa_2(M^{-1/2}HM^{-1/2})\).

notation.meaning: Error in the reconstructed Schur-system iterate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Symmetric preconditioning and its conjugate-gradient convergence bound for a positive-definite SDP Schur-complement equation.

source_refs.locator: 1.5 Algorithms and software for SDP p. 21
source_refs.source_title: Advances in Linear Matrix Inequality Methods in Control

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\in\mathbb S^m\) satisfy \(H\succ0\), let \(M\in\mathbb S^m\) satisfy \(M\succ0\), and consider \(H\Delta y=r\) with exact solution \(\Delta y_*\). Introducing \(z=M^{1/2}\Delta y\) gives the equivalent symmetrically preconditioned equation \[M^{-1/2}HM^{-1/2}z=M^{-1/2}r,\qquad \Delta y=M^{-1/2}z.\] Its matrix is positive definite. Let \(z_k\) be the conjugate-gradient iterate for this transformed system, define \(\Delta y_k=M^{-1/2}z_k\), \(e_k=\Delta y_k-\Delta y_*\), and \(\|v\|_H=(v^THv)^{1/2}\). In exact arithmetic, with \(\kappa=\kappa_2(M^{-1/2}HM^{-1/2})\), \[\frac{\|e_k\|_H}{\|e_0\|_H}\leq2\left(\frac{\sqrt\kappa-1}{\sqrt\kappa+1}\right)^k.\] Thus an easily applicable preconditioner is effective when it makes \(\kappa\) small.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Symmetric SPD preconditioning produces an equivalent Schur system. In exact arithmetic, the reconstructed conjugate-gradient iterates obey the standard energy-norm bound determined by the transformed matrix's condition number.
knowledge_statements.title: Schur-System Preconditioning

source_witnesses.locator: 1.5 Algorithms and software for SDP p. 21
source_witnesses.source_title: Advances in Linear Matrix Inequality Methods in Control

assumptions_latex: \(H\succ0\) has eigenpairs \((\lambda_i,u_i)\) ordered \(\lambda_1\geq\cdots\geq\lambda_n>0\).
An integer \(0\leq r<n\) and baseline \(\alpha>0\) are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The rank-\(r\) spectral preconditioner maps the selected eigenvalues to one and the remaining eigenvalues to \(\lambda_i/\alpha\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: exact eigenvalue action of a low-rank spectral preconditioner
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact low-rank spectral correction for a positive-definite linear system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H=\sum_{i=1}^n\lambda_i u_i u_i^T\succ0\), where the eigenvectors are orthonormal and \(\lambda_1\geq\cdots\geq\lambda_n>0\). For \(0\leq r<n\) and \(\alpha>0\), define \[M_r=\alpha I+\sum_{i=1}^r(\lambda_i-\alpha)u_i u_i^T.\] Then \(M_r\succ0\), and \(M_r^{-1}H\) has eigenvalue \(1\) on \(\operatorname{span}\{u_1,\ldots,u_r\}\) and eigenvalue \(\lambda_i/\alpha\) on \(u_i\) for \(i>r\). Hence \[\kappa_2(M_r^{-1/2}HM_r^{-1/2})=\frac{\max\{1,\max_{i>r}\lambda_i/\alpha\}}{\min\{1,\min_{i>r}\lambda_i/\alpha\}}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A low-rank spectral correction exactly normalizes selected eigenmodes; the uncorrected eigenvalues are scaled by a positive baseline parameter.
knowledge_statements.title: Spectral Preconditioning

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The low-rank spectral preconditioner and its eigenvalue action are mathematically precise and fit spectral preconditioning, but no inspectable source supports the construction or condition-number formula.

knowledge_statements.title: Operator-Based Primal–Dual Residuals
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residuals for the standard equality-form primal-dual SDP pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\mathcal A:\mathbb S^n\to\mathbb R^m\), primal-dual candidates \(X,S\in\mathbb S^n\) and \(y\in\mathbb R^m\), define \(r_p:=\mathcal A(X)-b\), \(r_d:=C-\mathcal A^*(y)-S\), \(r_c:=\langle X,S\rangle\), \(v_X:=\max\{0,-\lambda_{\min}(X)\}\), and \(v_S:=\max\{0,-\lambda_{\min}(S)\}\). Primal feasibility is equivalent to \(r_p=0\) and \(v_X=0\); dual feasibility is equivalent to \(r_d=0\) and \(v_S=0\). For a primal-dual feasible triple, \(r_c\geq0\), and \(r_c=0\) is equivalent to zero primal-dual objective gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Operator and cone residuals jointly characterize primal and dual feasibility; for a feasible primal-dual triple, the complementarity residual equals the nonnegative objective gap and vanishes exactly when that gap is zero.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal A:\mathbb S^n\to\mathbb R^m\) is linear, with adjoint \(\mathcal A^*\).
The primal problem is \(\min\{\langle C,X\rangle:\mathcal A(X)=b,\ X\succeq0\}\), and the dual problem is \(\max\{b^Ty:C-\mathcal A^*(y)=S,\ S\succeq0\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Primal feasibility is characterized by \(r_p=0\) and \(v_X=0\), dual feasibility by \(r_d=0\) and \(v_S=0\), and zero gap for a feasible triple by \(r_c=0\).

children.title: Objective-Gap Certificates
children.top_down_role: Certificate interfaces based on reported primal–dual objective separation.

knowledge_statements.title: Objective-Gap Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact-feasibility objective-gap certificate for an equality-form primal minimization SDP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a primal-feasible \(X\in\mathbb S^n\) and a dual-feasible pair \((y,S)\in\mathbb R^m\times\mathbb S^n\), weak duality gives \(b^Ty\leq p^\star\leq\langle C,X\rangle\). The computable gap is \[\Delta:=\langle C,X\rangle-b^Ty=\langle X,S\rangle\geq0.\] Consequently, \(0\leq\langle C,X\rangle-p^\star\leq\Delta\) and \(0\leq p^\star-b^Ty\leq\Delta\). Thus \(\Delta\leq\varepsilon\) certifies absolute objective error at most \(\varepsilon\) for both feasible objective values.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible primal-dual pair brackets the finite primal optimum, and its nonnegative objective gap bounds the absolute suboptimality of both objective values.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal A:\mathbb S^n\to\mathbb R^m\) is linear, and the primal problem is \(\min\{\langle C,X\rangle:\mathcal A(X)=b,\ X\succeq0\}\).
The dual problem is \(\max\{b^Ty:C-\mathcal A^*(y)=S,\ S\succeq0\}\).
\(X\) is primal feasible, \((y,S)\) is dual feasible, and the primal optimal value \(p^\star\) is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The verifiable quantity \(\Delta=\langle X,S\rangle\) satisfies \(0\leq\langle C,X\rangle-p^\star\leq\Delta\) and \(0\leq p^\star-b^Ty\leq\Delta\).

knowledge_statements.title: Dual-Bound Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lower-bound certificate for a primal minimization SDP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the primal SDP \(p^\star:=\inf\{\langle C,X\rangle:\mathcal A(X)=b,\ X\succeq0\}\), a dual-bound certificate consists of \(y\in\mathbb R^m\) and \(S\in\mathbb S^n\) satisfying \(C-\mathcal A^*(y)=S\) and \(S\succeq0\), together with \(L:=b^Ty\). It certifies \(L\leq\langle C,X\rangle\) for every primal-feasible \(X\), and hence \(L\leq p^\star\). Strong duality is not required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exactly dual-feasible point supplies a rigorous lower bound for every primal-feasible objective value and for the primal optimum, without requiring strong duality.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal A:\mathbb S^n\to\mathbb R^m\) is linear, with adjoint \(\mathcal A^*\).
The primal problem is \(p^\star:=\inf\{\langle C,X\rangle:\mathcal A(X)=b,\ X\succeq0\}\), and its feasible set is nonempty.
\((y,S)\in\mathbb R^m\times\mathbb S^n\) satisfies \(C-\mathcal A^*(y)=S\) and \(S\succeq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The scalar \(L=b^Ty\) satisfies \(L\leq\langle C,X\rangle\) for every primal-feasible \(X\), and therefore \(L\leq p^\star\).

knowledge_statements.title: Gap–Bound Consistency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic consistency test for exact primal and dual certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a primal-feasible \(X\in\mathbb S^n\) and dual-feasible \((y,S)\in\mathbb R^m\times\mathbb S^n\), define \(U:=\langle C,X\rangle\), \(L:=b^Ty\), and \(\Delta:=\langle X,S\rangle\). These quantities satisfy \[U-L=\Delta\geq0.\] Therefore, a reported triple \((U,L,\Delta)\) from exact feasible certificates is gap-bound consistent only if \(L\leq U\) and \(U-L=\Delta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact primal and dual certificates must report a nonnegative bound difference equal to their complementarity inner product.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal A:\mathbb S^n\to\mathbb R^m\) is linear, and the primal problem is \(\min\{\langle C,X\rangle:\mathcal A(X)=b,\ X\succeq0\}\).
The dual problem is \(\max\{b^Ty:C-\mathcal A^*(y)=S,\ S\succeq0\}\).
\(X\) is primal feasible and \((y,S)\) is dual feasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The exact certificate quantities satisfy \(L\leq U\) and \(U-L=\Delta\geq0\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min\{X_{22}:X_{11}=1,\ X\succeq0\}\). Its optimum is \(p^\star=0\), attained by \(X=\operatorname{diag}(1,0)\). With \(C=\operatorname{diag}(0,1)\), the dual constraint is \(C-yE_{11}\succeq0\), equivalently \(y\leq0\). For every \(M>0\), choosing \(y=-M\) is dual feasible and therefore certifies the valid lower bound \(-M\), but its distance from the optimum is \(M\). Hence exact dual feasibility and strong duality do not prevent arbitrarily weak bounds; usefulness additionally requires a small certified primal-dual gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Even with strong duality, a dual-feasible point can give an arbitrarily poor lower bound; a small gap is needed for an informative certificate.

assumptions_latex: A parallel iteration has computation time \(T_{\mathrm{comp}}(p)\) and communication time \(T_{\mathrm{comm}}(p)\) on \(p\) workers.
