knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The iteration is communication dominated when \(T_{\mathrm{comm}}(p)\geq T_{\mathrm{comp}}(p)\).
review_flags: latency-bandwidth model not supported by supplied locators
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Critical-path condition for communication-dominated parallel SDP execution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T_p:=T_{\mathrm{comp}}(p)+T_{\mathrm{comm}}(p)\) be the nonoverlapped critical-path time of one parallel SDP iteration on \(p\) workers. The iteration is communication dominated when \(T_{\mathrm{comm}}(p)\geq T_{\mathrm{comp}}(p)\), equivalently when communication contributes at least one half of \(T_p\). Under the latency-bandwidth model \(T_{\mathrm{comm}}(p)=\alpha m(p)+\beta w(p)\), where \(m(p)\) is the number of messages and \(w(p)\) the communicated words, increasing \(p\) cannot materially reduce iteration time unless it also reduces or overlaps this communication term.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Parallel execution is communication dominated when message latency and data movement consume at least as much critical-path time as local computation.
knowledge_statements.title: Communication-Dominated Parallelism

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition is plausible and correctly placed in the failure taxonomy, but no source supports the latency-bandwidth model or the conclusion about increasing worker count and material iteration-time reduction.

assumptions_latex: PSD block \(i\) has assigned processing cost \(w_i\geq0\).
A static assignment partitions the blocks into worker sets \(I_1,\ldots,I_p\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The assignment is imbalanced by factor \(\rho:=p\max_j L_j/\sum_jL_j\), with perfect balance exactly when \(\rho=1\).
review_flags: cost proxy for PSD-block processing requires algorithm-specific sourcing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Static load imbalance measured from heterogeneous PSD-block costs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For PSD blocks with nonnegative processing costs \(w_1,\ldots,w_q\), let worker \(j\) receive block set \(I_j\) and load \(L_j:=\sum_{i\in I_j}w_i\). Provided \(\sum_jL_j>0\), define the imbalance factor \[\rho:=\frac{p\max_{1\leq j\leq p}L_j}{\sum_{j=1}^pL_j}\geq1.\] Perfect balance holds exactly when \(\rho=1\). With a barrier after block processing and negligible overlap, the phase time is at least \(\max_jL_j\), so the utilization attributable to this assignment is at most \(1/\rho\). Large heterogeneous blocks can therefore determine the critical path even when total work is well distributed by block count.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: PSD-block scheduling is load imbalanced when the most heavily loaded worker substantially exceeds average load, limiting utilization at synchronization points.
knowledge_statements.title: Load Imbalance Across PSD Blocks

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The imbalance ratio is mathematically coherent and the condition kind fits the leaf, but the PSD-block cost proxy, barrier model, and utilization conclusion require an algorithm-specific parallel scheduling source.

assumptions_latex: Iteration \(k\) performs dense symmetric factorizations or eigendecompositions of PSD blocks having orders \(n_{k,1},\ldots,n_{k,q_k}\).
Each full dense spectral factorization uses cubic arithmetic in its block order.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The cumulative dense spectral work is \(\Theta\!\left(\sum_k\sum_i n_{k,i}^3\right)\).

notation.meaning: Order of spectral block \(i\) at iteration \(k\)

review_flags: algorithm-specific reuse and partial-spectrum assumptions are unspecified
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dense-arithmetic cost of repeatedly factoring large PSD blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose iteration \(k\) performs a full dense symmetric factorization or eigendecomposition of every PSD block with orders \(n_{k,1},\ldots,n_{k,q_k}\). In the dense-arithmetic model, the spectral work through \(K\) iterations is \[W_{\mathrm{spec}}=\Theta\!\left(\sum_{k=1}^{K}\sum_{i=1}^{q_k}n_{k,i}^3\right),\] with storage \(\Theta(\max_{k,i}n_{k,i}^2)\) per sequentially processed block. If one block has order \(N_k\) and \(N_k^3\) dominates all other iteration costs, repeated factorization of that block is the asymptotic execution bottleneck unless structure, reuse, or partial spectral computation lowers the cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeated full dense factorizations of PSD blocks accumulate cubic work in each block order and can dominate execution when a large block recurs.
knowledge_statements.title: Repeated Large Spectral Factorizations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity_bound kind fits the leaf, but no numerical-linear-algebra source is supplied for the dense spectral cost and storage bounds. The bottleneck conclusion also depends on the stated no-reuse and full-spectrum model.

assumptions_latex: Preconditioner construction costs \(T_{\mathrm{setup}}\) and each of \(K\) preconditioned iterations costs \(T_{\mathrm{iter}}\).
All other solve costs total \(T_{\mathrm{other}}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Setup dominates total solve time exactly when \(T_{\mathrm{setup}}>KT_{\mathrm{iter}}+T_{\mathrm{other}}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Runtime condition identifying unamortized preconditioner construction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For one linear solve, write total time as \(T_{\mathrm{solve}}:=T_{\mathrm{setup}}+KT_{\mathrm{iter}}+T_{\mathrm{other}}\), where \(T_{\mathrm{setup}}\) constructs the preconditioner, \(K\) is the number of preconditioned iterations, and \(T_{\mathrm{other}}\) contains remaining work. Preconditioner setup dominates when \[T_{\mathrm{setup}}>KT_{\mathrm{iter}}+T_{\mathrm{other}},\] equivalently when it exceeds one half of \(T_{\mathrm{solve}}\). If a reusable setup serves \(R\) comparable solves, its amortized contribution is \(T_{\mathrm{setup}}/R\); setup dominance then persists precisely when \(T_{\mathrm{setup}}/R>KT_{\mathrm{iter}}+T_{\mathrm{other}}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Preconditioner setup dominates when its construction time exceeds all subsequent iteration and ancillary costs, after accounting for reuse across solves.
knowledge_statements.title: Preconditioner-Setup Dominance

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The timing inequality is internally consistent and condition is the correct role, but no iterative-SDP source supports the additive timing decomposition, comparability across reused solves, or the claimed precise amortized dominance criterion.

assumptions_latex: \(C_{\mathrm{tot}}=C_{\mathrm{solve}}+C_{\mathrm{cert}}>0\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C_{\mathrm{cert}}\ge \eta C_{\mathrm{tot}}\)

notation.meaning: cost of residual, feasibility, and spectral certificate computations

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A threshold-parametrized execution-cost condition, not a solver-independent complexity theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a fixed implementation, hardware platform, problem instance, and accuracy tolerance, partition the measured execution cost as \(C_{\mathrm{tot}}=C_{\mathrm{solve}}+C_{\mathrm{cert}}\), where certification includes all work performed solely to verify the returned point. Certificate-cost dominance at threshold \(\eta\in(1/2,1]\) holds exactly when \[C_{\mathrm{cert}}\ge \eta C_{\mathrm{tot}}.\] Equivalently, \(C_{\mathrm{cert}}\ge \eta(1-\eta)^{-1}C_{\mathrm{solve}}\) when \(\eta<1\). The condition must use the same resource measure, such as wall time, communication volume, or arithmetic work, for both terms.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Certification cost dominates when, under one fixed resource measure and accuracy target, it exceeds a prescribed majority fraction of total execution cost.
knowledge_statements.title: Certificate-Cost Dominance

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines simultaneous coefficient support on a prescribed graph and existence of a rank-bounded optimum; graph sparsity itself must be assessed separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m,n\in\mathbb N\), \(C,A_1,\ldots,A_m\in\mathbb S^n\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), \(G=(V,E)\) with \(V=\{1,\ldots,n\}\), and \(1\le r\le n\). Consider the attained SDP \[\min_{X\in\mathbb S^n}\ \langle C,X\rangle\quad\text{subject to}\quad \langle A_i,X\rangle=b_i\ \text{ for }i=1,\ldots,m,\qquad X\succeq0.\] It is sparse low-rank relative to \((G,r)\) when every off-diagonal nonzero of \(C,A_1,\ldots,A_m\) corresponds to an edge of \(G\), and at least one optimal solution \(X^\star\) satisfies \(\operatorname{rank}(X^\star)\le r\). The support condition concerns the data, whereas the rank condition concerns an optimal solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relative to a prescribed support graph and rank bound, a sparse low-rank SDP has coefficient matrices supported on that graph and admits an optimal positive-semidefinite matrix of rank at most the bound.

knowledge_statements.title: Chordal SDP Structure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: States the positive-semidefinite completion theorem underlying chordal SDP decomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a chordal graph on \(V=\{1,\ldots,n\}\), with maximal cliques \(K_1,\ldots,K_q\), and let \(Z\in\mathbb S^n(E)\) be a partial symmetric matrix whose diagonal and edge entries are specified. Then \[Z\text{ has a completion }X\succeq0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad Z[K_k,K_k]\succeq0\ \text{ for every }k=1,\ldots,q.\] In a formulation using separate clique copies, copies of entries shared by multiple cliques must satisfy consistency equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a chordal graph, a partial symmetric matrix has a positive-semidefinite completion exactly when every maximal-clique principal submatrix is positive semidefinite; separate clique copies must agree on overlaps.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the nonempty feasible set \(\mathcal F=\{X\in\mathbb S_+^n:\mathcal A(X)=b\}\), primal degenerate geometry in the facial sense means \[\mathcal F\cap\mathbb S_{++}^n=\varnothing.\] Equivalently, the minimal face \(\operatorname{face}(\mathcal F)\) of \(\mathbb S_+^n\) containing \(\mathcal F\) is a proper face. Hence there exist \(r<n\) and a full-column-rank matrix \(U\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}\) such that every feasible matrix has the form \(X=UYU^\top\) with \(Y\succeq0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible SDP is facially degenerate when it has no positive-definite feasible matrix, so its entire feasible set lies in a proper face of the PSD cone.

children.title: Chordality Under Degeneracy

assumptions_latex: \(G\) is the aggregate support graph of \(C,A_1,\ldots,A_m\)
\(\mathcal F\subseteq\mathbb S_+^n\) is nonempty but not strictly feasible
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Chordality of \(G\) is unchanged by degeneracy, but need not be inherited by facially reduced coefficient matrices
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates graph chordality from strict feasibility and from sparsity after facial reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Chordality and facial degeneracy describe different objects. Whether \(G\) is chordal depends only on the zero pattern of the coefficient matrices, whereas failure of strict feasibility depends on the affine feasible set. Consequently, making the feasible set degenerate does not by itself change chordality of \(G\). If facial reduction uses \(X=UYU^\top\), however, the reduced coefficients are \(U^\top C U\) and \(U^\top A_iU\). A dense \(U\) can make these matrices dense, so the original chordal sparsity need not survive in the reduced coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Data-graph chordality is logically independent of strict feasibility, but a dense facial-reduction basis can destroy sparsity in the reduced SDP.
knowledge_statements.title: Chordality Under Degeneracy

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The distinction between data-graph chordality and facial degeneracy is plausible, but the claim about loss of chordal sparsity under facial reduction requires a source addressing their composition.

knowledge_statements.title: Matrix-Free–Sketch Composition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact Nyström reconstruction from matrix-free products under a range-capture condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\in\mathbb S_+^n\) have rank \(r\), and let \(\Omega\in\mathbb R^{n\times k}\), with \(k\ge r\), satisfy \(\operatorname{rank}(X^{1/2}\Omega)=r\). Using only the matrix-free block product, form \(Y=X\Omega\) and the small matrix \(W=\Omega^{\mathsf T}Y\). Then the generalized Nyström reconstruction is exact:
\[
X=Y W^\dagger Y^{\mathsf T}.
\]
Thus a matrix-free application of \(X\) composes with a rank-revealing sketch without explicitly storing the \(n\times n\) matrix; approximate range capture yields the corresponding low-rank approximation rather than this exact identity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A matrix-free block product and a range-capturing sketch exactly reconstruct a positive semidefinite low-rank matrix through a small pseudoinverse.

knowledge_statements.title: Sparsity Without Small Cliques
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Graph sparsity alone does not bound the clique sizes created by chordal conversion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
There exist constants \(c>0\) and bounded-degree graphs \((G_n)\) with \(|V(G_n)|=n\), \(|E(G_n)|=O(n)\), and \(\operatorname{tw}(G_n)\ge cn\). For every chordal extension \(H_n\supseteq G_n\), its largest clique therefore satisfies
\[
\omega(H_n)\ge \operatorname{tw}(G_n)+1\ge cn+1.
\]
Consequently, an SDP whose aggregate sparsity graph is \(G_n\) may be sparse in edge count while every chordal decomposition contains a positive-semidefinite block of order \(\Omega(n)\). Entry sparsity by itself therefore cannot guarantee small clique subproblems or subquadratic storage for all clique matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bounded-degree graphs can have linear treewidth, forcing a linear-size clique in every chordal extension despite having only linearly many edges.
assumptions_latex: G_n\text{ is a bounded-degree graph family}
|V(G_n)|=n,\quad \operatorname{tw}(G_n)\ge cn
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \min_{H_n\supseteq G_n\,\mathrm{chordal}}\omega(H_n)=\Omega(n)

notation.meaning: maximum clique cardinality of graph H

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure_boundary role matches the diagnostic leaf, and the conclusion is consistent with the standard relation between treewidth and minimum maximum-clique size over chordal extensions. No source is supplied for either the existence of bounded-degree linear-treewidth families or the chordal-extension characterization.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(n,r\in\mathbb N\) satisfy \(n\ge r+1\), let \(\varepsilon>0\), and define \(X_0=\operatorname{diag}(I_r,0,0_{n-r-1})\) and \(X_\varepsilon=\operatorname{diag}(I_r,\varepsilon,0_{n-r-1})\). Then \(X_0,X_\varepsilon\in\mathbb S_+^n\), \(\operatorname{rank}(X_0)=r\), \(\operatorname{rank}(X_\varepsilon)=r+1\), and \(\|X_\varepsilon-X_0\|_2=\varepsilon\). In the observation model \(\|\widehat X-X\|_2\le\delta\), no procedure can uniformly identify the exact rank of every positive-semidefinite \(X\) when \(\delta\ge\varepsilon/2\), since one observation can be consistent with both \(X_0\) and \(X_\varepsilon\). Thus low rank alone does not provide stable exact-rank certification under positive norm-bounded uncertainty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive semidefinite matrices of different ranks can be arbitrarily close, and an error radius at least half their separation makes uniform exact-rank identification impossible.

knowledge_statements.title: Sketchability Without Cheap Oracles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compact sketches do not reduce the cost of obtaining matrix–vector products.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider an unknown linear operator \(X:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\) accessed only through queries \(v\mapsto Xv\), each costing \(T_X\), and let \(\Omega\in\mathbb R^{n\times k}\) have rank \(k\). Any deterministic algorithm that must determine \(Y=X\Omega\) exactly for every \(X\) requires at least \(k\) oracle queries: fewer queries leave a nonzero direction in \(\operatorname{range}(\Omega)\) on which two admissible operators can agree on all queried vectors but differ. Therefore forming the sketch costs at least \(kT_X\) in this oracle model, even though storing \(Y\) requires only \(nk\) scalars.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sketch may be compact yet expensive to form: an exact rank-k range sketch needs at least k costly operator applications in the basic oracle model.

X\text{ is an arbitrary linear operator}
\text{one oracle query returns }Xv\text{ for one }v
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N_{\mathrm{queries}}(X\Omega)\ge k,\quad \operatorname{cost}(X\Omega)\ge kT_X

knowledge_statements.title: Parallelism Without Low Communication
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact dense aggregation remains communication-intensive despite perfect local parallelism.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(p\ge2\) workers hold arbitrary symmetric matrices \(S_i\in\mathbb S^n\), and suppose a coordinator must compute \(S=\sum_{i=1}^p S_i\) exactly. In the coordinator model, where workers do not communicate with one another and one word carries one scalar, each noncoordinator worker must transmit \(d=n(n+1)/2\) words in the worst case: with all other inputs fixed, its arbitrary \(d\)-dimensional contribution must remain distinguishable. Thus exact dense aggregation requires at least
\[
(p-1)d=\Omega(pn^2)
\]
communicated words, even when all local matrix computations are performed concurrently.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Parallel local matrix work does not ensure low communication: exact aggregation of arbitrary dense symmetric matrices costs quadratically many words per contributing worker.
assumptions_latex: p\ge2
S_i\in\mathbb S^n\text{ is arbitrary for each worker}
\text{communication uses scalar words in a coordinator model}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: W_{\mathrm{comm}}\ge (p-1)n(n+1)/2=\Omega(pn^2)

No source is supplied to fix and support the model-specific bound.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(n,r\in\mathbb N\) satisfy \(1\le r\le n\), and let \(V\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}\) have full column rank. Define \(\mathcal L_V:\mathbb S^r\to\mathbb S^n\) by \(\mathcal L_V(Z)=VZV^{\mathsf T}\), with both spaces equipped with the Frobenius norm. The largest and smallest singular gains of \(\mathcal L_V\) are \(\sigma_{\max}(V)^2\) and \(\sigma_{\min}(V)^2\), respectively, so
\[
\operatorname{cond}_F(\mathcal L_V)=\frac{\sigma_{\max}(V)^2}{\sigma_{\min}(V)^2}=\kappa_2(V)^2.
\]
Consequently, inversion on \(\operatorname{range}(\mathcal L_V)\) can amplify absolute perturbations by \(\sigma_{\min}(V)^{-2}\), while the worst-case relative sensitivity of the parameterization is \(\kappa_2(V)^2\). Dimension reduction therefore does not ensure numerical stability when the reduction basis is ill conditioned.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the Frobenius-norm map sending reduced coordinates Z to VZV transpose, the condition number equals the square of the spectral condition number of V, so an ill-conditioned basis can strongly amplify coordinate-recovery errors.
knowledge_statements.title: Reduction Without Numerical Stability
